Your monthly Brightline Solar invoice is organized into three sections: Charges, Credits, and Summary. Here is what each line item means:

Charges

Line ItemWhat It Is
Solar Service FeeYour fixed monthly charge for system access, monitoring, and support. This amount is set in your financing agreement and does not change month to month.
Monitoring SubscriptionA $4.99/month fee for advanced Brightline Home app features including real-time alerts and historical exports. See Understanding the Monitoring Subscription Line for details.
Late Payment FeeA $15.00 fee applied when a balance remains unpaid 10 days after the due date.
Credit Card Convenience FeeA 2.1% fee added when paying by credit card. See our fee change notice for background.

Credits

  • Net Production Credit: A bill reduction calculated from the kilowatt-hours your system exported to the grid under your net-metering agreement.
  • Carry-Forward Credit: Unused credit from a previous billing period rolled into the current invoice. Credits accumulate for up to 12 months before expiring.
  • Referral Credit: A one-time $150 credit applied after a referred customer reaches Permission to Operate.

Summary

The Amount Due line reflects all charges minus all credits. If the result is negative, the surplus appears as a carry-forward credit on your next invoice—you will never receive a cash refund for credit balances under $50.00.

articles.title: Why is my invoice total higher than I expected this month?
articles.summary: Common reasons your Brightline Solar invoice may be larger than usual, and steps to investigate or dispute unexpected charges.
articles.question: My invoice this month is noticeably higher than normal. I haven't changed anything—why would my bill go up, and what can I do about it?
articles.answer:
Why Your Invoice May Be Higher Than Usual

Several factors can cause a one-time or recurring increase in your invoice total. Work through the checklist below to identify the cause.

1. Reduced Net Production Credit

If your system produced less electricity than usual—due to seasonal shading, soiling, or an inverter issue—your Net Production Credit will be smaller, leaving a higher balance. Check your production history in the Brightline Home app under Home > Production > Monthly View. If output looks abnormally low, see Report Low Production to open a service ticket.

2. Carry-Forward Balance from a Missed Payment

A prior unpaid balance plus a $15.00 late fee may have rolled into this invoice. Review the Previous Balance line at the top of your invoice PDF. To avoid future late fees, consider enrolling in autopay at Set Up Autopay.

3. New or Changed Fees

Occasionally Brightline Solar adjusts ancillary fees with 30 days' written notice. Check your email for a notice with subject line Important Update to Your Brightline Solar Account, or review the fee history section in the app under Account > Billing > Fee History.

4. Prorated Charges After a Billing Date Change

If you recently moved your billing date, a prorated invoice covering a partial period may appear larger than a standard monthly bill. This is a one-time occurrence.

Still Unclear?

Download your full invoice PDF for an itemized view, then contact Brightline Support via Account > Help > Chat with your invoice number (format: BLS-YYYYMM-XXXXX) ready. Our billing team can issue a credit within 5 business days if an error is confirmed.

articles.title: How do I read my Brightline Solar invoice?
articles.summary: A section-by-section walkthrough of every part of your monthly Brightline Solar invoice.
articles.question: I just received my invoice and I'm not sure what all the sections and numbers mean. Can you walk me through how to read it?
articles.answer:
Invoice Header

The top of your invoice shows your Account Number (format: BLS-XXXXXXXX), your service address, and the Statement Date—the date the invoice was generated. Your Due Date is always 21 days after the Statement Date unless you have a custom billing date (see Change your billing date).

Summary Box

Just below the header you'll find a shaded summary box with three figures:

  • Previous Balance: Any unpaid amount carried from your last statement.
  • Payments Received: Credits applied since your last statement, including AutoPay transactions.
  • Amount Due Now: The total you owe by the Due Date.

Line Items Section

This section breaks your charges into individual rows. Common line items include:

Line ItemWhat It Covers
Solar Lease / Loan PaymentYour monthly financing installment
Monitoring Subscription$9.99/mo for Brightline Home app access and production alerts
Battery Management FeeApplies only to accounts with a Brightline PowerVault battery
Late Fee$15.00 assessed if prior balance was not paid within 5 days of due date

Production Summary

At the bottom of the invoice you'll see a 30-day production snapshot (kWh generated) pulled directly from your system's monitoring data. If these numbers look off, visit Report low production.

Need the PDF?

You can download a print-ready copy of any invoice from the Brightline Home app under Billing → Statements → Download PDF. For step-by-step instructions, see Download invoice PDF.

articles.title: Why is my invoice total different from last month?
articles.summary: Common reasons your Brightline invoice amount changed and how to investigate each one.
articles.question: My invoice this month is higher (or lower) than usual and I wasn't expecting it to change. What could have caused this?
articles.answer:
Most Common Reasons for a Change

Your monthly total can shift for several reasons. Work through the list below to identify the cause on your specific invoice.

  1. Prorated charge or credit: If your billing date recently changed, or you added a battery mid-cycle, you'll see a one-time prorated line item that won't appear next month.
  2. Monitoring Subscription adjustment: The $9.99/mo Monitoring Subscription fee may have been waived, reinstated, or adjusted. See Understand the monitoring subscription line on your invoice for a full explanation.
  3. Late fee applied: A $15.00 late fee is added automatically if your previous balance was not settled within 5 days of its due date. This appears as "Late Payment Fee – [date]" in the Line Items section.
  4. Financing rate step-up: Some promotional loan agreements include scheduled rate increases at 12, 24, or 60 months. Check page 2 of your original loan agreement for a rate schedule, or open Brightline Home → Billing → Financing Details to view your current rate tier.
  5. Credit card convenience fee: If you recently switched from bank-transfer (ACH) payments to a credit card, a 2.9% convenience fee now applies to each transaction. See Credit card fee change for details.
  6. Outstanding balance carried forward: A missed or partial AutoPay payment from a prior month may have rolled into this statement. Visit AutoPay failed – what to do if you suspect a payment didn't process correctly.

Still Can't Identify the Difference?

Open your last two invoices side by side using Billing → Statements in the Brightline Home app and compare each line item individually. If a charge still appears unexplained, tap Get Help on the invoice screen to start a billing inquiry and our team will respond within 2 business days.

articles.title: SMS Verification Codes Delayed Due to Carrier Routing Issue — July 2025
articles.summary: A third-party carrier routing disruption is causing SMS two-factor authentication codes to arrive late or not at all for some Brightline Home users.
articles.abstract: Beginning July 9, 2025, some Brightline Home customers have reported that SMS verification codes sent during login are arriving significantly delayed or failing to deliver entirely. Our messaging provider has identified a routing issue affecting several major US carriers. We are actively working with them to restore full delivery speed and reliability, and we expect the issue to be fully resolved by July 14, 2025.
articles.body:
Affected period: July 9, 2025 – ongoing (estimated resolution July 14, 2025)

If you are not receiving your SMS code within 60 seconds, try the following steps in order:

  • Tap Resend Code on the verification screen and wait an additional 90 seconds.
  • Check that your phone number on file is correct under Account > Profile > Contact Details. If it needs updating, see Update Contact Information.
  • Switch to an email-based one-time code: tap Send code via email instead on the verification screen.
  • If none of the above work, use a backup authentication app code if you previously enrolled one.

Error reference: Customers may see error AUTH-SMS-503 on the login screen during this event.

CarrierImpact Level
National Tier-1 GSM carriersModerate delays (2–8 min)
Regional MVNO carriersHigh — codes may not arrive
VoIP numbersUnaffected

We apologize for the inconvenience and will post an update here once service is fully restored.

articles.title: Why You May Not Be Receiving SMS Login Codes — Tips and Known Fixes
articles.summary: Brightline Home users who never receive SMS two-factor codes can use this guide to diagnose common causes and switch to a more reliable verification method.
articles.abstract: SMS one-time codes are a key part of Brightline Home's two-factor authentication flow, but several factors — including carrier filtering, VoIP numbers, and international roaming — can prevent codes from arriving. This article explains the most common causes and provides step-by-step fixes, including how to switch to an authenticator app for a more dependable login experience.
articles.body:
If you tap Send Code on the Brightline Home login screen and nothing arrives, one or more of the following issues is likely the cause:

CauseSymptomsFix
VoIP or landline number on fileCode never arrives; error AUTH-SMS-101Add a mobile number under Account > Profile > Contact Details
Carrier spam filterIntermittent deliveryText UNSTOP to 87654 to re-enable Brightline messages
International roamingLong delay or no deliveryUse email code or authenticator app while traveling
Incorrect phone number on fileCode always failsUpdate number before next login attempt

Recommended long-term fix: Enroll a time-based authenticator app (such as any TOTP-compatible app) so you never depend on SMS delivery. See Enable Two-Factor Authentication for step-by-step instructions — setup takes under three minutes and works offline.

If you are locked out and cannot resolve the issue yourself, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 (Mon–Fri, 8 am–6 pm local time) and reference error code AUTH-SMS-101 or AUTH-SMS-102 for priority routing to our account recovery team.

articles.title: How do I request a copy of my personal data from Brightline Solar?
articles.summary: You can submit a Data Access Request through the Brightline Home app or by contacting support, and you will receive your data export within 30 days.
articles.question: I want to see all the personal information Brightline Solar has about me. How do I request a copy of my data, and what will it include?
articles.answer:
Submitting a Data Access Request

Brightline Solar supports Data Access Requests (DARs) under applicable U.S. privacy laws, including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and similar state statutes. To request a copy of your personal data, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Profile → Privacy & Data → Request My Data.
  2. Select Data Access Request from the request-type menu.
  3. Confirm your identity using your account password and, if enabled, your two-factor authentication code. (See Enable Two-Factor Authentication for setup help.)
  4. Tap Submit Request. You will receive a confirmation email to your address on file within 15 minutes.

What Your Export Includes

Your data package is delivered as a .zip file containing structured JSON files within 30 calendar days of submission. The package covers:

  • Account profile details (name, contact info, service address)
  • System monitoring history (production and consumption readings)
  • Billing records and invoice line items
  • Communications log (emails and in-app messages)
  • Partner API access grants linked to your account

Need to Update Your Contact Information First?

Make sure your email address is current before submitting so the export link reaches you. Visit Update Contact Information if you need to make changes. If your request is not acknowledged within 2 business days, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0174 and reference request type DAR-ACC.

articles.title: How do I ask Brightline Solar to delete my personal data?
articles.summary: You can submit a Data Deletion Request through the Brightline Home app or by contacting support, and Brightline will process it within 45 days, subject to legal and contractual retention obligations.
articles.question: I want Brightline Solar to delete my personal information. How do I make that request, and is there anything they are allowed to keep?
articles.answer:
How to Submit a Data Deletion Request

Brightline Solar honors Data Deletion Requests (DDRs) as required by applicable U.S. privacy law. To submit one:

  1. In the Brightline Home app, go to Profile → Privacy & Data → Request My Data.
  2. Select Data Deletion Request.
  3. Complete identity verification (password + optional two-factor code).
  4. Tap Submit Request. A confirmation email with reference number prefix DDR- will arrive within 15 minutes.

Brightline will complete the deletion or issue a written exception notice within 45 calendar days. Complex cases may be extended by an additional 45 days with prior notice.

What Brightline Is Required to Retain

Certain data cannot be deleted due to legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations:

Data TypeRetention PeriodReason
Billing & payment records7 yearsTax and financial regulations
Permit documentationLife of systemState licensing requirements
Interconnection records10 yearsUtility agreement obligations
Safety incident reports10 yearsOSHA recordkeeping rules

Effect on Your Account and Services

Submitting a DDR will not automatically cancel your Brightline service agreement. If you also wish to cancel service, contact your account manager separately. Note that deleting your profile data will remove your ability to log in to the Brightline Home app and will revoke any active Partner API access tokens associated with your account. If you have household members on your account, review Add a Household Member to understand how their access is affected. For questions, call 1-800-555-0174 and reference your DDR- number.

articles.title: How long does it take for Brightline to fulfill a data privacy request?
articles.summary: Data privacy requests at Brightline Solar are processed within 45 calendar days, with specific timelines and status updates depending on request type.
articles.question: I submitted a request to access or delete my personal data. How long will it take, and how will I know when it's done?
articles.answer:
Standard Processing Timeframes

Brightline Solar processes all data privacy requests—including access, correction, portability, and deletion—within 45 calendar days of verified receipt. If your request is complex or you have submitted multiple requests simultaneously, we may extend this window by an additional 45 days. We will notify you by email before the original deadline if an extension is needed.

What Happens After You Submit

  1. Confirmation email (within 24 hours): You will receive a confirmation with a unique request ID (format: DPR-XXXXXXXX). Save this for your records.
  2. Identity verification (within 3 business days): We will send a verification link to the email address on your Brightline account. The link expires after 72 hours. If it expires, log in to the Brightline Home app and resubmit under Profile → Privacy & Data → My Requests.
  3. Processing begins: Once verified, your request enters our privacy queue. Status updates appear in the app under the same menu path.
  4. Completion notification: You will receive an email when your request is fulfilled, along with a secure download link (for access/portability requests) that expires in 14 days.

Possible Delays

  • Unverified identity holds the request in Pending Verification status indefinitely.
  • Active legal holds or billing disputes may pause deletion requests until resolved.

For questions about what data we collect, see How do I request a copy of my personal data? or update your account details first at Update Contact Information.

articles.title: What personal data does Brightline keep even after I request deletion?
articles.summary: Certain categories of data must be retained for legal, safety, or contractual reasons even after a deletion request is approved.
articles.question: I requested deletion of my personal data. Will Brightline really delete everything, or is some data kept? What are my rights if data is retained?
articles.answer:
What We Delete

When a verified deletion request (request type DPR-DEL) is approved, Brightline Solar removes or anonymizes the following within 30 days of approval: your name, email address, phone number, saved payment methods, app login credentials, and granular production monitoring history tied to your identity.

Data We Are Required to Retain

Federal and state law, as well as your financing or lease agreement, require us to retain certain records. The table below summarizes key categories:

Data CategoryRetention PeriodLegal Basis
Billing & invoice records7 yearsIRS / state tax law
Interconnection & permit documents10 yearsUtility & municipal requirements
Warranty and service recordsLife of system + 3 yearsConsumer protection statutes
Safety incident reports10 yearsOSHA / state regulations

How Retained Data Is Protected

Retained records are moved to a restricted archive accessible only to Brightline's compliance team. They are not used for marketing, shared with third-party partners, or visible in the Brightline Home app.

Your Right to Object

If you believe data has been retained beyond its lawful period, email privacy@brightlinesolar.com with your request ID. We will respond within 15 business days. Residents of California, Virginia, and Colorado have additional appeal rights under applicable state privacy laws; our full Privacy Notice is available at brightlinesolar.com/privacy.

To manage your account before submitting a deletion request, see Update Contact Information or review How do I request deletion of my personal data?

articles.title: Understanding Your Microinverter Offline Alert in Brightline Home
articles.summary: A new in-app alert now notifies you when one or more microinverters stop reporting data, so you can act quickly to restore full production.
articles.abstract: As of June 10, 2025, Brightline Home sends a Microinverter Offline alert (alert code MI-4031) when any microinverter on your system has not reported production data for 90 consecutive minutes during daylight hours. The alert appears on the Alerts tab and, if enabled, is also pushed as a mobile notification. This article explains what triggers the alert, what it does not mean, and the recommended steps to resolve it.
articles.body:
What Triggers a MI-4031 Alert?

The alert fires when Brightline's cloud platform receives no heartbeat signal from a microinverter between sunrise and 30 minutes before sunset for your zip code. Common causes include:

  • Temporary Wi-Fi or gateway communication drop
  • A tripped circuit breaker on the microinverter branch circuit
  • Firmware update in progress (expected duration: up to 20 minutes)
  • Hardware fault requiring a service visit

What the Alert Does NOT Mean

A single microinverter offline does not mean your entire system has stopped producing energy. Remaining microinverters continue to operate independently.

Recommended Steps

  1. Check the Alerts tab in Brightline Home for the specific panel location listed in the alert detail.
  2. Attempt a gateway restart by following the steps in Reconnect Gateway Wi-Fi.
  3. Wait 15 minutes and check whether the alert clears automatically.
  4. If the alert persists beyond 24 hours, tap Request Service within the alert to open a warranty ticket.

Alert Auto-Clear Timeline

ScenarioExpected Auto-Clear
Gateway reconnectedWithin 15 min
Firmware update completedWithin 25 min
Hardware fault confirmedRemains open until service

Service visits for microinverter faults under active warranty are scheduled within 5–10 business days.

articles.title: Microinverter Offline Alerts Now More Sensitive — What Changed on July 1, 2025
articles.summary: Brightline has reduced the offline detection threshold from 90 minutes to 30 minutes, which may cause more frequent MI-4031 alerts for systems with marginal gateway signal strength.
articles.abstract: Effective July 1, 2025, Brightline updated its cloud monitoring platform to shorten the microinverter offline detection window from 90 minutes to 30 minutes of missed reporting. This change improves early fault detection but may generate additional MI-4031 alerts on systems where the Brightline Gateway has an intermittent or weak Wi-Fi connection. Customers seeing a higher alert volume are encouraged to review their gateway placement before requesting a service visit.
articles.body:
Why We Made This Change

Analysis of warranty claims from January–May 2025 showed that a 90-minute detection delay allowed minor faults to progress into full microinverter failures in approximately 18% of cases. Reducing the window to 30 minutes is expected to cut escalated failures by roughly half.

Who Is Most Affected?

  • Systems installed before December 2023 using the BL-GW2 gateway model
  • Homes where the gateway is more than 40 ft from the router or separated by masonry walls
  • Customers in areas with high network congestion (dense apartment complexes, HOA communities)

Detection Threshold Comparison

PeriodOffline ThresholdAlert Code
Before July 1, 202590 minutesMI-4031
July 1, 2025 onward30 minutesMI-4031

Steps to Reduce False Alerts

  1. Move your Brightline Gateway within 20 ft of your router if possible.
  2. Follow the full reconnection guide at Reconnect Gateway Wi-Fi to ensure a stable link.
  3. Upgrade to the BL-GW3 gateway (available at no cost for systems under 36-month monitoring agreements) by contacting Brightline Support.

If alert volume remains high after improving Wi-Fi signal, open a diagnostic ticket through Brightline Home → Help → Contact Support and reference code MI-4031-FREQ.

articles.title: Updated Production Estimate Methodology Now Live in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Brightline Solar has revised how first-year and lifetime production estimates are calculated, improving accuracy for systems installed after June 1, 2025.
articles.abstract: Starting June 1, 2025, Brightline Solar is rolling out an updated production estimate engine that incorporates localized irradiance data, panel degradation curves, and real-time shading models to deliver more accurate kWh projections for new and existing customers. Customers will see revised estimates reflected in the Reports section of the Brightline Home app within 30 days of the update reaching their account.
articles.body:
Effective date: June 1, 2025

Brightline Solar has updated the modeling engine behind the production estimates shown in your Reports tab. The new methodology replaces the previous static regional averages with three dynamic inputs:

  • Localized irradiance data — sourced from a 4 km² grid updated quarterly
  • Panel degradation curves — modeled per panel series, typically 0.5 %–0.7 % annual degradation
  • Real-time shading analysis — recalculated each spring using updated satellite imagery

The table below summarizes how estimates may shift for common system sizes:

System SizePrevious Avg. Annual EstimateRevised Avg. Annual Estimate
6 kW7,800 kWh8,150 kWh
10 kW12,900 kWh13,480 kWh
14 kW17,600 kWh18,200 kWh

If your actual output falls significantly below your revised estimate, review our guide on how to report low production and schedule a system check. Updated estimates will appear automatically — no action is required from customers.

articles.title: Winter 2025 Seasonal Production Estimate Adjustments Coming to the Reports Tab
articles.summary: Brightline Home will display adjusted seasonal production estimates for Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 beginning October 15, 2025, reflecting updated winter weather and daylight models.
articles.abstract: Each fall, Brightline Solar recalibrates seasonal production estimates to account for shorter daylight hours, increased cloud cover probability, and potential snow-load shading specific to each customer's region. Beginning October 15, 2025, customers will see Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 estimates updated in the Reports tab of the Brightline Home app, with region-specific notes explaining any meaningful deviation from prior projections.
articles.body:
Announcement date: September 22, 2025 | Effective in-app: October 15, 2025

Brightline Solar performs a seasonal recalibration of production estimates twice a year — once in spring and once in fall. The upcoming winter adjustment affects all active residential systems across our service regions.

Key changes customers may notice in the Reports → Production Estimates screen:

  • Month-by-month kWh projections for October 2025 through March 2026 will be refreshed
  • Customers in snow-prone regions (Zone C and Zone D) may see estimates reduced by 6 %–12 % compared to summer peaks
  • A new "Seasonal Note" badge will appear alongside estimates that differ by more than 8 % from the previous period
  • Year-end annual totals will be recalculated automatically to reflect the updated seasonal figures

These adjustments are normal and do not indicate a problem with your system. However, if your live output is tracking below even the adjusted winter estimate for more than two consecutive weeks, you can learn how to clean your solar panels to rule out soiling or debris as a contributing factor. Contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 if concerns persist after cleaning.

articles.title: Ground-Mount Permit Fees Increasing in Select Counties Beginning August 1, 2025
