articles.title: Interpret and Resolve 4xx Client Error Codes in the Partner API
articles.summary: Identify the cause of 4xx HTTP error responses from the Brightline Partner API and take the correct corrective action for each code.
articles.body:
Prerequisites: You must have an active Brightline Partner API integration with a valid OAuth2 client ID and secret. Ensure you have completed initial setup as described in Partner API Overview and can successfully obtain tokens per Get an Access Token.

  1. Capture the full error response body. Every 4xx response from the API returns a JSON object with three fields: error_code (string), message (human-readable description), and request_id (UUID for support escalation). Log all three fields immediately.
  2. Match the HTTP status and error_code to the table below.
    • 400 / INVALID_PARAM — A required field is missing or a value is outside the accepted range. Check your request body against the schema in the API reference for that endpoint.
    • 401 / TOKEN_EXPIRED — Your access token has exceeded its 60-minute TTL. Request a new token using your refresh token before retrying.
    • 401 / TOKEN_INVALID — The token is malformed or was issued to a different client. Regenerate credentials in the Partner Portal under Settings > API Credentials.
    • 403 / SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT — Your OAuth2 token was issued without the scope required by this endpoint. Re-authorize with the correct scopes listed in the endpoint documentation.
    • 403 / SITE_ACCESS_DENIED — Your partner account has not been granted access to the requested site ID. Ask the homeowner to re-authorize your integration in Brightline Home under Settings > Connected Partners.
    • 404 / RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND — The site, device, or record ID does not exist or belongs to a different partner. Verify the ID in your database and confirm it was returned by a prior Brightline API response.
    • 409 / DUPLICATE_REQUEST — An identical request (same idempotency key) was already processed. Retrieve the original response using the request_id from the 409 body.
    • 422 / SCHEMA_MISMATCH — The payload passed schema validation but contains a logical conflict (for example, a battery charge schedule with overlapping time windows). Adjust the conflicting fields and resubmit.
    • 429 / RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED — Your partner account has exceeded 300 requests per minute. Back off for the number of seconds indicated in the Retry-After response header before retrying.
  3. Retry with exponential backoff where appropriate. Errors 429 and transient 400-series errors may resolve on retry. Do not retry 401 TOKEN_INVALID or 403 SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT without first correcting credentials or scopes.
  4. Escalate unresolved errors to Brightline Partner Support. Open a ticket at partners.brightlinesolar.com/support and include the request_id, the full request body (redact any PII), and the timestamp of the failure. Response SLA is one business day for standard partners and four business hours for Premier partners.

Troubleshooting

I keep receiving 403 / SITE_ACCESS_DENIED even after the homeowner re-authorized. Authorization tokens issued before a homeowner changes their email address are invalidated. Ask the homeowner to sign out of Brightline Home, sign back in, and repeat the partner authorization flow. See Update Contact Information for guidance on email changes.

My error_code is not listed above. Error codes in the 4xx range not documented here may be introduced in minor API releases. Check the Partner API changelog in the Partner Portal under Documentation > Changelog. If the code was introduced after your integration was certified, you may also be affected by a version change — review Partner API v1 Deprecation to confirm your integration targets the correct version.

The request_id field is absent from the response. This indicates the request did not reach the API gateway. Check your base URL, TLS certificate validity, and DNS resolution for api.brightlinesolar.com.

articles.title: Handle 5xx Server Error Codes and Webhook Delivery Failures in the Partner API
articles.summary: Diagnose Brightline Partner API 5xx server errors and failed webhook deliveries, and implement the correct retry and escalation strategy for each scenario.
articles.body:
Prerequisites: Your integration must already be receiving live API responses or webhook events. If you have not yet configured webhooks, complete Set Up a Webhook first. You will need access to your endpoint's server logs and the Brightline Partner Portal (partners.brightlinesolar.com).

  1. Identify whether the failure is a synchronous 5xx response or a failed webhook delivery. Synchronous failures occur during REST calls your server initiates. Webhook failures occur when Brightline's delivery system cannot reach your endpoint. Both produce distinct error surfaces — treat them separately in steps 2 and 4.
  2. For synchronous 5xx errors, match the status code.
    • 500 / INTERNAL_ERROR — An unexpected condition occurred on Brightline's servers. Log the request_id and retry once after 5 seconds. If the error persists across three retries spanning at least 30 seconds, do not continue retrying; open a support ticket.
    • 502 / UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT — A dependency (such as the utility data feed or metering service) did not respond in time. Retry with exponential backoff: 5 s, 15 s, 45 s. If all retries fail, queue the operation and attempt again after 10 minutes.
    • 503 / SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE — The API is temporarily offline for a planned maintenance window or an incident. Check the Brightline Partner Status page at status.brightlinesolar.com for an active incident. Honor the Retry-After header if present; otherwise wait 60 seconds before retrying.
    • 504 / GATEWAY_TIMEOUT — Your request reached the gateway but the processing node did not respond within 30 seconds. This typically affects bulk operations. Consider breaking large payloads into smaller batches as described in Partner API Bulk Export, then retry.
  3. Implement idempotency keys for all mutating requests. Include a unique Idempotency-Key header (UUID v4) on every POST or PATCH request. If a 5xx error occurs and you are unsure whether the operation was applied, re-send the identical request with the same key. Brightline will return the original outcome without double-processing, and will include a replayed: true field in the response body.
  4. For webhook delivery failures, review the delivery log in the Partner Portal. Navigate to Partner Portal > Webhooks > [your endpoint] > Delivery History. Each failed delivery shows an HTTP status code your endpoint returned, or a connection error label (CONNECT_TIMEOUT, TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED, DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILED).
    • Your endpoint returned 5xx — The fault is on your server. Fix the handler and use the Replay button in the Partner Portal to resend the event. Brightline retains events for 72 hours for replay.
    • CONNECT_TIMEOUT — Your server did not accept the TCP connection within 10 seconds. Verify your firewall rules allow inbound connections from Brightline's webhook IP range, published in the Partner Portal under Documentation > Network Requirements.
    • TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED — Your endpoint's TLS certificate is expired, self-signed, or uses a cipher suite not on Brightline's approved list (TLS 1.2+ with ECDHE or DHE key exchange). Renew or replace the certificate and confirm the chain is complete.
    • DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILED — Brightline's delivery nodes cannot resolve your webhook hostname. Confirm your domain's DNS records are publicly accessible and have propagated fully.
  5. Monitor for automatic suspension of your webhook endpoint. If your endpoint returns non-2xx responses for 50 consecutive deliveries within any 24-hour window, Brightline will automatically suspend delivery and send an alert email to your technical contact. To reinstate delivery, fix the underlying issue, then navigate to Partner Portal > Webhooks > [your endpoint] > Status and click Reactivate.
  6. Escalate to Brightline Partner Support when needed. For persistent 500 or 502 errors lasting more than 15 minutes, or for any incident affecting production data integrity, open a Priority ticket at partners.brightlinesolar.com/support. Include all relevant request_id values, the affected site IDs (if known), and a description of business impact. Premier partners may also call the dedicated partner support line listed in their onboarding documentation.

Troubleshooting

I retried with the same Idempotency-Key but received a 400 / IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH. This means the request body does not exactly match the body sent with the original key. Idempotency keys are bound to the full request body at first use. Generate a new UUID key if you need to submit a modified payload.

The Partner Portal shows a webhook delivery as successful (HTTP 200), but my system never processed it. Your endpoint returned 200 before your application finished processing the event. Move all processing logic to an asynchronous background job, return 200 immediately upon receipt, and use the event's event_id field to deduplicate in your queue.

503 errors started occurring at the same time every week. Brightline schedules routine maintenance on Sundays between 02:00–04:00 UTC. Events queued during this window are delivered automatically once the service resumes. If your SLA cannot tolerate this window, contact your Partner Success Manager to discuss a maintenance notification subscription.

I am seeing mixed 200 and 5xx responses with no clear pattern. This may indicate a load-balancing issue on your infrastructure rather than an API-side incident. Check the Brightline Partner Status page first; if no incident is reported, the problem is likely isolated to your environment.

articles.title: Partner API Now Requires Idempotency Keys on All Mutating Requests
articles.summary: Starting August 1, 2025, the Brightline Partner API will reject POST, PUT, and PATCH requests that do not include a valid Idempotency-Key header, helping partners avoid duplicate transactions and data inconsistencies.
articles.abstract: Brightline is rolling out mandatory idempotency key enforcement across all mutating Partner API endpoints effective August 1, 2025. This change ensures that retried or duplicated network requests never create duplicate records — protecting both partner integrations and homeowner accounts from double-posted payments, duplicate work orders, and redundant webhook registrations. Partners have a 60-day grace period beginning June 2, 2025, during which requests missing the header will receive a warning response rather than a hard rejection.
articles.body:
What Is Changing

Effective August 1, 2025, any POST, PUT, or PATCH request sent to the Brightline Partner API without an Idempotency-Key header will receive an HTTP 422 error with error code MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY. Requests that reuse a key for a different payload will receive HTTP 409 with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT.

Key Requirements

  • Format: UUID v4 (e.g., a3f1c2d4-11ab-47fe-b830-9e4d7c820001)
  • Scope: per partner application, per endpoint
  • Expiry: keys are retained and deduplicated for 24 hours after first use
  • Maximum length: 64 characters

Grace Period Timeline

DateBehavior
June 2, 2025Missing key returns HTTP 200 with X-Idempotency-Warning: required-soon header
August 1, 2025Missing key returns HTTP 422 MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY — hard rejection

For guidance on handling related 4xx responses, see Interpret 4xx Error Codes in the Partner API.

articles.title: Updated Best Practices Guide: Generating and Managing Idempotency Keys in Your Integration
articles.summary: Brightline has published updated integration guidance covering how to correctly generate, store, and recycle idempotency keys to maximize reliability and avoid common pitfalls in the Partner API.
articles.abstract: Following the announcement of mandatory idempotency key enforcement, Brightline's Partner Engineering team has released a refreshed set of best practices to help integration partners implement keys correctly from day one. The guidance addresses the most common mistakes observed during the June–July 2025 grace period, including key reuse across different resource types, failure to persist keys before sending requests, and incorrect handling of cached responses returned for duplicate submissions.
articles.body:
Published July 10, 2025

During the grace period that began June 2, 2025, Brightline's API gateway logged over 14,000 mutating requests per week arriving without a valid Idempotency-Key header. The patterns below represent the most frequent mistakes and the recommended remediation for each.

Common Mistakes and Fixes

  • Generating the key after a failure: Always generate and persist the UUID before sending the initial request. If the request times out, reuse the same key on retry — do not generate a new one.
  • Sharing keys across endpoints: Keys are scoped per endpoint. A key used for POST /v2/orders can safely be reused for POST /v2/payments without conflict.
  • Ignoring cached responses: When the API returns a cached result for a duplicate request, the HTTP status will match the original response. Treat an HTTP 201 cache hit identically to a live 201.
  • Key length violations: Keys exceeding 64 characters will return HTTP 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TOO_LONG.

Recommended Storage Pattern

Store each key alongside the request payload hash and creation timestamp in your database before transmission. Purge records older than 48 hours to stay safely within Brightline's 24-hour deduplication window with margin.

Review the foundational OAuth2 setup required before making any API calls in Get an Access Token for the Partner API.

articles.title: Prorated Charges Now Itemized Separately on All Invoices Starting July 1, 2025
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is updating how prorated charges appear on customer invoices so that partial-month fees are clearly broken out as distinct line items rather than folded into the base service total.
articles.abstract: Effective July 1, 2025, all Brightline Solar invoices will display prorated charges as individually labeled line items, making it easier to understand exactly what you are being charged when your service starts, ends, or changes mid-billing cycle. This update applies to monitoring subscriptions, loan servicing fees, and any plan changes that take effect on a date other than the first of the month.
articles.body:
What is changing?

Before July 1, 2025, prorated amounts were silently merged into existing line items, which caused confusion when invoice totals differed unexpectedly from month to month. Beginning with the July billing cycle, each prorated entry will appear with a dedicated label such as Monitoring Subscription – Prorated (Jun 14–Jun 30) and a clear daily-rate calculation.

Common scenarios that generate prorated charges:

  • System activation mid-month after utility interconnection is approved
  • Plan upgrade or downgrade effective on a date other than the 1st
  • Cancellation or transfer of service before the billing period ends
  • Addition of a battery storage subscription during an active billing cycle

How prorated amounts are calculated:

Monthly RateDays in MonthDays of ServiceProrated Charge
$12.993017$7.36
$19.99318$5.16

No action is required on your part. If you have questions about a specific line item after July 1, visit Understanding Your Invoice Line Items for a full glossary of charge descriptions. Customers enrolled in autopay will see the corrected amount debited automatically on their due date.

Published June 3, 2025

articles.title: How Prorated Charges Apply When You Change Your Brightline Plan Mid-Cycle
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is publishing updated guidance explaining exactly how prorated charges are calculated and applied whenever a customer upgrades, downgrades, or cancels a service plan on any day other than their regular billing date.
articles.abstract: When you make a change to your Brightline service plan mid-cycle — such as adding a battery monitoring tier, switching financing terms, or removing an add-on — the charges for both the old and new plan are prorated to the day the change takes effect, ensuring you never pay a full month's rate for a partial month of service on either plan.
articles.body:
Effective date: August 1, 2025, updated proration logic applies to all plan changes processed through the Brightline Home app or by calling support at 1-800-555-0174.

How it works step by step:

  1. You request a plan change on, for example, August 12.
  2. Brightline calculates the daily rate for your current plan: monthly fee ÷ days in billing month.
  3. You are charged that daily rate × 11 days (August 1–11) for the old plan.
  4. The new plan's daily rate × 20 days (August 12–31) is added to the same invoice.
  5. Any credit balance from a prepaid period is automatically applied before the net amount is charged.

Proration does not apply to:

  • One-time installation fees already collected at contract signing
  • Permit or inspection fees (billed as incurred)
  • Loan principal and interest, which follow the original amortization schedule

Where to see the breakdown: Open Brightline Home → Billing → Invoice Detail and tap any prorated line item for a day-by-day calculation popup. For background on all charges that can appear on your statement, see How to Read Your Brightline Invoice.

Questions? Contact billing support Monday–Friday 8 am–8 pm ET.

Published July 10, 2025

articles.title: Brightline Extends Invoice Dispute Window from 30 to 60 Days Starting July 1, 2025
articles.summary: Customers now have 60 days from the invoice date to formally dispute a charge, giving more time to review statements and gather supporting documentation.
articles.abstract: Effective July 1, 2025, Brightline Solar is extending the standard invoice dispute window from 30 calendar days to 60 calendar days. This change applies to all residential accounts and means that any invoice dated on or after July 1, 2025 can be disputed through the Brightline Home app or by contacting Billing Support up to 60 days after the invoice date, replacing the previous 30-day limit. Invoices dated before July 1, 2025 remain subject to the original 30-day window.
articles.body:
What Is Changing

Beginning July 1, 2025, the dispute eligibility window for Brightline Solar invoices doubles from 30 to 60 calendar days, measured from the invoice date printed on your statement.

How to File a Dispute

  1. Open Brightline Home and navigate to Billing > Invoice History.
  2. Select the invoice you wish to dispute and tap Dispute This Invoice.
  3. Choose a dispute reason, enter a description, and attach any supporting documents (photos, utility bills, permit receipts).
  4. Tap Submit Dispute. You will receive confirmation code DSP-XXXXXX by email within 15 minutes.

Dispute Resolution Timeframes

Dispute TypeTarget Resolution
Incorrect line-item charge7 business days
Monitoring subscription discrepancy10 business days
Prorated charge adjustment14 business days
Credit or refund request21 business days

If Brightline rules in your favor, credits appear on your next invoice within one full billing cycle. For background on specific line items, see Understanding Your Invoice Line Items.

Questions? Contact Billing Support at billing@brightlinesolar.example or call 1-800-555-0192, Monday–Friday, 8 am–6 pm local time.

articles.title: New Evidence Upload Requirement for Invoice Disputes Effective August 15, 2025
articles.summary: Starting August 15, 2025, all formal invoice disputes must include at least one supporting document uploaded through the Brightline Home app or Partner API, or the dispute will be automatically closed within 5 business days.
articles.abstract: To improve dispute accuracy and reduce resolution times, Brightline Solar is introducing a mandatory evidence-upload step for all invoice disputes submitted on or after August 15, 2025. Disputes filed without an attached supporting document—such as a utility bill, bank statement, production report, or written explanation—will enter a 5-business-day pending period during which customers are prompted to upload evidence; if none is received, the dispute will be automatically closed with status DSP_CLOSED_NO_EVIDENCE and the original charge will stand.
articles.body:
Why We Are Making This Change

Analysis of disputes filed in Q1 2025 showed that 38% lacked sufficient context for our billing team to make a determination, leading to an average resolution delay of 19 additional business days. Requiring upfront evidence reduces that delay significantly.

Accepted Evidence Types

  • Utility company statement showing net-metering credits or charges
  • Bank or credit card statement confirming a specific deduction
  • Brightline production report exported from the Monitoring tab
  • Screenshot of an incorrect amount shown in the app
  • Written explanation (PDF or DOCX, 200-word minimum) for billing calculation disputes

File Requirements

  • Formats accepted: PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX
  • Maximum file size: 10 MB per file, up to 5 files per dispute

Key Dates

DateMilestone
July 15, 2025In-app banner notifications begin
August 1, 2025Upload prompt shown on dispute form (optional)
August 15, 2025Upload becomes mandatory; policy fully in effect

For tips on reading your statement before filing, see How to Read Your Brightline Invoice.

Need help? Email billing@brightlinesolar.example or call 1-800-555-0192.

articles.title: Payment Receipts Now Delivered Faster and Include More Detail
articles.summary: Starting July 1, 2025, Brightline Solar upgraded its receipt delivery system so customers receive itemized payment confirmations within minutes of a successful transaction.
articles.abstract: Brightline Solar has improved the speed and content of payment receipts sent after every successful charge, ensuring customers get a full breakdown of what was paid, when, and through which method—all delivered to their inbox within five minutes of the transaction posting.
articles.body:
What Changed on July 1, 2025

Before this update, payment receipt emails could take up to 24 hours to arrive and showed only a total amount. Receipts now reach your inbox within 5 minutes of a confirmed payment and include the following detail:

  • Invoice number and billing period covered
  • Payment method (e.g., Visa ending 4821, ACH bank account ending 0033)
  • Line-item breakdown matching your invoice (solar plan, monitoring subscription, any prorated charges)
  • Confirmation ID (format: RCP-XXXXXXXX) for your records
  • Next payment due date

Receipts are sent to the email address on file. To verify or update that address, visit Brightline Home → Account → Contact Information. If you need help changing your details, see Update Contact Information.

Accessing Past Receipts

All receipts generated on or after July 1, 2025 are also stored in Brightline Home → Billing → Payment History and can be downloaded as PDF at any time. Receipts from before July 1 remain available as plain summary PDFs.

If a receipt does not arrive within 15 minutes, check your spam folder or contact support at support@brightlinesolar.com.

articles.title: Updated PDF Receipt Format Rolls Out September 15, 2025
articles.summary: On September 15, 2025, Brightline Solar will introduce a redesigned PDF payment receipt that adds a QR code, clearer fee disclosures, and a machine-readable transaction summary for property managers and tax purposes.
articles.abstract: Brightline Solar is releasing a new PDF receipt format on September 15, 2025 that makes it easier for homeowners, accountants, and property managers to verify payments, understand any applicable processing fees, and store records in document-management systems—without needing to log in to the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
Launch Date: September 15, 2025

The redesigned PDF receipt will apply to all payments processed on or after September 15, 2025. Receipts for earlier payments retain the previous format.

New Fields in the Updated Receipt

FieldDescription
QR CodeScans to a secure, read-only payment verification page valid for 12 months
Processing Fee DisclosureShows any card processing fee applied; $0.00 for ACH payments
Payment Method TokenLast four digits and card type or bank name—no full account numbers stored
Tax-Year AttributionFlags which tax year the payment applies to for solar incentive documentation
Confirmation IDUnique RCP-XXXXXXXX code matching the in-app Payment History record

Customers who pay by credit card should note that processing fees are disclosed separately on the receipt. For background on how those fees are calculated, see Credit Card Fee Change.

No Action Required

The new format will apply automatically. PDF receipts can be downloaded from Brightline Home → Billing → Payment History or retrieved via the Partner API using the GET /receipts/{confirmation_id} endpoint. Questions? Contact support@brightlinesolar.com.

articles.title: Brightline Now Accepts Partial Payments on Outstanding Invoices
articles.summary: Starting July 1, 2025, customers can submit partial payments toward any open invoice directly through the Brightline Home app, reducing the risk of service interruptions due to balance shortfalls.
articles.abstract: Brightline Solar is pleased to announce that partial payment support is now live in the Brightline Home app as of July 1, 2025. Customers who cannot cover a full invoice balance in a single transaction may now pay any amount equal to or greater than the $25.00 minimum partial payment threshold, with the remaining balance carried forward to the next billing cycle. A one-time partial payment convenience fee of $1.99 applies per transaction, and balances unpaid after two consecutive cycles remain subject to the standard late fee schedule. This update is intended to give customers greater financial flexibility while keeping their solar service active.
articles.body:
What's Changing

Effective July 1, 2025, the Brightline Home app accepts partial payments on any open invoice. Previously, only full-balance payments were processed through the app.

Key Details

  • Minimum partial payment: $25.00 per transaction
  • Convenience fee: $1.99 per partial payment transaction
  • Carry-forward window: Remaining balance is due by the following invoice due date
  • Late fee trigger: Balances unpaid after two consecutive billing cycles incur the standard 1.5% monthly late fee
  • Autopay interaction: If autopay is enabled, it will attempt to collect only the remaining balance on the due date

How to Make a Partial Payment

Open the Brightline Home app, navigate to Billing > Current Invoice > Pay Now, then tap Enter Custom Amount and type your desired payment. Confirm the $1.99 fee prompt to complete the transaction. A receipt will be emailed within 15 minutes.

If your autopay setup needs updating after this change, see how to update your autopay payment method.

articles.title: Partner API Now Supports Partial Payment Submission and Balance Queries
articles.summary: As of July 14, 2025, Brightline's Partner API exposes new endpoints and webhook events for partial payment posting and outstanding balance retrieval, enabling integrators to reflect partial-pay activity in third-party billing platforms.
articles.abstract: Following the July 1, 2025 launch of partial payments in the Brightline Home app, Brightline is extending the same capability to Partner API integrators. Beginning July 14, 2025, the Partner API includes a new POST /v2/invoices/{invoice_id}/partial-payments endpoint, an updated GET /v2/invoices/{invoice_id}/balance response schema, and two new webhook event types—payment.partial_received and payment.partial_failed—so that third-party platforms can accurately track partial-pay activity and outstanding balances in real time.
articles.body:
Release Date

July 14, 2025 — available in production for all active Partner API credentials.

New and Updated API Surface

ItemTypeDescription
POST /v2/invoices/{invoice_id}/partial-paymentsNew endpointSubmit a partial payment; minimum amount_cents value is 2500 (i.e., $25.00)
GET /v2/invoices/{invoice_id}/balanceUpdated schemaResponse now includes remaining_balance_cents and partial_payments[] array
payment.partial_receivedNew webhook eventFires within 30 seconds of a successful partial payment posting
payment.partial_failedNew webhook eventFires when a partial payment is declined; includes decline_code field

Error Codes

  • 422 PARTIAL_BELOW_MINIMUM — submitted amount is under $25.00
  • 409 INVOICE_ALREADY_SETTLED — invoice has a zero balance and cannot accept further payments

Ensure your webhook receiver handles the new event types before going live. For webhook setup guidance, see how to configure Partner API webhooks. Idempotency keys are strongly recommended for all payment POST requests to avoid duplicate charges.

articles.title: Loan Statements Now Available Directly in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Starting July 14, 2025, customers with a Brightline Solar financing loan can view and download monthly loan statements without leaving the Brightline Home app.
articles.abstract: Brightline Solar is pleased to announce that monthly loan statements are now accessible directly inside the Brightline Home app under Account → Financing → Loan Statements, eliminating the need to log into a separate portal. Statements are generated on the first business day of each month, cover principal, interest, and any applicable fees for the prior billing period, and are retained in-app for a rolling 24 months.
articles.body:
Effective July 14, 2025, all customers with an active Brightline Solar loan can access their loan statements in the Brightline Home app. Here is what the new section includes:

  • Statement date & loan balance – current outstanding principal after each payment
  • Interest breakdown – monthly interest calculated at your fixed APR
  • Payment applied – amount credited, including any partial payments
  • Fees & adjustments – late fees ($15 per occurrence) or rate-lock adjustment credits, if applicable
Statement archive windowFormat availableDownload limit
Last 24 monthsPDF & CSV50 downloads per day

To receive an email reminder when each new statement is ready, visit Account → Notification Preferences and enable Loan Statement Ready under the Financing category. For help configuring alerts, see Manage Notification Preferences.

Statements older than 24 months can be requested by contacting Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192. Allow up to 5 business days for delivery.

articles.title: Loan Statement PDF Redesign Launching August 4, 2025
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is refreshing the loan statement PDF format on August 4, 2025 to add an amortization snapshot, clearer fee disclosures, and improved accessibility for screen readers.
articles.abstract: On August 4, 2025, all loan statements generated in Brightline Home will adopt a redesigned PDF layout that meets WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards, introduces a 6-month amortization snapshot table, and separates origination-related disclosures from recurring monthly charges so customers can more easily reconcile their loan balance against their invoice.
articles.body:
Launching August 4, 2025, the updated loan statement PDF includes the following improvements:

  • 6-month amortization snapshot – shows projected principal, interest, and remaining balance for the next six payment dates
  • Separated fee section – one-time origination fees and recurring service charges now appear in distinct labeled blocks
  • Accessible tagging – all tables and headings are tagged for compatibility with screen-reader software
  • QR code shortcut – scan to jump directly to your loan dashboard in the Brightline Home app
ChangeOld formatNew format
Amortization dataNot included6-month snapshot
Fee disclosureCombined line itemSeparated sections
Accessibility standardNone specifiedWCAG 2.1 AA
File size (avg.)420 KB310 KB

Statements generated before August 4, 2025 will retain the previous format in your archive. If you use the Partner API to retrieve statement PDFs, the document_version field in the response payload will increment from v1 to v2; review Partner API: Interpret 4xx Error Codes if your integration surfaces unexpected errors after the transition. Contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 with any questions.

articles.title: How do I sign in to Brightline Home with my Apple ID?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to setting up and troubleshooting Sign in with Apple on the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: I want to use my Apple ID to log in to the Brightline Home app instead of a password. How do I set that up, and what should I do if it stops working?
articles.answer:
Setting Up Sign in with Apple

You can link your Apple ID to your Brightline Home account in just a few steps:

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Log In on the welcome screen.
  2. Tap Continue with Apple beneath the email/password fields.
  3. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your Apple ID password when prompted by iOS.
  4. On first use, Apple will ask whether to Share My Email or Hide My Email. We strongly recommend choosing Share My Email so your Brightline account stays linked to your verified contact address. If you choose Hide My Email, Apple generates a relay address (e.g., abc123@privaterelay.appleid.com) that we store instead.

What If Sign in with Apple Fails?

Common error codes and fixes:

ErrorMeaningFix
BL-AUTH-4011Apple token expiredForce-close the app and try again; re-authenticate with Apple ID.
BL-AUTH-4013Email relay mismatchYour Apple relay address changed. Contact support to re-link your account.
BL-AUTH-5002Brightline server timeoutWait 5 minutes and retry; if persistent, check our status page.

Unlinking Your Apple ID

To remove Apple sign-in, go to Brightline Home → Account → Security → Linked Sign-In Methods and tap Remove Apple ID. You will be prompted to set a Brightline password before the link is removed so you do not lose access.

For more detail on managing your Apple sign-in after setup, see Sign in with Apple – Full Reference. If you also need to update the email address on your account, visit Update Contact Information.

articles.title: How do I sign in to Brightline Home with my Google account?
articles.summary: Instructions for connecting a Google account to Brightline Home and resolving common Google sign-in errors.
articles.question: Can I use my Google account to log in to the Brightline Home app? How do I connect it, and what do I do if I get an error?
articles.answer:
Enabling Sign in with Google

Brightline Home supports Google sign-in on both iOS and Android. Follow these steps:

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Log In.
  2. Tap Continue with Google.
  3. Select the Google account whose email matches your Brightline account. If you use a different Google address, you will see error BL-AUTH-4021 (Email Not Found).
  4. Grant the requested permissions — Brightline only requests your name and email address; we do not access your Google Drive or other Google data.

Troubleshooting Common Errors

  • BL-AUTH-4021 – Email Not Found: The Google account email does not match any Brightline account. Log in with your Brightline email/password first, then link Google under Account → Security → Linked Sign-In Methods.
  • BL-AUTH-4022 – Token Revoked: You revoked Brightline's access in your Google Account settings. Re-authorize by tapping Continue with Google again.
  • BL-AUTH-4023 – Duplicate Link: That Google account is already linked to a different Brightline profile. Contact support at 1-800-555-0192 to resolve.
  • BL-AUTH-5002 – Server Timeout: A temporary Brightline outage. Wait 5 minutes and retry.

Unlinking Google from Your Account

Navigate to Brightline Home → Account → Security → Linked Sign-In Methods, tap Remove Google Account, and confirm. You must have either a Brightline password or an Apple ID linked before removal is allowed.

For a full reference on Google sign-in behavior and token lifetimes, see Sign in with Google – Full Reference. If you need to update the email address tied to your account, see Update Contact Information.

articles.title: Why can't I log in with Apple after switching to a new iPhone?
articles.summary: Explains why Sign in with Apple may fail after a device change and how to restore access to your Brightline Home account.
articles.question: I just got a new iPhone and now when I tap "Sign in with Apple" in the Brightline Home app, I either get an error or it creates a duplicate account. What's going on and how do I fix it?
articles.answer:
Why This Happens

Sign in with Apple ties your authentication to your Apple ID session and, in some configurations, to a device-level credential stored in iCloud Keychain. When you restore a new iPhone from a backup or set it up as new, there can be a brief period where the Keychain credential hasn't fully synced, causing Brightline Home to receive an invalid or unrecognized token. You may see error code AUTH-4031 or a prompt to create a new account.

Step-by-Step Fix

  1. On your new iPhone, open Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud and confirm iCloud Keychain is turned On. Wait 5–10 minutes for sync to complete.
  2. Force-quit Brightline Home, then relaunch it and tap Sign in with Apple again.
  3. If you still see AUTH-4031, go to Settings → [Your Name] → Password & Security → Apps Using Apple ID, find Brightline Home, tap it, then tap Stop Using Apple ID. Return to the app and sign in fresh — this resets the token without deleting your account data.
  4. If a duplicate account was created, do not use it. Contact Brightline Support at 1-833-274-5463 within 30 days and we'll merge or remove the duplicate at no charge.

Still Stuck?

For a full walkthrough of the initial Apple sign-in setup process, see Apple Sign-In Setup and Troubleshooting. If SMS backup codes are involved, check SMS Code Delivery Tips and Known Issues.

articles.title: How do I switch from Google sign-in to a regular email and password login?
articles.summary: Walks customers through converting their Brightline Home account from Google-linked authentication to a standalone email and password credential.
articles.question: I no longer want to use my Google account to log in to Brightline Home. Can I switch to a regular email and password instead, and will I lose any of my account history or billing data?
articles.answer:
What Changes and What Stays the Same

Switching login methods does not affect your production history, billing records, alerts, or payment methods. It only changes how you authenticate. Your account data is stored separately from your sign-in credential.

How to Switch

  1. Log in to Brightline Home using your existing Google account.
  2. Tap the Menu icon (☰) in the top-left corner, then go to Account Settings → Security & Login.
  3. Under Linked Accounts, tap Google and select Unlink Google Account.
  4. You'll be prompted to set a new password for your Brightline Home account. Your login email will automatically be set to the Gmail address previously used — you can change this to any address you prefer on the same screen.
  5. Tap Save Changes. You'll receive a confirmation email to your new address within 5 minutes. Click the verification link inside to activate the new credential.

Important Notes

  • You have 24 hours to click the verification link before it expires. If it expires, repeat the process from step 3.
  • If you don't receive the email, check your spam folder or see Google Sign-In Setup and Troubleshooting for known Gmail filtering issues.
  • For privacy questions about what Google data Brightline previously accessed, visit How Do I Request a Copy of My Personal Data.

articles.title: Add a Shared Device User to Your Brightline Home Account
articles.summary: Grant a household member or trusted person access to your Brightline Home app on a shared device without giving them your login credentials.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be the primary account owner to add a shared device user. The person you are adding must have a valid email address. Shared device users can view production monitoring and alerts but cannot change billing settings, approve payments, or modify autopay. A maximum of four shared device users is allowed per account.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and sign in as the account owner.
  2. Tap the Account icon (bottom-right corner), then select Household Access.
  3. Tap Add Shared User.
  4. Enter the person's first name, last name, and email address, then tap Send Invitation. An invitation email valid for 72 hours is sent to that address.
  5. Ask the new user to open the invitation email and tap Accept Invitation. They will be prompted to create a Brightline Home password or continue with an existing social login. See Apple sign-in setup and troubleshooting or Google sign-in setup and troubleshooting if they prefer a social login method.
  6. Once the user accepts, they appear in your Household Access list with status Active. You will receive a confirmation email at your account address.
  7. To adjust what the shared user can see, tap their name and toggle permissions under Access Level, then tap Save.

Troubleshooting

Invitation email not received: Ask the recipient to check their spam folder. If the email does not arrive within 10 minutes, return to Household Access, tap the pending user's name, and select Resend Invitation. Only one resend is allowed per 24-hour period.

"Maximum users reached" error (error code HH-401): You have reached the four-user limit. Remove an existing shared user before adding a new one by tapping their name and selecting Remove Access.

Shared user sees a blank dashboard: This usually resolves within 15 minutes of acceptance as the app syncs property data. If the dashboard remains blank after 30 minutes, ask the shared user to sign out and sign back in. If the problem persists, contact Brightline Support with your account email and the shared user's email so our team can manually link the user record.

articles.title: Remove or Change Permissions for a Shared Device User
articles.summary: Revoke access or update what a shared device user can see in Brightline Home, for example after a roommate moves out or household responsibilities change.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Only the primary account owner can remove or modify shared device users. If you are selling your home, removing shared users is a recommended step in the transfer process; see solar transfer home sale process and update for the full checklist. Changes take effect immediately, and the affected user is notified by email within five minutes.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and sign in as the account owner.
  2. Tap the Account icon (bottom-right corner), then select Household Access.
  3. Tap the name of the shared user you want to modify.
  4. To change permissions only: Under Access Level, toggle individual permissions (e.g., View Alerts, View Production Data, View Invoices) on or off, then tap Save Changes. A confirmation banner appears at the top of the screen.
  5. To remove the user entirely: Scroll to the bottom of the user's detail screen and tap Remove Access. Confirm by tapping Remove in the dialog. The user's session is terminated on all devices within 60 seconds, and their account is unlinked from your property.
  6. Verify the change by returning to the Household Access list. A removed user no longer appears; a permission-updated user shows a Last modified timestamp.

Troubleshooting

Removed user can still log in (error code HH-403 on their device): Session termination normally takes up to 60 seconds. If the user reports access after two minutes, tap Force Sign-Out All Sessions on their detail screen (available under Household Access > [User Name] > Advanced Options). This immediately invalidates all active tokens for that user on your account.

"Save Changes" button is greyed out: Your app may be offline. Check your internet connection and try again. If the problem continues, force-close and reopen the Brightline Home app.

Permission changes not reflected on the shared user's device: Ask the user to pull down on the dashboard to force a data refresh. Changes to alert visibility may take up to five minutes to propagate. For persistent issues with alert settings not saving, see notification preferences not saving for general sync guidance that also applies to shared users.

articles.title: Brightline Home Now Supports Multiple Display Languages
articles.summary: Starting July 14, 2025, Brightline Home app users can select their preferred display language directly from their Profile settings.
articles.abstract: Brightline Home now offers in-app language selection, allowing customers to view menus, alerts, invoices, and support content in their preferred language. At launch, four languages are supported, with additional languages planned for later in 2025.
articles.body:
Effective July 14, 2025, all Brightline Home users on app version 4.11.0 or later can choose a display language from their Profile. This setting controls the language used throughout the app, including dashboard labels, alert messages, billing summaries, and notification text.

Supported Languages at Launch

  • English (default)
  • Spanish (Español)
  • French (Français)
  • Portuguese (Português)

How to Change Your Language

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Profile in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Display & Accessibility.
  3. Tap Language and choose your preferred option.
  4. Tap Save. The app will reload within 3 seconds.

Your language preference is stored to your Brightline account, so it persists across devices and after reinstalls. If you use shared device access, each user profile maintains its own language setting independently. For details on shared access, see Add a Shared Device User to Your Account.

Note: Legal documents, loan statements, and permit-related PDFs continue to be issued in English only, regardless of your language preference.

articles.title: Resolved: Language Preference Not Persisting After App Restart
articles.summary: A bug causing the Brightline Home language setting to reset to English after every app restart has been fixed in version 4.11.2, released July 28, 2025.
articles.abstract: Between July 14 and July 27, 2025, some Brightline Home users who selected a non-English display language found that the setting reverted to English each time they closed and reopened the app; this issue is now fully resolved in version 4.11.2.
articles.body:
Following the July 14, 2025 launch of multi-language support in Brightline Home, our engineering team identified a session-caching defect that prevented language preferences from being written correctly to account storage on iOS 16 and Android 12 devices. The fix was released in app version 4.11.2 on July 28, 2025.

Who Was Affected

PlatformAffected VersionsStatus
iOS4.11.0 – 4.11.1Resolved in 4.11.2
Android4.11.0 – 4.11.1Resolved in 4.11.2

What to Do

  1. Update Brightline Home to version 4.11.2 or later from your device's app store.
  2. Go to Profile > Display & Accessibility > Language and reselect your preferred language.
  3. Tap Save. Your preference will now persist across sessions and devices.

If notifications were delivered in English during the affected window and you missed a time-sensitive alert, we recommend reviewing your alert history under Profile > Notification History. For guidance on configuring future alerts, see Manage Notification Preferences.

We apologize for the inconvenience. No account data was lost as a result of this issue.

articles.title: How do I close my Brightline account?
articles.summary: Explains the steps, eligibility requirements, and timeline for permanently closing a Brightline Home account.
articles.question: I no longer need my Brightline account. How do I close it and what happens to my data and any remaining balance?
articles.answer:
Before You Request Closure

Account closure is permanent and cannot be undone. Before submitting a request, confirm the following:

  • No active solar agreement: Accounts tied to a current lease, PPA, or loan cannot be closed until the agreement is transferred or paid in full. If you are selling your home, see Solar Transfer: Home Sale Process instead.
  • Zero outstanding balance: Any unpaid invoices must be settled first. Partial payments are accepted if needed — see Partial Payments Now Accepted.
  • Autopay disabled: Cancel any active autopay enrollment before submitting your request to avoid unexpected charges.

How to Submit a Closure Request

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Profile → Account Settings → Close Account.
  2. Select a closure reason from the dropdown menu.
  3. Confirm your identity with a one-time SMS code sent to your registered phone number.
  4. Tap Submit Request. You will receive a confirmation email within 15 minutes (subject line: Your Brightline account closure request — #CL-XXXXXX).

What Happens Next

Our team reviews closure requests within 3–5 business days. Once approved, your account is deactivated and app access is removed. A $0.00 final statement is emailed to your address on file. Your personal data is handled according to our retention policy; to request deletion, visit How Do I Request Deletion of My Personal Data.

Need Help?

Contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 (Mon–Fri, 8 AM–6 PM ET) or chat in the app under Help → Live Chat.

articles.title: What happens to my data and billing when I close my Brightline account?
articles.summary: Details what Brightline does with your personal data, payment methods, invoices, and monitoring history after your account is closed.
articles.question: Once my Brightline account is closed, what happens to my billing information, production history, and personal data? Will I still get charged?
articles.answer:
Billing After Closure

No new charges are issued after your account closure is confirmed. However, any invoice already generated before the closure date remains due. A final statement is emailed within 2 business days of closure approval. If you had autopay active, it is automatically cancelled at closure — no further debits will occur.

What Happens to Your Data

Data TypeRetention PeriodNotes
Production & monitoring history7 yearsRequired for warranty and regulatory purposes
Invoice & payment records7 yearsRequired for tax compliance
Profile & contact information90 days, then deletedDeletion begins automatically
Saved payment methodsDeleted immediately on closureTokenized data purged from payment processor

Requesting Formal Data Deletion

Closing your account does not automatically trigger a formal data deletion request under applicable privacy law. If you want Brightline to delete specific records sooner than the standard retention schedule, you must submit a separate request. See How Do I Request Deletion of My Personal Data for instructions, and What Data Does Brightline Retain After a Deletion Request for details on legally required retention categories.

App Access

Brightline Home app access is revoked within 24 hours of closure confirmation. Any shared device users you previously added are also removed automatically at that time.

articles.title: Can I reopen my Brightline account after closing it?
articles.summary: Explains whether and how a closed Brightline account can be reactivated, including the timeframe, any fees, and what data is recoverable.
articles.question: I closed my Brightline account but I've changed my mind. Is it possible to reopen it, and will my old data still be there?
articles.answer:
Reopening a Closed Account

Yes, account reopening is possible, but only within a 30-day grace period from the date your closure was confirmed. During this window your account is placed in a suspended state rather than fully deleted, so your production history, billing records, and notification preferences are preserved.

How to Request Reactivation

  1. Email account-support@brightlinesolar.com with the subject line Account Reactivation Request and include the email address on your account.
  2. A support specialist will verify your identity using the last four digits of your installation address ZIP code and your account PIN.
  3. If approved, your account is restored within 2 business days and you will receive a confirmation email with a new temporary password.

After the 30-Day Grace Period

Once the grace period expires, Brightline initiates its standard data-deletion workflow. At that point, reactivation is not possible and you would need to create a brand-new account. Historical production data and billing records cannot be restored after deletion is complete. For details on what data is retained after deletion, see What data does Brightline retain after a deletion request?

Fees

There is a one-time $15 account reactivation fee applied to your first invoice after reopening. This fee is non-waivable.

If your system is being sold or transferred, reopening may not be the right path. Review Solar transfer and home sale process instead.

articles.title: What happens to my system monitoring and alerts when I close my Brightline account?
articles.summary: Describes how production monitoring, active alerts, and notification preferences are affected when a customer closes their Brightline account.
articles.question: If I close my Brightline account, will my solar panels still be monitored? What happens to any active alerts or notifications I had set up?
articles.answer:
Monitoring After Account Closure

When you submit a closure request in the Brightline Home app under Profile → Account Settings → Close Account, remote production monitoring is disabled immediately upon closure confirmation. Your microinverters and gateway hardware continue to operate and produce power normally — monitoring is a software service, not a hardware function.

What Happens to Active Alerts

All active and snoozed alerts are automatically dismissed at the moment of closure. You will not receive further push notifications, emails, or SMS messages related to system performance after that point. If you have alerts that require action (for example, a microinverter-offline alert), resolve them before closing. See Dismiss or snooze an active alert for instructions.

Notification Preferences

Your saved notification preferences are deleted as part of the closure process and cannot be exported or transferred to a new account.

Monitoring Subscription Fees

ScenarioMonitoring Fee Outcome
Closure mid-billing cycleProrated credit issued for unused days
Closure on billing dateNo charge for the new cycle
Annual planProrated refund within 10 business days

For a full explanation of how monitoring subscription charges appear on your invoice, see Understand the monitoring subscription line on your invoice.

Emergency Contact

If you close your account but experience a physical equipment issue, call the Brightline hardware support line at 1-800-555-0172 (available 7 days a week, 7 AM–7 PM local time).

articles.title: Why am I not receiving alert notifications from the Brightline Home app?
articles.summary: Explains the most common reasons alert notifications stop arriving and walks through the steps to restore them.
articles.question: I used to get push notifications and emails when something was wrong with my system, but I haven't received any alerts recently even though I think there may be an issue. Why are my alert notifications not coming through?
articles.answer:
Common Reasons Alerts Stop Arriving

There are several reasons you might stop receiving alert notifications from Brightline Home. Working through the checklist below resolves the issue in most cases.

1. Device or OS Notification Permissions

If your phone's operating system has blocked notifications for Brightline Home, no alerts will appear regardless of your in-app settings. On iOS, go to Settings → Notifications → Brightline Home and confirm Allow Notifications is toggled on. On Android, go to Settings → Apps → Brightline Home → Notifications and enable all notification categories.

2. In-App Alert Preferences Turned Off

Open Brightline Home, tap Account → Notification Preferences → Alert Notifications and verify that the alert types you expect—such as System Offline, Production Low, and Battery Fault—are individually enabled. Each alert category has its own toggle.

3. Do Not Disturb or Focus Mode

Scheduled Do Not Disturb or Focus Mode profiles on your device will suppress push notifications during active hours. Check your device's Focus/DND schedule and add Brightline Home as an allowed app if needed.

4. Email Alerts in Spam

Email alerts from alerts@mail.brightlinesolar.com may be filtered to your spam or promotions folder. Add this address to your contacts to prevent future filtering.

5. App Needs Updating

Versions of Brightline Home older than 4.2.0 have a known issue where alert delivery silently fails after 30 days. Update to the latest version from your device's app store.

For a full walkthrough of configuring which alerts you receive, see Set Up Alert Notifications or Manage Notification Preferences.

articles.title: What do the different alert severity levels mean in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Describes the three alert severity levels—Informational, Warning, and Critical—and explains what action, if any, you should take for each.
articles.question: I see alerts in the Brightline Home app that are different colors, and some say things like 'Warning' or 'Critical.' What do these severity levels actually mean, and do I need to do anything when I get one?
articles.answer:
Alert Severity Levels Explained

Brightline Home uses three severity levels to help you quickly understand how urgent an alert is and whether you need to act. Each level has a distinct color and icon in the app's Alerts tab.

LevelColorWhat It MeansTypical Action
InformationalBlueA normal system event worth noting, such as a scheduled firmware update completing or a routine self-test passing.No action required. You may dismiss the alert at any time.
WarningYellowA condition that may affect performance if left unaddressed, such as a microinverter reporting intermittent communication or production running 15–30% below the daily estimate.Monitor your system over the next 24–48 hours. If the warning persists, contact Brightline Support.
CriticalRedA condition requiring prompt attention, such as a complete system shutdown, a battery fault code (e.g., BF-402), or grid disconnection outside a planned outage.Do not attempt to reset hardware yourself. Tap Get Help inside the alert to open a support ticket. A technician will contact you within 4 business hours.

Snoozing vs. Dismissing an Alert

You can snooze a Warning or Informational alert for 1, 4, or 24 hours without dismissing it, so it reappears automatically if the condition continues. Critical alerts cannot be snoozed—they must be resolved or acknowledged by Support. For details on managing active alerts, see Dismiss or Snooze an Active Alert or Microinverter Offline Alert — What It Means.

articles.title: How do alert notifications work in the Brightline Home app?
articles.summary: Explains how Brightline Home detects system issues and delivers alert notifications to customers across push, email, and SMS channels.
articles.question: How does Brightline Home decide when to send me an alert, and how will I actually receive it?
articles.answer:
How Alerts Are Triggered

Brightline Home continuously monitors your solar system — including panels, inverters, and any connected battery — through our cloud monitoring platform. When a sensor reading or production metric falls outside expected thresholds, the system automatically creates an alert event. Common triggers include:

  • Production gap: Output drops more than 20% below your system's projected baseline for 30 consecutive minutes during daylight hours.
  • Device offline: An inverter or microinverter stops reporting data for more than 15 minutes.
  • Battery fault: A connected Brightline Reserve battery reports a temperature or charge error code (e.g., BAT-4031 or BAT-5002).
  • Grid event: An unexpected grid outage or voltage irregularity is detected at your meter.

How You Receive Notifications

Once an alert is created, Brightline Home sends notifications through whichever channels you have enabled in your account settings:

  • Push notification — delivered within about 2 minutes to your mobile device.
  • Email — sent to your account email address within 5 minutes.
  • SMS — sent to your verified mobile number within 5 minutes (carrier delays may occasionally apply).

All three channels are enabled by default for High and Critical severity alerts. For lower severity levels, only push and email are on by default.

Managing Your Preferences

You can customize which channels receive which alert types at any time. See Manage Notification Preferences for step-by-step instructions, or What Do the Different Alert Severity Levels Mean? to understand how severity affects delivery.

articles.title: Can I set quiet hours so alert notifications don't wake me up at night?
articles.summary: Describes how to configure a quiet-hours window in Brightline Home that silences non-critical alert notifications during times you choose.
articles.question: Is there a way to stop Brightline Home from sending me alert notifications in the middle of the night, without turning off alerts completely?
articles.answer:
About Quiet Hours

Yes — Brightline Home includes a Quiet Hours feature that lets you define a daily time window during which non-critical alert notifications are held and delivered as a single digest when the window ends. This way you stay informed without being woken by a push or SMS at 2 a.m.

How to Set Up Quiet Hours

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Notifications & Alerts, then tap Quiet Hours.
  3. Toggle Enable Quiet Hours to on.
  4. Set your Start Time and End Time (e.g., 10:00 PM – 7:00 AM).
  5. Tap Save. Changes take effect within 5 minutes.

What Quiet Hours Does — and Doesn't — Silence

Alert SeverityBehavior During Quiet Hours
Low / InformationalHeld; delivered as digest at window end
MediumHeld; delivered as digest at window end
HighHeld; delivered as digest at window end
CriticalSent immediately regardless of quiet hours

Critical alerts — such as a complete system shutdown (SYS-9001) or a battery thermal fault (BAT-5002) — are always delivered in real time because they may require urgent action.

Troubleshooting

If alerts are still arriving during your quiet window, confirm your phone's Focus / Do Not Disturb mode is not overriding app settings separately. For broader notification issues, see Why Am I Not Receiving Alert Notifications? or Set Up Alert Notifications.

articles.title: How is my CO2 offset figure calculated in the app?
articles.summary: Explains the methodology Brightline uses to convert your solar production into a CO2 offset number shown in the Reports section.
articles.question: The Reports tab shows a CO2 offset figure in pounds and metric tons, but I'm not sure how that number is calculated. Where does it come from and how accurate is it?
articles.answer:
Where the Number Comes From

Your CO2 offset figure in Brightline Home → Reports → Environmental Impact is calculated by multiplying your system's total kilowatt-hours (kWh) generated by a regional grid emissions factor. Brightline updates these factors quarterly using data from the seven regional transmission zones that cover the contiguous US (e.g., Zone NE-6 for the Northeast, Zone SW-3 for the Southwest).

The Formula

The calculation works as follows:

  1. Total kWh produced (pulled from your inverter telemetry over the selected date range)
  2. Multiplied by your regional emissions factor (displayed in lb CO₂ per kWh on the same screen — typical range: 0.38–0.82 lb/kWh)
  3. Result shown in pounds and automatically converted to metric tons (1 metric ton = 2,204.6 lb)

Accuracy and Limitations

The figure is an estimate, not a certified carbon credit. Emissions factors are regional averages and do not reflect real-time grid conditions. If your system was offline for any period, that time is excluded from the production total, which will reduce the offset figure accordingly.

Changing the Date Range

Tap the calendar icon at the top of the Environmental Impact screen to switch between Monthly, Annual, or Lifetime views. Lifetime figures begin from your system's Permission-to-Operate (PTO) date.

For questions about how production data is collected, see Production Estimates Methodology Update.

articles.title: Why did my CO2 offset figure suddenly change or drop?
articles.summary: Describes the common reasons a customer's CO2 offset number may decrease or shift unexpectedly, including quarterly factor updates and production gaps.
articles.question: My CO2 offset number in Reports went down compared to last month, and it even looks lower than it did a few weeks ago for the same time period. Did something go wrong, or is this normal?
articles.answer:
Most Common Reasons for a Change

There are three typical causes for a CO2 offset figure that looks lower than expected or has changed retroactively:

  • Quarterly emissions factor update: Brightline recalculates historical offset figures every quarter when new regional grid emissions factors are published (updates occur on Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, and Oct 1). If your region's grid became cleaner, the lb CO₂ per kWh factor decreases, which lowers your offset number even for past periods.
  • Production data revision: Occasionally, inverter telemetry is re-synced after a connectivity gap, correcting over- or under-reported kWh. This directly changes the offset total. You can verify whether a revision occurred by checking Reports → Production History → Data Quality Flags — any revised intervals show a yellow triangle icon.
  • System downtime: If a microinverter or gateway was offline, those hours produce zero kWh and therefore zero offset. See Microinverter Offline Alert — What It Means for steps to restore connectivity.

Is the Figure Certified?

No. As noted in our methodology, the CO2 offset is an informational estimate only and does not constitute a verified carbon credit or renewable energy certificate (REC).

Exporting Your Data

To keep a snapshot of your offset figures before a quarterly update, go to Reports → Environmental Impact → Export CSV. The export is timestamped with both the generation data and the emissions factor version used.

If you believe a production revision is incorrect, review Production Estimates Seasonal Adjustment — Winter 2025 for context on recent model changes.

articles.title: What units does Brightline use for CO2 offset figures, and what do they represent?
articles.summary: Explains the units, conversion factors, and real-world equivalents Brightline uses to display CO2 offset data in the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: My Reports tab shows a CO2 offset number but I'm not sure what the units mean or how accurate they are. Can you explain what I'm actually looking at?
articles.answer:
Understanding Your CO2 Offset Display

In the Brightline Home app, your CO2 offset figure is shown in pounds of CO2 equivalent (lbs CO₂e) by default. You can switch to kilograms by going to Reports → Environmental Impact → Units and selecting Metric. The toggle applies to all historical data immediately.

How the Conversion Works

Brightline multiplies your system's total kilowatt-hours (kWh) of solar generation by a regional grid emissions factor, expressed in lbs CO₂e per kWh. For example, a home in the Mid-Atlantic region currently uses a factor of 0.823 lbs CO₂e / kWh, while a home in the Pacific Northwest may use 0.341 lbs CO₂e / kWh due to a cleaner regional grid mix. Your specific factor is listed under Reports → Environmental Impact → Calculation Details.

Real-World Equivalents

To make the number more tangible, the app also shows optional equivalents:

  • Miles not driven — based on a fleet-average of 0.404 lbs CO₂e per mile
  • Tree-years of absorption — based on 48 lbs CO₂e absorbed per urban tree per year
  • Gallons of gasoline avoided — based on 19.6 lbs CO₂e per gallon

These equivalents are illustrative estimates and are clearly labeled as such in the app.

Related Articles

To understand how the underlying generation figures are calculated, see How is my CO2 offset figure calculated? If your offset figure changed unexpectedly, see Why did my CO2 offset figure change unexpectedly?

articles.title: Why do my Brightline CO2 offset figures not match what a third-party app or my utility portal shows?
articles.summary: Describes the most common reasons CO2 offset numbers differ between Brightline Home and external tools, and what customers can do about it.
articles.question: I compared my CO2 offset number in Brightline Home to what a third-party energy tracking app and my utility's portal are showing, and the numbers are all different. Which one is correct, and why don't they match?
articles.answer:
Why Differences Are Common

CO2 offset figures depend on two inputs that vary by source: generation data and emissions factors. It is normal for Brightline Home, your utility portal, and third-party apps to show different numbers because each uses its own values for both inputs.

Generation Data Differences

Brightline Home reads production directly from your inverter or microinverter array, typically updated every 15 minutes. Your utility portal measures energy at the meter, which reflects what actually flowed onto the grid and does not include power consumed directly by your home. Third-party apps often import data via manual export or delayed API feeds, which can introduce lag of 24–72 hours.

Emissions Factor Differences

Brightline applies the EPA eGRID subregion factor assigned to your service address, updated annually each January. Utility portals may use a statewide average, and third-party apps often use a national average factor, which is currently 0.709 lbs CO₂e / kWh—meaningfully different from regional figures. To see your exact factor, navigate to Reports → Environmental Impact → Calculation Details in Brightline Home.

What to Do

  1. Confirm your address is correct under Account → System Details so the right eGRID factor is applied.
  2. If you believe a data gap is causing a discrepancy, visit Reports → Environmental Impact → Export Data to download a CSV and compare totals manually.
  3. For persistent discrepancies larger than 5%, contact Brightline Support and reference error code ENV-304 in your message.

For more on how your base generation figures are produced, see Production Estimates Methodology Update and How is my CO2 offset figure calculated?

articles.title: Schedule Automated Reports in Brightline Home — Now Available
articles.summary: Brightline Home users can now set up recurring production and billing reports delivered directly to their inbox on a schedule they choose.
articles.abstract: As of July 14, 2025, all Brightline Home account holders can schedule automated reports — including monthly production summaries, billing snapshots, and CO₂ offset digests — to be emailed as PDF attachments on daily, weekly, or monthly cadences, eliminating the need to log in and export data manually each time.
articles.body:
Released: July 14, 2025

Report scheduling is now live in Brightline Home. Navigate to Account → Reports → Scheduled Reports → + New Schedule to get started.

Supported report types at launch:

  • Production Summary — daily, weekly, or monthly energy output
  • Billing Snapshot — current charges and payment status
  • CO₂ Offset Digest — cumulative and period offset totals
  • System Health Overview — alert counts and uptime percentage

Each schedule allows up to three recipient email addresses. Reports are generated between 2:00 AM and 4:00 AM local time and delivered before 6:00 AM on the scheduled day. PDF attachments are retained in-app under Reports → Archive for 24 months.

If a scheduled report fails to generate, you will receive an in-app notification within one hour and the system will retry automatically at the next available window. Persistent failures generate error code RPT-501, which you can report to support.

For details on how production figures within these reports are calculated, see Production Estimates Methodology Update.

articles.title: Partner API Now Supports Report Scheduling Endpoints — August 2025
articles.summary: Brightline's Partner API has been updated with new endpoints that allow integrators to create, modify, and delete report schedules programmatically on behalf of customers.
articles.abstract: Effective August 4, 2025, the Brightline Partner API (v2.6) introduces a dedicated /v2/report-schedules resource, enabling authorized integration partners to manage automated report delivery for their customers without requiring those customers to configure schedules manually in Brightline Home.
articles.body:
Released: August 4, 2025

Partners with the reports:write OAuth2 scope can now interact with the following endpoints:

MethodEndpointAction
POST/v2/report-schedulesCreate a new schedule
GET/v2/report-schedules/{id}Retrieve schedule details
PATCH/v2/report-schedules/{id}Update cadence or recipients

Accepted cadence values are daily, weekly, and monthly. Each schedule supports up to five recipient addresses. Webhook event report.generated fires when a PDF is ready, carrying a signed 48-hour download URL in the payload.

Duplicate POST requests using the same idempotency key within 24 hours will return the existing schedule record rather than creating a second entry. Requests missing the key return a 400 RPT-400 error. For guidance on correct key usage, see Partner API Idempotency Keys Best Practices Update.

Rate limits for this resource are set at 120 requests per minute per partner token.

articles.title: Updated Weather Delay Policy Takes Effect January 6, 2025
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is rolling out a revised weather delay policy that standardizes how installations are rescheduled when severe weather prevents crews from working safely.
articles.abstract: Beginning January 6, 2025, Brightline Solar's updated weather delay policy introduces clear trigger thresholds, automatic customer notifications, and a streamlined rebooking process, reducing the average time between a weather cancellation and a confirmed new installation date from 10 business days to 5.
articles.body:
Effective January 6, 2025, Brightline Solar is replacing its previous case-by-case weather cancellation process with a standardized policy that applies to all residential installation appointments nationwide.

What triggers a weather delay?

  • Sustained winds exceeding 25 mph at the job-site ZIP code
  • Active precipitation (rain, snow, sleet) forecast at 60% probability or higher within the 4-hour installation window
  • Temperature at or below 20°F (−7°C) at scheduled crew start time
  • Lightning within 10 miles of the site, per National Weather Service data

What happens next?

When a delay is triggered, you will receive an SMS and Brightline Home push notification by 6:00 a.m. local time on the day of your appointment. A new date will be offered within 48 hours, and no rebooking fee applies. Customers in high-volume regions (Mountain West, Upper Midwest) may see up to 72 hours for a confirmed slot during peak winter periods.

If your appointment is rescheduled more than twice due to weather, you may request a priority slot by contacting support — reference code WD-PRIORITY. For details on how arrival windows work, see Crew Arrival Windows Are Now Narrower.

articles.title: New In-App Weather Delay Tracker Now Live in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Brightline Home now includes a real-time weather delay tracker so customers can monitor their installation status and expected reschedule timeline without calling support.
articles.abstract: As of March 3, 2025, customers with an upcoming installation appointment can open the Brightline Home app and view a live weather delay status card that shows the specific condition causing any hold, the estimated window for rescheduling, and a direct link to accept or decline a newly offered date — all without contacting support.
articles.body:
Brightline Solar launched the Weather Delay Tracker inside the Brightline Home app on March 3, 2025. The tracker is visible to any customer whose installation appointment falls within the next 14 calendar days.

Where to find it

Open Brightline Home → tap My Project → select Appointment Details → scroll to the Weather Status card.

Status indicators

StatusMeaning
On ScheduleNo weather concerns detected for your window
WatchBorderline conditions; monitoring hourly
DelayedAppointment cancelled; reschedule offer pending
RescheduledNew date confirmed; tap to accept

Customers have 24 hours to accept a rescheduled date through the app before the slot is released. If no action is taken, the system will auto-assign the next available date and send a confirmation. A reschedule offer declined twice within the same delay event will require a manual call to the Scheduling team (reference code WD-MANUAL).

For same-day arrival window communications related to your rescheduled appointment, see Same-Day Crew Arrival Window Updates.

articles.title: What happens after my solar installation fails an inspection?
articles.summary: Explains the steps Brightline takes after a failed inspection, including correction timelines, re-inspection scheduling, and any associated fees.
articles.question: My installation just failed its municipal inspection. What does this mean for my project, and what will Brightline do next?
articles.answer:
Understanding a Failed Inspection

A failed inspection means the local Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) found one or more items on your installation that do not meet the applicable electrical, building, or fire code at the time of inspection. This is more common than many customers expect—roughly 12% of Brightline installations require at least one re-inspection—and it does not automatically indicate a serious problem with your system.

What Brightline Does Immediately

Within one business day of receiving the failed inspection report, your Brightline Project Coordinator will:

  • Review the inspector's correction notice (also called a "red tag" or "NOV").
  • Classify each deficiency as minor (paperwork or labeling), moderate (wiring adjustment), or major (structural or equipment change).
  • Contact you via email and the Brightline Home app with a summary and an estimated correction timeline.

Correction and Re-Inspection Timelines

Deficiency ClassTypical Correction WindowRe-Inspection Scheduled Within
Minor1–3 business days5 business days
Moderate3–7 business days10 business days
Major7–21 business days21 business days

Fees

Brightline covers the cost of the first re-inspection at no charge to you. If a second re-inspection is required due to the same uncorrected item, a $150 administrative fee may apply. Your coordinator will notify you before any fee is assessed.

Impact on Interconnection

Your utility interconnection application is paused while a failed inspection is open. Once the AHJ issues a passing inspection certificate, Brightline resubmits the documentation automatically. For context on interconnection timelines, see Utility Interconnection Delays – Summer 2025.
