  6. Log all results in your integration test suite before promoting code to the production environment.

Troubleshooting

Sandbox always returns live execution (never replays): Confirm your sandbox client ID is correct — production credentials are rejected by the sandbox and silently skip caching.

X-Sandbox-Expire-Idempotency-Key header has no effect: This header is only honoured when the request also carries a valid sandbox bearer token. Check token scope with the /v2/token/introspect endpoint.

Unexpected 429 errors during repeated test sends: Rapid retries in the sandbox share rate-limit quotas. Review What Does Error Code 429 Mean in the Partner API for guidance on backing off correctly.

articles.title: What happens when my payment card expires?
articles.summary: Explains what Brightline does when a saved card reaches its expiry date and how to avoid a missed payment.
articles.question: My credit card is expiring soon. What will happen to my Brightline payments, and do I need to do anything before the expiry date?
articles.answer:
How Brightline handles expiring cards

Brightline Home checks your saved card's expiry date 30 days before it expires and sends you an in-app alert and an email to your registered address. A yellow banner also appears at the top of the Billing tab reminding you to update your payment method.

What happens if the card expires before you update it

If your card expires and a payment is due, Brightline will attempt to charge the card one time. Most card networks pass updated card details to merchants automatically; if your issuer supports this, the charge may succeed without any action on your part. If the charge fails, the invoice moves to a Payment Pending status and you have 7 calendar days to add a valid card before a $9.95 late-processing fee is applied. After 30 days of non-payment, your account may be referred to our collections process.

How to update your card before it expires

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account → Billing → Payment Methods.
  2. Tap Add Payment Method and enter your new card details.
  3. Tap Set as Default to make it your primary card.
  4. Optionally remove the expired card by tapping it and selecting Delete.

Tips

  • Update your card as soon as your replacement arrives — typically 2–3 weeks before expiry.
  • If your new card has the same number but a new expiry date, you still need to re-enter it manually in the app.

For questions about specific charges on your invoice, see What is the monitoring subscription line on my invoice?

articles.title: My payment failed because my card expired — what do I do?
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for resolving a failed payment caused by an expired card and understanding any fees that may apply.
articles.question: I got a notification saying my payment failed because my card expired. How do I fix this and will I be charged any fees?
articles.answer:
Understanding the failed-payment notice

When a charge fails due to an expired card, Brightline Home displays an alert banner in the app and sends an email with the subject line "Action Required: Payment failed for your Brightline account." The notification includes the invoice number, the amount due, and the deadline to resolve the issue without incurring a late-processing fee.

Steps to resolve the failed payment

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account → Billing → Payment Methods.
  2. Tap Add Payment Method, enter your new or replacement card details, and tap Save.
  3. Tap Set as Default so future invoices use the new card.
  4. Go to Account → Billing → Invoices, locate the invoice marked Payment Pending, and tap Retry Payment.
  5. Confirm the charge; you will receive an email receipt within a few minutes if successful.

Fees and grace period

Days since failureStatusFee
0–7 daysPayment PendingNo fee
8–30 daysPayment Overdue$9.95 late-processing fee added
31+ daysReferred for collectionsAdditional fees may apply

Need to dispute a fee?

If you believe the late-processing fee was applied in error — for example, if you updated your card before the deadline but the retry did not process — contact Brightline Support via Account → Help → Contact Us with your invoice number. Fee waivers are reviewed case by case and typically take 3–5 business days to resolve.

Learn more about how financing and billing interact by visiting Does applying for Brightline financing affect my credit score?

articles.title: How do I update an expiring or expired payment card in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to replacing or updating a payment card in the Brightline Home app before or after it expires.
articles.question: My card is expiring soon (or has already expired). How do I update my payment method in the Brightline Home app so my bill gets paid on time?
articles.answer:
Updating Your Card in the Brightline Home App

You can replace or update a payment card at any time — ideally before your card's expiration date to avoid a failed payment and any associated late fees.

Steps to Update Your Card

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Billing & Payments, then tap Payment Methods.
  3. Tap the card you want to update or replace. If the card has already expired, it will be flagged with an orange "Expired" badge.
  4. To update the expiry date only, tap Edit Card and enter the new expiration date and CVV, then tap Save.
  5. To replace the card entirely, tap Add New Card, enter your new card details, and set it as the Default Payment Method. You may then delete the old card.

Important Timing Notes

  • Changes saved before 11:59 PM ET on your billing due date will apply to that billing cycle.
  • If your payment has already failed due to an expired card, the system will automatically retry within 24 hours of a successful card update.
  • A $3.50 returned-payment processing fee applies if the original charge was declined and not recovered within the retry window.

For details on what happens after a failed payment, see My payment failed because my card expired — what do I do?

articles.title: Will Brightline notify me before my payment card expires?
articles.summary: Explains the card-expiry reminder schedule Brightline uses and how to ensure you receive those alerts in time.
articles.question: Does Brightline send any warnings before my credit or debit card expires? I don't want to miss a payment just because I forgot to update my card details.
articles.answer:
Brightline's Card-Expiry Reminder Schedule

Yes — Brightline Home automatically sends a series of reminders when a saved payment card is approaching its expiration date, so you have plenty of time to update your details.

Reminder Timeline

Days Before ExpiryNotification Type
60 daysIn-app banner + email to account holder
30 daysPush notification + email
7 daysPush notification + email (marked Urgent)
Day of expiryIn-app alert + email with direct link to Payment Methods

Making Sure You Receive Reminders

  • Push notifications must be enabled for the Brightline Home app on your device. Go to Account > Notification Preferences > Billing Alerts and confirm Card Expiry Reminders is toggled On.
  • Check that your account email address is current under Account > Profile > Contact Information.
  • If you have enabled quiet hours, billing alerts are exempt and will still deliver at the time they are triggered.

If You Missed the Reminders

If a payment has already failed because your card expired, the account will enter a 7-day grace period before any service notices are issued. Update your card as soon as possible to avoid a $3.50 returned-payment fee.

See also: What happens when my payment card expires?

articles.title: How do I change my email address in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for updating the email address associated with your Brightline Home account.
articles.question: I need to update the email address I use to log in to Brightline Home. How do I change it, and how long does it take?
articles.answer:
Before You Begin

You must be logged in to make this change. Your new email address cannot already be associated with another Brightline Home account. If you use Sign in with Google or Sign in with Apple, see the section below.

Steps to Change Your Email

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap the Profile icon (bottom-right corner).
  2. Select Account Settings > Login & Security.
  3. Tap Change Email.
  4. Enter your current password to confirm your identity.
  5. Type your new email address and tap Send Verification Link.
  6. Open the verification email sent to your new address and tap Confirm Email Change within 24 hours.

Once confirmed, your login email updates immediately. A notification is also sent to your old address as a security alert. If you did not request this change, contact Brightline support at 1-800-555-0192 immediately.

Social Login Accounts

If your account is linked to Google or Apple, Brightline Home uses the email provided by that service. To change it, update your email with your social provider first, then unlink and relink the account under Login & Security > Connected Accounts.

Billing and Alerts

Your updated email becomes the address for all future invoices and alert notifications automatically. No separate update is needed. If you stop receiving alerts after the change, see Why am I not receiving alert notifications?

articles.title: Why isn't my email change going through in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Troubleshooting common reasons why an email address update may fail or the verification link may not arrive.
articles.question: I tried to change my email in Brightline Home but the verification email never arrived, or I got an error when I clicked the link. What should I do?
articles.answer:
Verification Email Not Arriving

  • Check your spam, junk, and promotions folders for a message from noreply@brightlinesolar.com.
  • Make sure you entered the new address correctly — tap Change Email again to resend.
  • Some corporate or school email systems block automated messages. Try a personal address if possible.
  • Allow up to 5 minutes for delivery during peak times.

Verification Link Errors

Error MessageCauseFix
Link expiredLinks are valid for 24 hours onlyRestart the process in Account Settings
Link already usedLink was clicked more than onceCheck whether the change already succeeded; if not, restart
Email already in useNew address belongs to another accountUse a different email address
Session mismatch (error AUTH-4031)Link opened in a different browser than the one used to request itCopy the link and open it in the same browser, or restart the process

Locked Out After a Failed Attempt

Three consecutive failed password confirmations during the email-change flow will temporarily lock the Login & Security section for 30 minutes. After the lock expires, try again or reset your password first.

Still Stuck?

Contact Brightline support via in-app chat (Profile > Help > Chat with Us) or call 1-800-555-0192. If you are concerned your account may have been accessed without your permission, also review how to close your Brightline account as a precautionary option.

articles.title: Brightline Home Update Cuts False Alarms by Up to 60% with New Smart Filtering Engine
articles.summary: A behind-the-scenes update to the Brightline Home alert engine, rolling out November 12, 2025, introduces smart debounce filtering that dramatically reduces nuisance false alarms caused by brief grid fluctuations and temporary shade events.
articles.abstract: Starting November 12, 2025, all Brightline Home customers will receive the updated Alert Filtering Engine (AFE v2.3), which applies configurable debounce windows and cross-sensor correlation checks before triggering a notification—eliminating the majority of false Low Production and Grid Fault alerts that have been reported during morning ramp-up periods and passing cloud events.
articles.body:
What Is Changing

Prior to this update, a voltage dip lasting as little as 3 seconds could generate a ALERT-4012 Grid Instability notification. AFE v2.3 raises the confirmation window to 90 seconds and requires agreement from at least two inverter channels before escalating to a customer-visible alert.

Expected Impact by Alert Type

  • Low Production (Severity: Warning) — false alarm rate reduced ~60%
  • Grid Fault (Severity: Critical) — false alarm rate reduced ~45%
  • Battery Discharge Anomaly (Severity: Info) — false alarm rate reduced ~55%

Roll-out Schedule

PhaseDateScope
1Nov 12, 2025New England & Mid-Atlantic regions
2Nov 19, 2025Southeast & Midwest regions
3Dec 3, 2025All remaining regions

No action is required. To understand how severity levels are assigned to each alert type, see What do the different alert severity levels mean?

articles.title: Known Issue: Weather-Sensor Firmware Bug Causing False Overtemperature Alerts — Fix Deploying January 8, 2026
articles.summary: A firmware defect introduced in Weather Sensor Module (WSM) version 4.1.0 is triggering spurious ALERT-5031 Overtemperature warnings for affected customers; a corrective firmware push is scheduled for January 8, 2026.
articles.abstract: Between December 18, 2025, and the corrective release on January 8, 2026, customers whose rooftop Weather Sensor Module received the WSM 4.1.0 automatic firmware update may see repeated ALERT-5031 Overtemperature (Critical) notifications even when ambient and panel temperatures are within safe operating ranges; no hardware damage is occurring, and Brightline is fast-tracking firmware version 4.1.2 to resolve the issue.
articles.body:
Am I Affected?

You are affected if all three of the following are true:

  • Your system was installed with a Weather Sensor Module (check Brightline Home → System → Hardware Details)
  • Your WSM firmware shows version 4.1.0 under Settings → Device Firmware
  • You received one or more ALERT-5031 notifications after December 18, 2025

What You Should Do Now

  • Do not power cycle your inverter — it will not resolve the false alert and may trigger a brief production outage.
  • You may safely dismiss or silence these specific alerts while the fix is pending.
  • If you have Quiet Hours configured, consider temporarily extending your window. See Can I set Quiet Hours for alert notifications? for steps.

Fix Timeline

MilestoneDate
WSM 4.1.2 staged rollout beginsJan 8, 2026
Full deployment completeJan 13, 2026
Post-fix monitoring period endsJan 20, 2026

Customers do not need to schedule a technician visit; the firmware update is applied automatically over Wi-Fi overnight.

articles.title: Make a Partial Payment on Your Brightline Account
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for submitting a payment amount less than your full balance due through the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be the account owner with billing permissions. Partial payments are available only on accounts in good standing or in an approved payment arrangement. Your account must have an outstanding balance of at least $10.00. Partial payments are not available within 3 days of an active autopay draft date; contact support to temporarily pause autopay before proceeding.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and sign in with your account owner credentials.
  2. Tap the Billing icon in the bottom navigation bar, then select Account Balance.
  3. On the Account Balance screen, tap Make a Payment.
  4. When the payment amount field appears, clear the pre-filled full-balance amount and enter the dollar amount you wish to pay. The minimum accepted partial payment is $10.00.
  5. Select your preferred payment method from the saved methods listed, or tap Add New Card / Bank Account to add one.
  6. Review the payment summary — confirm the amount, payment method, and the remaining balance that will be due after this payment.
  7. Tap Submit Payment. A confirmation screen will display a Payment Reference ID (format: PAY-XXXXXXXX). Save this for your records.
  8. You will receive a confirmation email at your account address within 5 minutes. If you do not receive it, check your spam folder or see how to verify your email address in Brightline Home.

Troubleshooting

"Payment amount below minimum" error: Ensure the amount entered is at least $10.00.

"Partial payments unavailable" message: Your account may have an active autopay scheduled within 3 days, or your account may have a restriction due to a prior returned payment. Call Brightline Billing Support at 1-800-555-0192 (Mon–Fri, 7 AM–7 PM local time) to resolve restrictions.

Payment posts but balance does not update: Allow up to 2 business days for bank-originated payments to fully reflect. Card payments typically update within 1 hour. If the balance still appears incorrect after 2 business days, contact support with your Payment Reference ID.

Autopay conflict: If autopay drafts your full balance before your partial payment clears, a duplicate-payment refund will be issued within 5–7 business days. See also what happens when your payment card expires for related billing scenarios.

articles.title: Set Up a Partial Payment Arrangement with Brightline
articles.summary: How to request and activate a formal partial payment plan when you cannot pay your full balance by the due date.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Payment arrangements are available to account owners who have received a past-due notice (balance overdue by 1–90 days). Accounts with balances overdue more than 90 days must speak with a Billing Specialist directly. You will need your Brightline account number (found on any invoice under Billing › Invoice History) and a valid payment method on file. Enrolling in a payment arrangement pauses late fees for the arrangement period but does not waive them; fees already assessed remain on the account.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and sign in as the account owner.
  2. Navigate to Billing › Account Balance. If a past-due banner is displayed, tap Explore Payment Options; otherwise tap the ⋮ More menu and select Request Payment Arrangement.
  3. On the Payment Arrangement screen, review your total outstanding balance. The app will display up to three pre-calculated plan options (e.g., 2-month, 3-month, or 4-month splits) based on your balance and account history.
  4. Select the plan that works for you, or tap Custom Amount to propose a different first-payment amount. Custom proposals must cover at least 25% of the outstanding balance as a down payment.
  5. Choose the day of the month (1st–28th) for recurring arrangement drafts.
  6. Review the full arrangement schedule — dates, amounts, and the total balance breakdown — then tap Agree & Activate Arrangement.
  7. An arrangement confirmation will be emailed to you within 10 minutes. The confirmation includes your Arrangement ID (format: ARR-XXXXXXXX), the payment schedule, and terms. Store this document.
  8. Your first payment will be drafted on the date shown in step 6. Subsequent payments auto-draft monthly on your chosen day until the balance is cleared.

Troubleshooting

"Not eligible for self-serve arrangement" message: Your account may be outside the 1–90 day overdue window, or a prior arrangement may have defaulted. Call Billing Support at 1-800-555-0192 to discuss options.

Arrangement payment fails: If a scheduled arrangement draft fails, you have a 5-day cure window to make the payment manually via Make a Partial Payment before the arrangement is considered in default. You will receive an in-app alert and email at the time of failure.

Cannot see the "Request Payment Arrangement" option: This option is hidden if autopay is active and no balance is overdue. If you believe you have a qualifying past-due balance, force-refresh the app (pull down on the Account Balance screen) or log out and back in.

Monitoring subscription charges during arrangement: Ongoing monthly charges, including your monitoring subscription, continue to accrue during an active arrangement. See what the monitoring subscription line on your invoice means for details on that charge.

articles.title: What happens to my solar agreement when I sell my home?
articles.summary: When you sell your home, your Brightline solar agreement must be formally transferred to the buyer before closing—it cannot simply be left behind or cancelled without fees.
articles.question: I'm selling my house. What happens to my Brightline solar loan or lease agreement? Can the buyer just take it over, or do I have to pay it off first?
articles.answer:
Your Options at a Glance

When you sell your home, you have three paths for handling your Brightline solar agreement:

  1. Transfer to the buyer – The buyer assumes your remaining loan or lease. This is the most common outcome and has no early-termination fee.
  2. Prepay the balance – You pay off the full remaining principal before or at closing. A prepayment quote valid for 30 days can be requested in the Brightline Home app under Account → Financing → Request Payoff Quote.
  3. Buyer buyout at closing – The buyer purchases the system outright at a negotiated price; Brightline issues a lien release within 5 business days of receiving funds.

Transfer Is the Default Path

If the buyer qualifies and agrees to assume the agreement, Brightline will conduct a credit review of the buyer (typically 3–5 business days). Once approved, both parties sign a Transfer & Assumption Agreement electronically through Brightline Home. Monitoring access, billing, and alert settings move to the buyer's new account automatically at closing.

Important Timelines

StepTypical Duration
Initiate transfer requestSame day
Buyer credit review3–5 business days
Document signing & countersigning1–2 business days
Lien release recorded5–7 business days after closing

What If the Transfer Is Rejected?

If the buyer does not qualify, you will need to prepay or find an alternative arrangement. See What to do if a solar transfer is rejected or stalls for next steps.

To start the process, see How to transfer your solar agreement to a home buyer.

articles.title: Are there fees or costs when transferring my solar agreement to a home buyer?
articles.summary: Brightline charges a one-time transfer processing fee and may require an inspection; this article explains every cost you could encounter during a solar agreement transfer at home sale.
articles.question: My realtor mentioned there might be fees involved when I transfer my solar system to the buyer. What exactly will I be charged, and who pays what?
articles.answer:
Standard Transfer Processing Fee

Brightline charges a $299 Transfer Processing Fee for all loan and lease transfers completed at home sale. This fee covers document preparation, the buyer credit review, and lien-release recording. It is due at the time you submit the transfer request in Brightline Home under Account → Financing → Initiate Transfer and is non-refundable once the buyer credit review begins.

Who Pays the Fee?

The fee is billed to the seller's account by default. Some sellers negotiate for the buyer to cover it as part of closing costs—Brightline accepts payment from either party, but only one payer can be designated at submission.

Additional Costs to Be Aware Of

  • Transfer inspection (if required): If your system is more than 7 years old or has open service tickets, Brightline may require a transfer inspection at $149 before approving the assumption. You will be notified within 24 hours of submitting your request if this applies.
  • Monitoring subscription continuity: The buyer's monitoring subscription begins on the day the transfer closes. Any unused days the seller has pre-paid are not refunded but are credited to the buyer's first invoice. See Monitoring subscription charge after account closure or system transfer for details.
  • Late transfer surcharge: If the transfer request is submitted fewer than 10 business days before closing, an expedited processing surcharge of $75 applies.

No Penalty for Transferring

Unlike prepayment, a completed transfer carries no early-termination penalty. Only if you cancel the transfer mid-process and choose not to proceed with any other resolution path will a $50 administrative cancellation fee apply.

For a full walkthrough of the transfer steps, visit How to transfer your solar agreement to a home buyer.

articles.title: Who is responsible for the solar system during the home sale closing period?
articles.summary: Explains how responsibility for the solar agreement, payments, and system care is divided between seller and buyer during the period between listing and final closing.
articles.question: I'm selling my home and we're in escrow. My buyer wants to take over the solar agreement, but closing isn't for another six weeks. Who is responsible for payments, damage, and monitoring alerts during that time?
articles.answer:
Responsibility During the Closing Window

Until Brightline Solar issues a formal Transfer Confirmation Notice (TCN), the original account holder remains fully responsible for the solar agreement. This includes monthly loan or lease payments, any damage to equipment, and responding to system alerts in the Brightline Home app. Closing escrow with a title company does not automatically transfer the Brightline agreement.

What Changes — and When

  • Before TCN: Seller pays all invoices, receives production data, and is liable for equipment under the agreement's maintenance terms.
  • After TCN (typically 3–5 business days post-closing): The buyer's Brightline Home account becomes the active account; seller access is revoked within 24 hours of TCN issuance.
  • Monitoring subscription: The subscription fee follows the agreement — the buyer will see it on their first invoice. See Monitoring Subscription Charge After Account Closure or System Transfer for details.

Recommended Steps Before Closing

  1. Submit your Transfer Request in Brightline Home under Account → Solar Agreement → Transfer Ownership at least 15 business days before your target closing date.
  2. Ensure the buyer completes their credit and identity verification promptly — delays on their end do not pause your payment obligations.
  3. Do not cancel autopay until after the TCN is issued.

For a full walkthrough of the transfer process, see How to Transfer Your Solar Agreement to a Home Buyer.

articles.title: What happens if my home sale falls through after I started a solar transfer?
articles.summary: Describes how to cancel an in-progress solar agreement transfer if the home sale does not complete, and what fees or timeline impacts to expect.
articles.question: I started the process to transfer my solar agreement to a buyer, but the sale just fell through. How do I cancel the transfer, and will I be charged anything? Will my account go back to normal automatically?
articles.answer:
Canceling an In-Progress Transfer

If your home sale falls through before a Transfer Confirmation Notice (TCN) has been issued, you can cancel the pending transfer at no charge. Go to Brightline Home → Account → Solar Agreement → Transfer Ownership → Pending Transfer → Cancel Request. Cancellation is instant if the buyer has not yet signed their new agreement; if they have signed but the TCN has not been issued, allow 1–2 business days for Brightline's transfer team to unwind the records.

Fees to Be Aware Of

ScenarioFee
Cancelled before buyer signature$0
Cancelled after buyer signature, before TCN$75 administrative reversal fee
TCN already issued (transfer complete)Cannot be reversed; a new transfer must be initiated

What Returns to Normal

  • Your original payment schedule, autopay settings, and account permissions are restored automatically within 24 hours of cancellation confirmation.
  • Any monitoring alerts that were paused during the transfer review window will resume.
  • Your production history and lifetime stats remain intact — no data is lost.

If the Sale Falls Through Repeatedly

Multiple cancelled transfers within a 12-month period may require a manual review call with our Financing team before a new transfer request is accepted. Contact support at 1-800-555-0192 to schedule that review. For context on what causes transfers to stall or be rejected, see What to Do If a Solar Transfer Is Rejected or Stalls and What Happens to My Solar Agreement When I Sell My Home.

articles.title: Consumption Monitoring Is Now Live in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Brightline Home now displays your household electricity consumption alongside solar production, giving you a complete picture of your home's energy use.
articles.abstract: As of January 14, 2026, all Brightline Home customers with a compatible revenue-grade meter or Brightline-installed CT clamp can view real-time and historical household consumption data directly in the app, enabling side-by-side comparisons of how much energy your home draws versus how much your panels generate.
articles.body:
Released: January 14, 2026

Consumption monitoring is now available to all eligible Brightline Home users. To access it, open the app and navigate to Reports > Energy Overview > Consumption. Data refreshes every 15 minutes and is stored for up to 25 years.

The feature is available in three tiers depending on your installed hardware:

  • Full consumption + production: Brightline CT clamp installed at your main panel
  • Net consumption only: Utility bidirectional meter with smart-meter integration enabled
  • Production only (no change): Standard inverter monitoring, no CT clamp

You can export consumption data as a CSV or PDF from Reports > Download Report. Exported files include timestamps in local time and energy values in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

If your account shows "Consumption data unavailable," a CT clamp installation may be required; contact support to schedule a hardware upgrade visit, which carries a one-time fee of $149.

For customers who also use scheduled reports, consumption columns are now included automatically. See Report Scheduling Now Available in Brightline Home for setup instructions.

This feature is included at no additional cost for all active monitoring subscriptions.

articles.title: Consumption Monitoring Data Now Accessible via the Partner API
articles.summary: Partners can now retrieve household consumption metrics for enrolled sites through the new /v2/sites/{siteId}/consumption endpoint, available as of February 3, 2026.
articles.abstract: Brightline's Partner API has been updated to expose consumption monitoring data alongside existing production endpoints, allowing integration partners and third-party energy management platforms to build comprehensive household energy dashboards without requiring separate data pipelines.
articles.body:
Released: February 3, 2026

The new GET /v2/sites/{siteId}/consumption endpoint returns interval-level consumption data for sites where a CT clamp or smart-meter integration is active. The endpoint supports the following query parameters:

ParameterTypeDescription
intervalstring15min, hourly, or daily
start_dateISO 8601Range start (inclusive)
end_dateISO 8601Range end (inclusive, max 90-day window)
cursorstringPagination cursor for large result sets

Responses include consumption_kwh, net_kwh, and self_consumption_kwh fields per interval. Sites without eligible hardware return error code BL-4032 (Consumption data not available for this site).

The endpoint requires the energy:consumption:read OAuth2 scope in addition to existing production scopes. Partners must re-authorize affected tokens before February 28, 2026.

Pagination follows the same cursor-based model introduced last year; see Partner API Cursor-Based Pagination Launch for implementation details.

Rate limits are shared with the production endpoint pool: 600 requests per minute per partner credential.

articles.title: See How Your Solar Output Compares to Nearby Homes — Now in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Brightline Home's new Neighbor Comparison report lets you benchmark your system's production against anonymized local households with similar system sizes and sun exposure.
articles.abstract: Starting February 3, 2026, all Brightline Home app users can access the Neighbor Comparison report under Reports > Community Benchmarks. The feature anonymizes and aggregates production data from participating households within a 5-mile radius, grouping them by system size (±1 kW) and roof orientation, so your comparison is always apples-to-apples. If your output falls more than 15% below the neighborhood median, the report automatically flags potential causes — shading, soiling, or inverter underperformance — and links to a service request form.
articles.body:
What's New

Effective February 3, 2026, the Neighbor Comparison report is live for all residential Brightline Home accounts on Standard and Premium monitoring tiers. Basic-tier accounts will gain read-only access on March 1, 2026.

How to Access

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Reports in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Community Benchmarks.
  3. Choose a date range (monthly or annual views available).
  4. Tap Compare My System to generate the report.

Benchmark Grouping Criteria

VariableMatching Tolerance
System size±1 kW DC
Roof pitch±10°
Primary azimuth±15°
DistanceWithin 5 miles

Privacy

All neighbor data is anonymized; no addresses or account details are shared. A minimum of 8 matching households must exist in your area for the report to generate. If fewer matches are found, you'll see a "Insufficient local data" notice.

You can schedule this report for automatic monthly delivery — see Report Scheduling Now Available in Brightline Home for setup instructions.

articles.title: Neighbor Comparison Data Now Available via the Brightline Partner API
articles.summary: Partners can now retrieve anonymized neighborhood benchmark production data for enrolled sites using the new /v1/sites/{site_id}/neighbor-comparison endpoint, launched February 3, 2026.
articles.abstract: Alongside the consumer-facing Neighbor Comparison feature in Brightline Home, Brightline's Partner API now exposes the same benchmarking dataset through a dedicated REST endpoint. Available to all OAuth2-authenticated partners with the reports:read scope, the endpoint returns aggregated median, 25th-percentile, and 75th-percentile production figures for the anonymized peer group matched to a given site, enabling partners to surface actionable benchmarking insights inside their own dashboards and customer-facing tools.
articles.body:
Endpoint Details

Released February 3, 2026, the new endpoint is:

GET /v1/sites/{site_id}/neighbor-comparison

Required OAuth2 Scope

reports:read — no additional scope approval is needed if your application already holds this permission.

Query Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
periodstringYes"monthly" or "annual"
yearintegerYes4-digit year, e.g. 2025
monthintegerNo1–12; required if period=monthly

Response Fields

  • peer_median_kwh — median output of the matched peer group
  • peer_p25_kwh — 25th percentile
  • peer_p75_kwh — 75th percentile
  • site_output_kwh — the enrolled site's actual output
  • peer_count — number of anonymized households in the comparison

Error Codes

If fewer than 8 peer households match the site, the API returns HTTP 422 with error code NEIGHBOR_PEER_POOL_TOO_SMALL. For general 4xx guidance, see Partner API 4xx Error Code Reference.

Rate limits follow standard Partner API policy: 120 requests per minute per client credential.

articles.title: Schedule a Recurring Production Report in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Set up automatic weekly or monthly production reports delivered to your email directly from the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be logged in to the Brightline Home app (version 4.2.0 or later) as the primary account holder or an authorized account manager. Your system must have completed Permission to Operate (PTO) and have at least 7 days of recorded production data. If you want to review a one-time report instead, see How to View and Download Your Production Estimate Report.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Reports in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap Schedule Report in the upper-right corner of the Reports screen.
  3. Under Report Type, select Production Summary. Additional types (Consumption, Neighbor Comparison) appear if those features are enabled on your account.
  4. Under Frequency, choose Weekly (delivered every Monday for the prior week) or Monthly (delivered on the 2nd of each month for the prior month).
  5. Under Date Range Start, select the first period you want the schedule to cover. Reports will not be generated retroactively for periods before this date.
  6. Confirm the delivery email address shown. To use a different address, tap Edit Delivery Address and enter the new email. Note: changing the delivery address here does not change your Brightline account login email.
  7. Tap Save Schedule. You will see a confirmation banner: "Report schedule saved. First delivery: [date]."
  8. To review, pause, or delete an existing schedule, return to Reports > Scheduled Reports and tap the schedule name.

Troubleshooting

I saved a schedule but received no email on the expected date. Check your spam folder for messages from reports@brightline-notifications.com. If nothing is there, open Reports > Scheduled Reports and confirm the schedule status shows Active rather than Paused. Also verify the delivery email address is correct under Schedule Details.

The "Schedule Report" button is grayed out. This means your account does not yet meet the 7-day production data requirement, or your system is still pending PTO. The button will activate automatically once the requirement is met.

I see error BH-RPT-403 when saving. This error indicates your account role does not have scheduling permissions. Contact the primary account holder to grant you Account Manager access, then try again. For general app error guidance, see Partner API 4xx Error Code Reference for definitions shared across the platform.

articles.title: Configure Automated Report Schedules via the Partner API
articles.summary: Use the Partner API's Report Schedules endpoint to programmatically create, update, and delete recurring production or consumption report schedules for one or more customer sites.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Your integration must have a valid OAuth2 access token with the reports:write scope. Ensure you are familiar with cursor-based pagination if you plan to list schedules across many sites (see Partner API Cursor-Based Pagination). All requests must include an Idempotency-Key header when creating or modifying schedules to prevent duplicate records.

  1. Authenticate. Obtain a token from POST /v2/oauth/token with scope reports:write. Tokens expire after 3,600 seconds; refresh before expiry to avoid interruptions.
  2. Create a schedule. Send POST /v2/sites/{site_id}/report-schedules with a JSON body specifying: report_type (production_summary, consumption_summary, or neighbor_comparison), frequency (weekly or monthly), delivery_method (email or webhook), and delivery_target (email address or webhook URL). Include start_period in YYYY-MM format.
  3. Capture the schedule ID. A 201 Created response returns a schedule_id (format: rsch_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX). Store this for future updates or deletions.
  4. Update a schedule. Send PATCH /v2/sites/{site_id}/report-schedules/{schedule_id} with only the fields you want to change. Partial updates are supported; omitted fields retain their current values.
  5. Pause a schedule. Send the PATCH request with "status": "paused". Reports will not be generated while paused. Resume by sending "status": "active".
  6. List all schedules for a site. Send GET /v2/sites/{site_id}/report-schedules. Use ?cursor= and ?limit= query parameters to page through results.
  7. Delete a schedule. Send DELETE /v2/sites/{site_id}/report-schedules/{schedule_id}. A 204 No Content response confirms deletion. This action is irreversible.

Troubleshooting

Receiving 422 Unprocessable Entity. This typically means an invalid report_type value or a start_period that predates the site's PTO date. Check the errors array in the response body for the specific field causing the failure.

Receiving 409 Conflict on POST. A schedule with the same report_type and frequency already exists for this site. Retrieve existing schedules with a GET request and update the existing record instead of creating a new one.

Webhook deliveries are not arriving. Confirm your webhook endpoint returns a 200 status within 10 seconds; Brightline retries failed deliveries up to 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff. Check your server logs for the X-Brightline-Signature header to validate authenticity. For token-related errors blocking the entire request, see OAuth2 Token Lifetime and Error Handling.

Rate limit hit during bulk schedule creation. Space requests at least 200 ms apart and honor the Retry-After header returned with 429 responses.

articles.title: What is a crew arrival window, and how long is it?
articles.summary: Explains what a Brightline crew arrival window means, how wide the window is, and where to find yours in the app.
articles.question: My confirmation email mentions a "crew arrival window" for my installation day. What does that mean exactly, and how long is the window?
articles.answer:
What Is a Crew Arrival Window?

A crew arrival window is the range of time during which your Brightline installation crew is scheduled to arrive at your home. It is not a guaranteed single arrival time — crews move between job sites throughout the day, and travel time can vary due to traffic, weather, or how long a previous job takes.

Standard Window Lengths

Appointment TypeWindow Length
Full System Installation4 hours (e.g., 8 AM – 12 PM)
Add-On or Battery Installation3 hours (e.g., 10 AM – 1 PM)
Service or Inspection Prep Visit2 hours (e.g., 1 PM – 3 PM)

Where to Find Your Window

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap My Projects.
  2. Select your active project, then tap Upcoming Appointments.
  3. Your confirmed arrival window appears under Crew Arrival alongside the lead technician's name.

You will also receive a confirmation email and an SMS reminder 48 hours before your appointment that restates the window.

Day-of Updates

On the morning of your appointment, you will receive an automated push notification by 7:30 AM confirming whether the crew is on schedule. If the crew is running more than 45 minutes past the window end time, a Brightline scheduler will contact you directly.

For what to expect once the crew arrives, see Inspection Day: What to Expect (2025).

articles.title: My crew arrived outside my scheduled arrival window — what should I do?
articles.summary: Covers what to do if your installation crew arrives late or significantly early, and how to report or reschedule when the window is missed.
articles.question: The Brightline crew showed up more than an hour after my arrival window ended. What are my options, and can I report this or get a new appointment?
articles.answer:
First Steps When the Window Is Missed

If your crew has not arrived by the end of your scheduled window, wait up to 30 additional minutes — minor overruns are common. Check the Brightline Home app under My Projects > Upcoming Appointments for a real-time crew status badge labeled En Route, Delayed, or Rescheduling Required.

If the Status Shows "Delayed"

A push notification and SMS will be sent automatically with a revised estimated arrival time. No action is needed on your part unless the revised time no longer works for your schedule.

If You Need to Refuse or Reschedule

  1. Tap I Need to Reschedule on the appointment card in the app.
  2. Select Crew Did Not Arrive Within Window as the reason — this waives the standard $75 late-reschedule fee that applies to customer-initiated changes within 48 hours.
  3. Choose a new date from the next available slots, typically within 5–10 business days.

How to Report a Missed Window

If you believe the missed window caused a downstream problem — such as a utility coordination conflict — tap Contact Support in the app or call 1-833-BRTLINE (1-833-278-5463) and reference incident code SCH-MW. A scheduling supervisor will follow up within one business day.

Impact on Your Project Timeline

A single rescheduled installation appointment typically adds 1–2 weeks to your overall project timeline, which may affect your interconnection application status. For more on that process, see How to Track Your Utility Interconnection Application Status.

articles.title: Can I change my crew arrival window after I've already scheduled my appointment?
articles.summary: Explains how and when customers can modify their selected crew arrival window before installation day, including deadlines and any applicable fees.
articles.question: I picked a morning arrival window when I scheduled my installation, but my plans have changed and I need the crew to come in the afternoon instead. Can I switch my arrival window, and is there a deadline or fee to do that?
articles.answer:
Yes — You Can Change Your Arrival Window Before the Cutoff

Brightline allows you to modify your crew arrival window at no charge, as long as you make the change at least 72 hours before your scheduled appointment date. Changes requested inside that 72-hour window may incur a $75 late-change fee because your crew's routing and materials staging will already be finalized.

How to Change Your Window in Brightline Home

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap My Projects.
  2. Select your active installation appointment.
  3. Tap Modify Appointment, then choose Change Arrival Window.
  4. Select an available window from the calendar — options are 7 AM – 11 AM, 11 AM – 3 PM, or 1 PM – 5 PM depending on your region and crew availability.
  5. Confirm your selection. You will receive an updated confirmation email within 15 minutes.

What If No Other Windows Are Available?

If no alternate windows are shown on your preferred date, all slots for that day are full. You can either keep your current window or select a different date entirely. Rescheduling to a new date is treated as a standard reschedule and follows the same 72-hour policy.

Need Help?

If the app does not show a Modify Appointment option, your appointment may be locked for crew dispatch. Contact Brightline Support at 1-833-274-5463 as early as possible. You can also review what to expect on the day itself at Inspection Day — What to Expect.

articles.title: Why didn't I get a reminder about my crew arrival window before my appointment?
articles.summary: Explains the reminder notifications Brightline sends before a crew arrival window, common reasons they may not arrive, and how to verify your appointment details.
articles.question: My installation was scheduled for this week and I was expecting a reminder about my crew arrival window, but I never got one. Did something go wrong with my appointment? How do I confirm my crew is still coming?
articles.answer:
About Brightline Arrival Window Reminders

Brightline automatically sends arrival window reminders through the following schedule:

  • 7 days before: Email and push notification confirming your date and arrival window.
  • 48 hours before: SMS text with your crew arrival window and a link to your appointment details.
  • Morning of: Push notification between 6:30 AM and 7:00 AM local time with your crew's estimated on-site time within the window.

Common Reasons Reminders Don't Arrive

If you did not receive one or more of these notifications, check the following:

  • Push notifications disabled: In Brightline Home, go to Settings → Notifications → Scheduling Alerts and confirm alerts are toggled on.
  • Outdated contact info: Verify your phone number and email under Settings → My Profile. If your email recently changed, see How Do I Change My Email Address in Brightline Home to confirm the update completed successfully.
  • Appointment status change: A permit delay or weather hold can pause your appointment and suppress reminders. Check the My Projects tab for a status banner.
  • Spam or promotions folder: Brightline reminder emails come from no-reply@notifications.brightlinesolar.com — add this address to your safe senders list.

How to Confirm Your Appointment Right Now

Open Brightline Home, tap My Projects, and select your installation job. Your confirmed arrival window is displayed under Appointment Details. If the status reads Pending Confirmation or On Hold, contact Brightline Support at 1-833-274-5463 before your expected date. For self-serve scheduling options, see Site Survey Scheduling — Self-Serve Launch.

articles.title: Respond to a Weather Delay on Your Installation Day
articles.summary: Follow these steps when Brightline notifies you that your scheduled installation has been postponed due to unsafe weather conditions.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must have received a weather-delay notification via the Brightline Home app or SMS. Weather delays are issued when sustained winds exceed 25 mph, active precipitation is forecast during working hours, or temperatures fall below 28°F at the job site. No action is required to keep your agreement active; your project remains fully queued.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap My Project > Schedule. A yellow banner reading "Installation postponed – weather hold" will appear at the top of the screen along with the reason code (e.g., WX-WIND, WX-PRECIP, or WX-FREEZE).
  2. Tap View Rescheduling Options. The app will display the next three available installation windows, typically within 5–14 calendar days of your original date depending on crew availability and permit validity.
  3. Select your preferred date and tap Confirm New Date. You will receive an SMS and email confirmation within 15 minutes.
  4. If none of the offered windows work for you, tap Call Me to Discuss to request a scheduling specialist callback within one business day.
  5. Check your email for an updated crew arrival window notice 48 hours before your new installation date. For details on arrival windows, see What is a crew arrival window and how long is it?

Troubleshooting

The yellow weather-delay banner is not appearing, but my crew has not arrived. Pull down to refresh the Schedule screen. If the banner still does not appear after 30 minutes past your crew arrival window start time, tap Contact Support in the app or call 1-800-555-0192. Do not attempt to access your roof or electrical panel while awaiting crew.

My rescheduled date conflicts with my permit expiration. Brightline automatically flags permits expiring within 21 days. If your permit is at risk, a red alert labeled "Permit review needed" will appear alongside the rescheduling options. Tap it to connect with your project coordinator, who will file a no-fee extension request on your behalf within one business day. Also see Site survey weather delay policy update 2025 for related timeline rules.

I did not receive the delay notification. Verify your contact preferences under Account > Notifications in the Brightline Home app. Delays are sent at least 3 hours before the scheduled crew departure time.

articles.title: Reschedule Your Final Inspection After a Weather Delay
articles.summary: Use these steps to select a new final inspection date when a weather delay has caused your original municipal inspection appointment to be cancelled.
articles.body:
Before you begin: A final inspection weather delay occurs when the municipal inspector's office cancels due to hazardous conditions, or when Brightline cancels because site conditions would prevent a safe inspector walkthrough (e.g., standing water near the electrical panel, ice on the roof). Your system will remain in its pre-interconnection state and will not generate billable energy until the inspection is passed and utility authorization is received. Confirm you have the Brightline Home app version 4.3 or later installed.

  1. Open Brightline Home and navigate to My Project > Inspections. A status chip reading "Inspection cancelled – weather" will be visible next to your Final Inspection line item.
  2. Tap Reschedule Inspection. The app will show available dates that Brightline has already pre-cleared with your local building department. Available slots are typically shown 3–10 business days out.
  3. Select a date and tap Request This Date. Brightline will submit the rescheduling request to the municipality within 4 business hours and confirm acceptance by email, usually within one business day.
  4. Once the municipality confirms, you will receive a final push notification with the confirmed inspection window. Keep the area around your main electrical panel, attic access, and roof access point clear and accessible.
  5. For details on what the inspector will check and how to prepare, see Inspection day: what to expect.
  6. After the inspection passes, Brightline will submit your Permission to Operate request to your utility. To track that step, see How to track your utility interconnection application status.

Troubleshooting

The "Reschedule Inspection" button is greyed out. This means Brightline has not yet received the official cancellation notice from your municipality. The button activates automatically once cancellation is logged, typically within 2 hours of the original appointment time. If it remains greyed out after 4 hours, contact support via Help > Chat in the app.

No available dates are shown. Some municipalities limit rescheduling slots during periods of widespread severe weather. If the calendar is empty, Brightline's scheduling team will contact you within 2 business days with options. You do not need to call the building department yourself.

My loan payments have already started but my system isn't live due to the delay. Weather-related inspection delays are documented in your project record. Contact your Brightline financing specialist at 1-800-555-0197 to discuss a deferral; note that deferral eligibility depends on your specific loan terms.

articles.title: What is utility interconnection and why does it take so long?
articles.summary: Explains what the utility interconnection process is, why it involves multiple parties, and what typical timelines look like for Brightline customers.
articles.question: My system is installed and passed inspection, but I still can't turn it on. Brightline mentioned something about 'utility interconnection.' What is that, and why is it taking so long?
articles.answer:
What Is Utility Interconnection?

Utility interconnection is the formal process through which your local utility company reviews your solar installation, approves it as safe to connect to the grid, and issues Permission to Operate (PTO). Until PTO is granted, your system cannot legally export energy—even if it is fully installed and has passed all local inspections.

Why Does It Take So Long?

Interconnection review involves several steps that Brightline cannot fully control:

  1. Application submission – Brightline submits your interconnection application to the utility within 2 business days of your final inspection passing.
  2. Utility queue review – Most utilities process applications in the order received. Queue wait times currently range from 15 to 45 business days depending on your utility district.
  3. Engineering study (if required) – Systems larger than 10 kW, or properties in older grid zones, may trigger an additional engineering study, adding 10–20 business days.
  4. Meter upgrade or net-metering enrollment – Some utilities must physically reprogram or swap your meter before PTO is issued.

What Can I Do While I Wait?

You can monitor your application's status in real time inside the Brightline Home app under Account → Permits → Interconnection Status. For a step-by-step walkthrough, see How to Track Your Utility Interconnection Application Status.

Brightline will notify you by push notification and email the moment PTO is received so you can power on your system without delay.

articles.title: What happens if my utility rejects my interconnection application?
articles.summary: Describes the common reasons a utility may reject or revise an interconnection application and the steps Brightline takes to resolve it.
articles.question: I got a notification saying my utility rejected my interconnection application. Does this mean I can't go solar? What happens next?
articles.answer:
A Rejection Is Not the End

A utility interconnection rejection is rarely permanent. In most cases it means the utility requires additional information, design changes, or a formal revision before it will approve your application. Brightline's Interconnection Team will contact you within 3 business days of receiving a rejection notice to explain the specific reason and outline next steps.

Common Rejection Reasons

ReasonTypical ResolutionAdditional Time
System size exceeds feeder capacityReduce export limit or upgrade request10–25 business days
Missing or incorrect single-line diagramBrightline resubmits corrected drawings5–10 business days
Expired electrical permitBrightline coordinates permit renewal7–15 business days
Meter incompatibilityUtility schedules meter swap10–30 business days

What Brightline Does on Your Behalf

Brightline handles all communication and document resubmission with the utility at no additional charge for the first revision cycle. If a second revision is required due to a utility-requested engineering change that affects physical hardware, a Brightline project coordinator will discuss any associated costs before proceeding.

How to Stay Informed

Track every status update inside the Brightline Home app under Account → Permits → Interconnection Status. For detailed guidance on responding to specific utility requests, see How to Respond to a Utility Interconnection Rejection or Revision Request.

articles.title: Refund Processing Times Shortened Starting December 1, 2025
articles.summary: Brightline Solar has reduced standard refund processing times from 10–14 business days to 5–7 business days, effective December 1, 2025.
articles.abstract: Beginning December 1, 2025, Brightline Solar is shortening its standard refund processing window for eligible overpayments, canceled service fees, and billing corrections from 10–14 business days to 5–7 business days, giving customers faster access to their funds with clearer status tracking inside the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
What's Changing

Effective December 1, 2025, all approved refunds issued by Brightline Solar will be processed within the updated timeframes below.

Refund TypeOld TimeframeNew Timeframe
Overpayment credit10–14 business days5–7 business days
Canceled service fee10–14 business days5–7 business days

How to Track Your Refund

Once a refund is approved, you will receive an email confirmation with a Refund Reference ID (format: RFD-XXXXXXXX). You can also check refund status in the Brightline Home app under Billing > Payment History > Refunds. If the status shows Pending Review beyond 3 business days, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192.

For questions about monitoring-related charges that may qualify for a refund, see Monitoring Subscription Charge Changed or Appeared Unexpectedly.

articles.title: Refund Eligibility Policy Clarified for Partial Payments and Expired Cards
articles.summary: Brightline Solar has updated its refund eligibility policy as of January 15, 2026 to explicitly cover partial payment overpayments and refunds to expired or replaced payment cards.
articles.abstract: As of January 15, 2026, Brightline Solar's refund policy has been updated to clarify how refunds are handled when the original payment card is expired or replaced, and to confirm that overpayments made through the partial payment feature are fully eligible for refund, removing a previous ambiguity that led to unnecessary support contacts.
articles.body:
Policy Update Effective January 15, 2026

Two common refund scenarios were previously not addressed explicitly in our policy documentation. The updated policy covers both situations:

  • Expired or replaced cards: If your original payment card is no longer active, refunds will be automatically rerouted to your current default payment method on file. If no active card exists, Brightline will issue a check mailed to your billing address within 10 business days of approval.
  • Partial payment overpayments: Any amount paid in excess of your outstanding balance via the partial payment feature is now explicitly eligible for a full refund. No manual adjustment request is needed; the system will flag the overage automatically within 2 business days.

What Has Not Changed

Refunds are still limited to payments made within the last 365 days. Promotional credits and referral bonuses remain non-refundable and non-transferable.

If a failed or expired card was involved in the original charge, review What Happens When My Payment Card Expires before submitting a refund request to ensure your account is in the correct state.

articles.title: Official Brightline Partner API SDKs Now Available for Python and Node.js
articles.summary: As of January 14, 2026, Brightline is shipping maintained, open-source SDKs for Python and Node.js to streamline Partner API integration.
articles.abstract: Brightline is releasing official SDKs for Python and Node.js on January 14, 2026, giving integration partners pre-built authentication flows, typed request/response models, automatic retry logic, and built-in support for cursor-based pagination—reducing the time needed to go from zero to a working integration from days to hours.
articles.body:
Available January 14, 2026, the Brightline Partner API SDKs are published to PyPI (brightline-partner-sdk) and npm (@brightline/partner-sdk) under the MIT license. Both packages are versioned independently and maintained by the Brightline Platform Engineering team.

What's included in v1.0.0

  • OAuth 2.0 client — handles token acquisition, refresh, and the MFA challenge flow introduced in November 2025 (see MFA enforcement update)
  • Typed models — request and response objects for Sites, Production, Consumption, Battery, and Estimates endpoints
  • Cursor pagination helpers — iterators that automatically follow next_cursor tokens
  • Automatic retry — exponential back-off on 429 and 5xx responses with configurable max-attempts
  • Idempotency key generation — UUIDv4 factory attached to every mutating request

Minimum requirements

SDKRuntimeInstall
Python3.10+pip install brightline-partner-sdk
Node.js18 LTS+npm install @brightline/partner-sdk

Sandbox support is included; set environment="sandbox" on the client constructor to route all calls to sandbox-api.brightlinesolar.com. Bug reports and feature requests can be filed via the Partner Portal under Developer Tools > SDK Feedback.

articles.title: Partner API SDK v2.0.0 Releasing March 3, 2026 — Breaking Changes and Migration Guide
articles.summary: SDK v2.0.0 introduces breaking changes to authentication, pagination, and error handling; partners must migrate before the v1 deprecation date of June 30, 2026.
articles.abstract: On March 3, 2026, Brightline will publish v2.0.0 of the Python and Node.js Partner API SDKs, consolidating feedback from the first two months of general availability and aligning the client interface with the October 2025 OAuth2 token lifetime changes and the September 2025 rate-limit headers—partners on v1.x have until June 30, 2026 to complete migration before v1 reaches end-of-life.
articles.body:
Release date: March 3, 2026. v1.x enters maintenance-only mode on that date and reaches end-of-life on June 30, 2026. No new features will be backported to v1 after March 3.

Breaking changes at a glance

Areav1.x behaviorv2.0.0 behavior
Token clientBrightlineClient(client_id, secret)BrightlineClient.from_env() or explicit AuthConfig object
PaginationManual next_cursor passingclient.sites.list().pages() async iterator
Error classesGeneric ApiError(code, message)Typed subclasses: RateLimitError, AuthError, ServerError
Retry configTop-level kwargsRetryPolicy dataclass passed to constructor

Migration steps

  1. Upgrade: pip install "brightline-partner-sdk>=2.0.0" or npm install @brightline/partner-sdk@2
  2. Replace direct constructor calls with AuthConfig or from_env()
  3. Update exception handlers to catch typed error subclasses (reference 4xx error code reference for mapping)
  4. Switch pagination loops to the new .pages() iterator

A full diff-based migration guide and a v1-to-v2 codemod script are available in the Partner Portal under Developer Tools > SDK Migration. Office-hours sessions will run every Tuesday in March 2026 at 1 PM ET; register via the Partner Portal.

articles.title: Brightline Launches Financial Hardship Program for Eligible Solar Customers
articles.summary: Starting March 1, 2025, qualifying Brightline customers facing financial hardship can apply for temporary payment relief, including reduced monthly payments and fee waivers.
articles.abstract: Brightline Solar is introducing a formal Financial Hardship Program on March 1, 2025, offering eligible loan and lease customers up to six months of reduced or deferred payments, late-fee waivers, and a temporary suspension of service interruption notices—helping customers stay current on their solar agreements during periods of demonstrated financial difficulty.
articles.body:
Program Overview

Effective March 1, 2025, Brightline customers enrolled in a Brightline Solar Loan or PPA/Lease Agreement may apply for hardship relief through the Brightline Home app under Account → Billing → Request Hardship Relief.

Available Relief Options

  • Reduced Payment Plan: Pay as low as 50% of your scheduled monthly amount for up to 3 months.
  • Full Payment Deferral: Defer up to 2 consecutive monthly payments (deferred balance added to end of loan term, no additional interest).
  • Late-Fee Waiver: All outstanding late fees (code FEE-LATE-01) waived upon approval.
  • Service Notice Hold: Suspension of escalation notices for up to 90 days.

Eligibility

Applicants must have an account in good standing for at least 12 months prior to the qualifying hardship event. Supporting documentation (e.g., termination letter, medical bill) is required and reviewed within 5 business days.

If your account has a recent declined payment, review how to make a partial payment on your Brightline account as an interim step while your hardship application is processed.

articles.title: Hardship Program Expanded: Extended Deferral Window and New Automatic Renewal Option Added
articles.summary: As of January 15, 2026, Brightline is expanding its Financial Hardship Program to allow up to five months of full payment deferral and introduce an automatic 30-day renewal for customers whose hardship continues beyond the initial approval period.
articles.abstract: Building on the program launched in March 2025, Brightline Solar is broadening its Financial Hardship Program on January 15, 2026, extending the maximum full-deferral window from two to five months, adding an automatic 30-day renewal option for customers with ongoing demonstrated need, and introducing a dedicated in-app hardship dashboard so customers can track their relief status in real time.
articles.body:
What Is Changing

The following updates take effect January 15, 2026 for all active and new hardship applications:

FeaturePrevious LimitNew Limit
Full Payment Deferral2 months5 months
Reduced Payment Plan3 months4 months
Service Notice Hold90 days150 days
Auto-Renewal OptionNot available30-day increments (max 2)

New In-App Hardship Dashboard

Navigate to Account → Billing → Hardship Status in Brightline Home to view your current relief type, months remaining, deferred balance, and renewal eligibility. Approval decisions are still delivered within 5 business days of document submission; auto-renewal requests are processed within 2 business days.

Existing Applicants

Customers approved before January 15, 2026 will have their plans automatically migrated to the new limits with no action required. For accounts with a payment arrangement already in place, see how to set up a partial payment arrangement with Brightline to understand how existing arrangements interact with hardship relief.

articles.title: Why isn't my SMS verification code arriving when I try to log in?
articles.summary: Explains the most common reasons an SMS login code may not be delivered and the steps to get back into your Brightline Home account.
articles.question: I requested an SMS verification code to log into the Brightline Home app, but the text never arrived. What should I do?
articles.answer:
Why Your Code May Not Have Arrived

Brightline Home sends one-time SMS codes from short code 72537. Delivery failures are almost always caused by one of the following:

  • Carrier filtering: Some mobile carriers block short-code messages by default, especially on prepaid plans.
  • Do Not Disturb / Focus mode: Your phone may be silencing unknown senders.
  • Outdated phone number on file: Your account may still have an old number stored.
  • Network congestion: Codes can be delayed up to 3 minutes during peak hours.

Step-by-Step Fixes

  1. Wait the full 3 minutes before requesting a new code — sending multiple requests rapidly can trigger a temporary 10-minute lock.
  2. Check that short code 72537 is not blocked in your carrier settings or messaging app blocked-senders list.
  3. Try tapping "Send via voice call instead" on the login screen; Brightline will read your code aloud.
  4. On the login screen, choose "Use email link instead" to receive a magic-link to your registered email address.
  5. If your phone number has changed, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 (Mon–Fri 7 am–8 pm ET) to update it after verifying your identity.

Still Locked Out?

If none of the above works, our support team can issue a one-time identity-verified access token. Have your account email and the last four digits of your solar agreement number ready. For email-related account issues, see How do I change my email address in Brightline Home?

articles.title: My SMS login code is delayed or keeps failing — is there a carrier block?
articles.summary: Covers how to identify and resolve carrier-level blocks on Brightline's SMS short code, including escalation steps and alternative login methods.
articles.question: I've tried requesting the SMS code several times and either nothing arrives or it arrives too late and says it has expired. Could my carrier be blocking it?
articles.answer:
How to Tell If Your Carrier Is Blocking the Code

Brightline sends login codes from short code 72537. A carrier block is likely if:

  • You never receive any texts from five-digit short codes.
  • The code arrives consistently late (more than 3 minutes), then shows as expired — codes are valid for exactly 5 minutes.
  • Your account shows error AUTH-SMS-403 in the app after a failed delivery attempt.

How to Unblock Short-Code Messages

The process depends on your carrier, but the general steps are:

  1. Text UNSTOP to 72537 — this re-opts your number into Brightline messages if you (or a previous owner of the number) previously opted out.
  2. Contact your carrier's support line and ask them to whitelist short code 72537 for your account.
  3. On prepaid plans, short-code messaging sometimes requires a one-time feature activation through your carrier's account portal.

Alternative Login Methods

MethodWhere to find itDelivery time
Voice call codeLogin screen → "Call me instead"~30 seconds
Email magic linkLogin screen → "Use email link"~1 minute
Support-issued tokenCall 1-800-555-0192Same session

Partner API Users

If you manage a Brightline integration and MFA codes are failing at the token endpoint, see Partner API MFA Enforcement for Token Endpoint for short-code troubleshooting specific to API credentials.

articles.title: Why isn't my SMS verification code arriving when I try to log in?
articles.summary: Explains the most common reasons an SMS login code never reaches your phone and what to do about each one.
articles.question: I requested an SMS verification code to log in to Brightline Home, but it never arrived. I've waited several minutes and still nothing. What's going on?
articles.answer:
Why your code may not arrive

Brightline Home uses six-digit SMS codes that expire after 10 minutes. If yours hasn't arrived, one of the following is usually the cause:

  • Wrong phone number on file. The code goes to the number registered in your account. If you recently changed carriers or got a new number, it may be going to an old line.
  • Carrier filtering. Some carriers flag automated SMS as suspected spam and silently drop the message. This is especially common with certain prepaid and regional carriers.
  • Do Not Disturb or blocked sender. Your phone may be filtering the message before it appears in your inbox.
  • Temporary SMS gateway delay. High-traffic periods can cause delivery to lag by 2–5 minutes. Wait the full 10-minute code window before retrying.
  • SIM not active. If your SIM card is in airplane mode or has no signal, messages cannot be received.

Steps to try right now

  1. Wait up to 5 minutes, then tap Resend Code on the login screen. You may resend up to 3 times per 30-minute window.
  2. Toggle airplane mode off and on to force your phone to reconnect to your carrier's network.
  3. Check that your phone number is correct by going to Profile → Contact Info inside the app (if you are already partially logged in via a saved session).
  4. Request the code via voice call instead by tapping Call me instead on the login screen.

If none of these steps work, see SMS Code Delays and Carrier Blocks for carrier-specific guidance, or contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192.

articles.title: How do I log in to Brightline Home if I can't receive SMS codes at all?
articles.summary: Covers alternative login methods and how to update your phone number when SMS verification is completely unavailable.
articles.question: I can't receive SMS codes—my phone number changed, my carrier keeps blocking them, or I no longer have access to that number. How do I still get into my Brightline Home account?
articles.answer:
Alternative ways to verify your identity

If SMS codes are not an option, Brightline Home offers two fallback methods you can use from the login screen:

MethodHow to accessRequirements
Voice callTap Call me instead on the verification screenPhone must be able to receive calls
Email linkTap Send a magic link to my emailAccess to your registered email address

If you can't use any of those methods

Contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 (available Mon–Fri, 7 AM–8 PM local time) or start a live chat in the app's help widget. An agent will verify your identity using your account PIN and last four digits of the SSN on file, then grant you a single-use temporary access token valid for 30 minutes.

Updating your phone number after you're back in

Once logged in, go to Profile → Contact Info → Mobile Number → Edit. Enter your new number and confirm it with an SMS code sent to that new number. Changes take effect immediately. Note that your old number will receive a security alert SMS notifying it of the update — this is expected behavior.

If your email address also needs updating, see How do I change my email address in Brightline Home? before making contact-info changes, to ensure you don't lose access to both verification channels at once.

articles.title: Why is my microinverter showing offline in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Explains the most common reasons a microinverter appears offline in the Brightline Home app and what each status means.
articles.question: My Brightline Home app is showing one or more microinverters as "Offline" with an orange alert badge. What does this mean and should I be worried?
articles.answer:
What the Offline alert means

A Microinverter Offline alert (alert code MI-401) appears in Brightline Home under Alerts > Active when the Brightline monitoring gateway has not received a status packet from a specific microinverter for more than 15 consecutive minutes. One offline unit does not stop the rest of your panels from producing energy.

Common causes

  • Temporary communication gap – The gateway and microinverter communicate over your home's power-line carrier (PLC) network. A brief grid fluctuation or large appliance switching on can interrupt the signal.
  • Wi-Fi or gateway restart – If your internet router or the Brightline Gateway (model BLG-3) rebooted recently, microinverters may take up to 20 minutes to re-register.
  • Shading or weather – During heavy cloud cover or nighttime hours, some microinverter models enter a low-power sleep mode and report as offline. This is normal; they will resume reporting at sunrise.
  • Firmware update in progress – Brightline pushes microinverter firmware between 11 PM and 2 AM local time. Units reboot during this window and may show offline briefly.
  • Hardware fault – A persistent offline status lasting more than 24 hours on a single unit during daylight may indicate a hardware issue.

What to do next

If the alert clears within an hour, no action is needed. For alerts that persist through a full sunny day, see our step-by-step troubleshooting guide. You may also review recent alert history by tapping Alerts > History in the app. To reduce nuisance alerts, review our false alarm reduction update.

articles.title: How do I troubleshoot a microinverter that won't come back online?
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for resolving a persistent Microinverter Offline alert in the Brightline Home app before contacting support.
articles.question: One of my microinverters has been showing offline for more than 24 hours and the alert (MI-401) is still active. What steps can I take myself before calling support?
articles.answer:
Before you begin

Work through these steps in order. Each step takes only a few minutes. Do not attempt to access rooftop equipment yourself — Brightline technicians handle all panel-level hardware.

Step 1 – Confirm it is not a nighttime or weather event

Check your production graph in Home > Production > Today. If all other microinverters also show zero output, a weather or grid event may be the cause. Wait for a clear day before continuing.

Step 2 – Restart the Brightline Gateway

  1. Locate the BLG-3 Gateway (usually near your electrical panel or router).
  2. Hold the Reset button for 3 seconds until the LED flashes amber.
  3. Wait 10 minutes for the gateway to reconnect and poll all microinverters.
  4. Reopen Brightline Home and check Alerts > Active.

Step 3 – Check your home Wi-Fi

The gateway requires a stable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi connection. Confirm your router is online and that the gateway LED shows a solid green (connected) rather than blinking blue (searching).

Step 4 – Run a manual microinverter scan

In Brightline Home, go to System > Devices > Microinverters, tap the offline unit, then tap Request Status Update. Results appear within 5 minutes.

When to contact Brightline

If the unit remains offline after completing all steps, tap Alerts > MI-401 > Contact Support to open a service ticket. A technician will remotely diagnose within 1 business day and schedule an on-site visit if required at no cost during your 10-year workmanship warranty period. For context on how weather can affect scheduled visits, see our weather delay policy.

articles.title: What causes a microinverter to show offline in Brightline Home?
