articles.summary: Explains the most common reasons a microinverter appears offline in the Brightline Home app and what each cause means for your system.
articles.question: My Brightline Home app is showing one or more microinverters as offline. What does that mean and what usually causes it?
articles.answer:
What the Offline Status Means

When the Brightline Home app displays a microinverter as Offline, it means our monitoring platform has not received a data heartbeat from that unit within the expected 15-minute reporting window. The affected panel icon will appear grey in the System Map view under Home > My System > Panel View, and an ALT-201 alert will be logged under Alerts > Active.

Common Causes

  • Communication gateway interruption: Your Brightline Gateway (the white bridge device near your electrical panel) may have lost its Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection. This is the most frequent cause and affects all microinverters simultaneously.
  • Temporary grid voltage fluctuation: A brief under-voltage or over-voltage event can cause individual microinverters to disconnect and wait for grid conditions to stabilize, typically resuming within 5–10 minutes.
  • Nighttime or low-light reporting gap: Microinverters do not transmit data when production is below 5 W. An offline alert that appears after sunset and clears by mid-morning is usually normal behavior.
  • Firmware update in progress: Brightline pushes firmware to microinverters between 2:00 AM and 4:00 AM local time. Units may show offline for up to 20 minutes during this window.
  • Hardware fault: Less commonly, the microinverter unit itself has failed and will require a service visit.

Next Steps

If the alert persists beyond 90 minutes during daylight hours, see our step-by-step troubleshooting guide. You can also review recent false-alarm patterns described in False Alarm Reduction Update – Brightline Home Alerts.

articles.title: My microinverter offline alert has not cleared — what should I do?
articles.summary: Walks customers through a step-by-step process to resolve a persistent microinverter offline alert in Brightline Home when basic causes have already been ruled out.
articles.question: The microinverter offline alert in my Brightline Home app has been showing for several hours during a sunny day and has not cleared on its own. What steps should I take to fix it?
articles.answer:
Before You Begin

Confirm the alert code shown under Alerts > Active is ALT-201 (single unit) or ALT-202 (multiple units). If you see ALT-210 (gateway offline), resolve the gateway connection first, as all microinverter data flows through it.

Step-by-Step Troubleshooting

  1. Restart the Brightline Gateway: Unplug the gateway's power adapter, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Allow up to 10 minutes for all microinverters to re-register.
  2. Check your home Wi-Fi: Confirm the gateway's status LED is solid blue. A blinking amber light means it cannot reach your router. Move the gateway closer to your router or use the Ethernet port if available.
  3. Inspect the circuit breaker: Locate the dedicated Solar Array breaker in your main panel. If it has tripped, reset it once. Do not reset more than once without contacting support.
  4. Force a data refresh in the app: Go to Home > My System > Panel View, pull down to refresh, and wait 5 minutes.
  5. Review alert history: Tap the ALT-201 alert and check First Seen and Last Seen timestamps to determine how long the unit has truly been offline.

When to Contact Support

ScenarioAction
Single unit offline > 4 hours, sunny daySchedule a remote diagnostic via Support > Request Diagnostic
All units offline > 1 hourCall Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192
Recurring daily alerts, same unitRequest a field inspection; unit may need replacement

For context on how recent firmware updates have affected alert frequency, see False Alarm Surge – Weather Sensor Firmware January 2026.

articles.title: Temperature Warning Alerts Now Live in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Brightline Home now sends real-time temperature warning alerts when your solar panels or battery system reach unsafe operating thresholds.
articles.abstract: Starting April 14, 2026, all Brightline Home customers with app version 4.7.0 or later will receive automated temperature warning alerts when panel surface temperatures exceed 185°F or drop below −10°F, and when battery module temperatures exceed 113°F or fall below 14°F—helping you act before heat stress or cold-weather conditions reduce system performance or trigger a safety shutdown.
articles.body:
Released: April 14, 2026

Temperature extremes are one of the leading causes of temporary solar and battery output loss. The new temperature warning alert system continuously monitors thermal data reported by your inverter and battery management unit and notifies you the moment readings enter a caution or critical range.

Alert Thresholds at Launch

  • Panel surface – Caution: ≥ 175°F or ≤ 0°F
  • Panel surface – Critical: ≥ 185°F or ≤ −10°F
  • Battery module – Caution: ≥ 105°F or ≤ 23°F
  • Battery module – Critical: ≥ 113°F or ≤ 14°F

Alerts are delivered via push notification, email, and in-app banner. You can adjust notification channels anytime under Settings → Alerts → Temperature Warnings in Brightline Home.

Critical alerts include a one-tap shortcut to your battery control panel so you can switch storage mode to Protect, which reduces charge/discharge cycling during thermal stress.

If you are seeing an unusually high volume of alerts, review our guidance on how Brightline reduces false alarm rates before contacting support.

Update to app version 4.7.0 via your device's app store to enable this feature. No additional hardware is required.

articles.title: Partner API Now Exposes Temperature Warning Alert Events via Webhooks and REST
articles.summary: Brightline's Partner API has been updated to deliver temperature warning alert data through both a new REST endpoint and webhook event payloads, giving integrators real-time thermal visibility across managed customer sites.
articles.abstract: Effective April 14, 2026, Brightline Partner API version 2026-04 introduces the GET /v2/sites/{site_id}/alerts/temperature endpoint and two new webhook event types—alert.temperature.caution and alert.temperature.critical—enabling third-party platforms to programmatically monitor panel and battery thermal conditions and trigger automated customer workflows without polling the Brightline dashboard.
articles.body:
Released: April 14, 2026 — API version 2026-04

Integrators can now consume temperature warning alert data in two ways:

MethodEndpoint / EventPolling Required
RESTGET /v2/sites/{site_id}/alerts/temperatureYes (pull)
Webhookalert.temperature.cautionNo (push)
Webhookalert.temperature.criticalNo (push)

Each webhook payload includes site_id, component (panel or battery), severity, measured_temp_f, threshold_temp_f, and triggered_at in ISO 8601 format.

The REST endpoint supports cursor-based pagination and returns up to 100 alert records per page. Requests that exceed rate limits return HTTP 429; see what error code 429 means for retry guidance.

Webhook subscriptions can be registered or updated via POST /v2/webhooks. Deliveries that fail to receive an HTTP 200 acknowledgment within 10 seconds are retried with exponential back-off for up to 24 hours. Authentication follows existing OAuth2 client-credentials flow; no credential changes are required for current partners.

articles.title: Why does my production estimate differ from my actual output?
articles.summary: Explains the common reasons a system's estimated annual production may not match real-world generation figures shown in Brightline Home.
articles.question: My production estimate report shows I should be generating around 9,200 kWh per year, but my actual output over the past 12 months was only about 7,800 kWh. Why is there such a big gap, and should I be worried?
articles.answer:
Why Estimates and Actuals Sometimes Diverge

Production estimates are calculated at the time of your site survey using historical solar irradiance data, your roof's pitch and azimuth, shading analysis, and the rated output of your specific panel model. They represent a long-run average under typical conditions — not a guaranteed figure for any single year.

Common Causes of a Lower-Than-Expected Output

  • Unusual weather: A year with significantly more cloud cover, rain, or wildfire smoke than the 20-year historical average used in your estimate will reduce generation.
  • Panel soiling: Dust, pollen, bird droppings, or debris can reduce output by 3–8% if panels have not been cleaned in 12+ months.
  • Shading changes: Tree growth or new structures near your home may create shading that did not exist during your site survey.
  • Inverter or microinverter underperformance: One or more underperforming units can drag total output down. Check the Device Status tab in Brightline Home for any flagged units.
  • System degradation: Panels degrade at roughly 0.5% per year, which is already factored into multi-year estimates but can appear as a small annual shortfall.

When to Contact Support

A gap of up to 10% below the annual estimate is generally within normal variance. If your shortfall exceeds 15% and weather alone does not explain it, contact Brightline Support — a performance review ticket can be opened from Reports → Production Estimate → Request Performance Review in Brightline Home.

For details on viewing and downloading your full estimate report, see How to view and download your production estimate report. To understand how estimates are built from your site data, see Site survey scheduling — self-serve launch.

articles.title: What time periods are covered in my production estimate report?
articles.summary: Describes the monthly, annual, and 25-year projection breakdowns available in the Brightline Home production estimate report and how to access each view.
articles.question: I opened my production estimate report in the app but I'm not sure what all the different sections mean — it seems to show numbers for this month, this year, and something called a 25-year projection. Can you explain what each section covers and how accurate each one is?
articles.answer:
Overview of Report Time Periods

Your production estimate report in Brightline Home (Reports → Production Estimates) is organized into three nested time horizons, each serving a different planning purpose.

Monthly Estimates

The Monthly tab shows expected kWh output for each calendar month based on your location's average solar irradiance profile. Summer months will show higher estimates than winter months. These figures update automatically if Brightline recalibrates your system model — you will see a Revised badge on any month that has been updated since your original installation estimate.

Annual Estimates

The Annual tab aggregates monthly figures into a full-year total and compares it against your actual metered production year-to-date. A green indicator means you are tracking at or above estimate; amber means 5–14% below; red means 15%+ below and may trigger a proactive support outreach from Brightline.

25-Year Projection

The 25-Year Projection tab models cumulative production across your system's expected lifespan, applying a 0.5% annual degradation rate to each successive year. This view also shows estimated lifetime savings in kWh and, where applicable, estimated utility bill offset in dollars based on the rate you provided during onboarding.

Accuracy and Revisions

  • Monthly and annual estimates carry a stated accuracy range of ±8%.
  • 25-year projections carry a wider range of ±15% due to long-term irradiance and rate uncertainty.
  • Estimates can be revised after a system expansion, panel replacement, or tariff change — you will receive an in-app notification when a revision occurs.

To schedule automatic report delivery to your inbox, see How to schedule a recurring production report in Brightline Home. If you access estimates programmatically, see Retrieve production estimates via the Partner API.

articles.title: How accurate is my production estimate, and what factors affect it?
articles.summary: Explains how Brightline calculates production estimates, the typical accuracy range, and the key variables that can cause your actual output to differ.
articles.question: My production estimate said I'd generate around 9,200 kWh this year, but I'm tracking noticeably lower. How accurate are these estimates, and what could be causing the gap?
articles.answer:
How Brightline Builds Your Production Estimate

Your production estimate is generated at the time of system design using a combination of your roof's pitch, azimuth, and shading profile, your local historical solar irradiance data (sourced from a 20-year weather dataset), and the rated output of your specific panel and inverter models. The result is a modeled annual figure—for most systems, within ±8% of actual output under typical conditions.

Common Reasons for a Wider Gap

  • Weather variability: A cloudier-than-average year in your area can reduce generation by 5–12% on its own.
  • Shading changes: Tree growth, new structures, or seasonal shadows not present during your site survey.
  • System downtime: Inverter faults, microinverter outages, or grid outages reduce cumulative output. Check the Alerts tab in Brightline Home for any recorded events.
  • Panel soiling: Heavy pollen seasons or bird activity can cut output 2–4% if panels haven't been cleaned.
  • Temperature extremes: Panels lose roughly 0.35% efficiency per °C above 25°C (77°F), so unusually hot summers affect totals.

What to Do If the Gap Seems Too Large

If your actual output is more than 10% below your estimate after accounting for the factors above, contact Brightline Support to request a Performance Variance Review. A technician will audit your monitoring data and flag any hardware issues. You can also review your full estimate breakdown in the app—see How to view and download your production estimate report for step-by-step instructions.

For a deeper look at specific time periods covered in your report, see What time periods are covered in my production estimate report.

articles.title: Can I get a revised production estimate after system changes or an expansion?
articles.summary: Covers when and how Brightline issues updated production estimates following panel additions, battery installs, inverter swaps, or significant shading changes.
articles.question: I recently added six more panels and a Brightline PowerBank 10 battery to my system. Will my production estimate be updated automatically, or do I need to request a new one?
articles.answer:
When a Revised Estimate Is Issued Automatically

Brightline automatically generates a new production estimate whenever a permitted system modification is completed and passes final inspection. This includes panel expansions, full inverter replacements, and battery additions that alter your system's rated capacity. The revised estimate typically appears in Brightline Home within 3–5 business days after your utility interconnection approval is updated in our records.

You will receive an in-app notification (under Reports > Production Estimates) and an email confirming the new estimate is ready.

When You Need to Request a Revision

Some changes are not captured automatically and require a manual request:

  • Significant new shading (e.g., a neighbor's new addition or mature tree growth)
  • Panel cleaning or derating corrections after a soiling audit
  • Corrections to roof orientation data identified after installation

To submit a revision request, go to Brightline Home > Reports > Production Estimates > Request Revision and select the reason from the dropdown. A Brightline energy analyst will review your case within 7 business days and issue a revised report or contact you for a site re-assessment.

What Changes Between the Old and New Estimate

FieldOriginal EstimateRevised Estimate
System size (kW DC)Based on original designUpdated to new capacity
Annual estimate (kWh)Original modeled totalRe-modeled total
Monthly breakdownOriginal profileAdjusted seasonal profile

For information on why your revised estimate might still differ from actual output, see Why does my production estimate differ from my actual output. API users can retrieve revised estimates programmatically via Retrieve production estimates via the Partner API.

articles.title: Weather Adjustments Now Applied to Production Reports in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Brightline Home now automatically applies weather adjustment factors to your monthly and annual production reports, giving you a clearer picture of how local conditions affected your system's output.
articles.abstract: Starting March 3, 2026, all production reports generated in the Brightline Home app include a new Weather Adjustment column that accounts for irradiance variance, cloud cover, and temperature deviations recorded at your installation address during the reporting period. This update helps customers distinguish between system performance issues and expected output reductions caused by adverse weather, making it easier to evaluate your system's true health.
articles.body:
As of March 3, 2026, weather adjustment data is automatically included in every production report accessed via Reports > Production > Monthly Summary or Reports > Production > Annual Overview in Brightline Home.

What's New

  • Weather Adjustment Factor (WAF): A percentage displayed alongside each period's actual output, showing how much weather reduced or exceeded the baseline irradiance model.
  • Adjusted Estimate column: Your original production estimate revised by the WAF for direct comparison.
  • Weather Event Flags: Periods affected by named weather events (e.g., storm systems, extended overcast) are tagged with a W indicator.

Sample Report Row

PeriodActual (kWh)WAFAdjusted Estimate (kWh)
Feb 2026412−8%419
Jan 2026388−14%395

Reports covering periods before March 3, 2026 will display WAF data retroactively for the preceding 24 months by March 17, 2026. For background on how estimates are calculated before adjustments are applied, see How Accurate Is My Production Estimate and What Factors Affect It.

articles.title: Weather Adjustment Fields Now Available on the Partner API Reports Endpoint
articles.summary: The Partner API's production reports endpoint now returns weather adjustment factor fields, enabling partners to surface weather-corrected output data in their own customer dashboards.
articles.abstract: Effective March 3, 2026, the Partner API GET /v2/reports/production endpoint includes three new optional response fields—weather_adjustment_factor, weather_adjusted_estimate_kwh, and weather_event_flags—allowing API partners to display weather-corrected production comparisons without maintaining their own meteorological data pipelines.
articles.body:
The new fields are available on March 3, 2026 for all partners with a valid OAuth2 token and the reports:read scope. No scope changes or contract amendments are required to access them.

New Response Fields

FieldTypeDescription
weather_adjustment_factorfloatDecimal multiplier (e.g., 0.92 = −8% weather impact) for the period.
weather_adjusted_estimate_kwhfloatOriginal estimate revised by the weather adjustment factor.
weather_event_flagsarray of stringsList of internal event codes (e.g., WEF-STORM-024) affecting the period.

Request Example

Add the query parameter include_weather_adjustments=true to your existing GET /v2/reports/production request. Omitting the parameter returns the previous response shape with no new fields, preserving backward compatibility.

Retroactive Data

Weather adjustment data is available retroactively for periods back to January 1, 2024. Requests for periods before that date will return null for all three fields.

For details on retrieving production estimates through the API, see Retrieve Production Estimates via the Partner API.

articles.title: View Your Lifetime Production Stats in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Follow these steps to find and interpret your system's all-time energy generation totals in the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be logged in to the Brightline Home app (version 4.2.0 or later) as the account owner or an authorized household member. Lifetime stats are available starting 24 hours after your system's Permission to Operate (PTO) date is recorded in your account. If your system was installed before March 2023, data is displayed from the earliest available meter reading, which may not represent day one of operation.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Dashboard on the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap the Reports tab at the top of the screen.
  3. Select Production Summary from the report type menu.
  4. Tap the Date Range picker and choose Lifetime from the dropdown. The picker defaults to the current calendar month.
  5. Review the summary cards that appear: Total kWh Generated, Estimated CO₂ Offset (lbs), and Estimated Bill Savings ($). Savings figures are calculated using your rate plan on file and are estimates only.
  6. Tap View Detailed Breakdown to see a year-by-year table of annual production totals.
  7. To save the data, tap the Share icon (upper right) and choose Download PDF or Export CSV. The file will be emailed to your account email address within five minutes.

Troubleshooting

Lifetime option is grayed out: Your system's PTO date may not yet be recorded. Contact Brightline Support if it has been more than 48 hours since your system was activated.

Totals appear lower than expected: If you had a monitoring gateway replacement or a microinverter swap, a small data gap may exist. See What causes a microinverter to show offline in Brightline Home for context on data gaps caused by offline events.

Export email never arrives: Check your spam folder. If it does not arrive within 15 minutes, retry the export or review your account email address under Settings > Account Info. For help updating your email, see How do I change my email address in Brightline Home.

articles.title: Retrieve Lifetime Production Stats via the Partner API
articles.summary: Use the Partner API's Reports endpoint to programmatically request all-time production totals for one or more customer systems.
articles.body:
Prerequisites: You must hold a valid OAuth2 access token with the reports:read scope. Your application must be approved for the Lifetime aggregation tier in the Brightline Developer Portal (Portal > App Settings > Data Access > Aggregation Tiers). Accounts without this tier approved will receive a 403 TIER_NOT_AUTHORIZED response. Refer to your token management workflow before proceeding; see Partner API OAuth2 Token Lifetime and Error Handling Update (October 2025) for current token expiry rules.

  1. Construct a GET request to https://api.brightlinesolar.io/v2/reports/production.
  2. Set the Authorization header to Bearer <your_access_token>.
  3. Add the query parameter period=lifetime. Optionally add system_id=<id> to scope the request to a single system; omit it to return all systems your token is authorized to access.
  4. Send the request. A successful response returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing total_kwh, co2_offset_lbs, estimated_savings_usd, data_start_date, and data_end_date fields.
  5. If you need a breakdown by year, append the query parameter granularity=yearly. The response will include a periods array with one object per calendar year.
  6. Cache responses on your side for at least 1 hour. Lifetime totals update once every 6 hours on Brightline's side; polling more frequently wastes quota and may trigger rate limiting.
  7. For bulk requests covering more than 500 systems, use pagination: include page=1&page_size=500 and iterate using the next_cursor field returned in the response envelope.

Troubleshooting

HTTP 429 Too Many Requests: You have exceeded the Reports endpoint rate limit of 120 requests per minute per application. Implement exponential backoff and honor the Retry-After header. See What does error code 429 mean in the Partner API for detailed guidance.

Empty total_kwh value (returns 0 or null): The system's PTO date is not yet recorded, or the system has no meter readings older than 24 hours. Verify the system status using GET /v2/systems/{system_id}/status before retrying.

HTTP 503 or intermittent failures: The Reports service may be under maintenance. Check the Brightline API Status page and review retry strategies at How do I troubleshoot 5xx errors in the Partner API.

Mismatched totals vs. app: Confirm your token's authorized system list matches the customer's account. Discrepancies of under 2% are expected due to rounding; larger gaps should be reported to Brightline Partner Support with the response's request_id value.

articles.title: Schedule Your Site Survey in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for booking your pre-installation site survey through the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must have an active Brightline account with a signed solar agreement and have completed your welcome call with your project coordinator. Site surveys are typically available within 5–10 business days of your agreement activation date. You will need location services enabled on your device or your home address confirmed in your account profile.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and sign in. If you have trouble receiving your SMS verification code, see SMS Verification Code Not Arriving in Brightline Home.
  2. Tap My Project in the bottom navigation bar.
  3. On the Project Overview screen, locate the Site Survey milestone card and tap Schedule Now.
  4. Select your preferred date from the available calendar. Dates shown in green have open slots; dates in gray are fully booked.
  5. Choose a crew arrival window (morning: 8 AM–12 PM, or afternoon: 12 PM–4 PM). For more information about arrival windows, see What Is a Crew Arrival Window and How Long Is It?
  6. Confirm your site access details: gate codes, dogs on premises, or parking restrictions. Enter these in the Access Notes field (500-character limit).
  7. Tap Confirm Appointment. You will receive an email and push notification confirming your booking within 5 minutes.
  8. Add the appointment to your device calendar by tapping Add to Calendar on the confirmation screen.

Troubleshooting

The Schedule Now button is grayed out. Your agreement may still be in countersignature review, or your welcome call has not been logged as complete. Contact your project coordinator at the number shown in the My Team tab to resolve this before rescheduling.

No dates are available within 10 business days. High seasonal demand can temporarily reduce availability. Tap Notify Me on the calendar screen; the app will send a push notification within 24 hours when a closer slot opens due to a cancellation.

You do not receive a confirmation email within 5 minutes. Check your spam folder for messages from noreply@brightlinesolar.com. If the email has not arrived after 30 minutes, tap Resend Confirmation in My Project > Site Survey, or call support at 1-800-555-0192.

articles.title: Reschedule or Cancel Your Site Survey
articles.summary: How to change or cancel an existing site survey appointment in the Brightline Home app, including deadlines and any applicable fees.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must have a site survey already scheduled on your account. Have your new preferred date ready before starting. Note the following policy limits: rescheduling is free if completed more than 48 hours before your appointment start time. Rescheduling or cancelling within 48 hours incurs a $75 late-change fee charged to your payment method on file. Same-day cancellations (within 4 hours of the window start) incur a $150 fee. If you need to update your payment card before proceeding, see How Do I Update an Expiring or Expired Payment Card in Brightline Home.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and sign in.
  2. Tap My Project in the bottom navigation bar.
  3. On the Project Overview screen, tap the Site Survey milestone card to expand it.
  4. Tap Manage Appointment in the upper-right corner of the card.
  5. Choose either Reschedule or Cancel.
    • Reschedule: Select a new date and arrival window, update any access notes if needed, then tap Confirm New Appointment. A revised confirmation email is sent within 5 minutes.
    • Cancel: Select a cancellation reason from the dropdown (required), then tap Confirm Cancellation. Your project timeline will pause until a new survey is scheduled.
  6. If a fee applies, a modal will display the charge amount and your card ending in the last four digits shown. Tap Accept & Continue to authorize the fee, or Go Back to keep your original appointment.
  7. Confirm the action. You will receive an updated email and push notification within 5 minutes.

Troubleshooting

The Manage Appointment button does not appear. Your survey may have been locked by your project coordinator because crew routing has already been finalized. In this case, call support at 1-800-555-0192 at least 24 hours before your appointment; an agent can make changes manually and advise on any applicable fees.

You were charged a fee but believe it was applied in error. If you rescheduled more than 48 hours before your appointment and were still charged $75, tap My Project > Billing History to locate the transaction, then tap Dispute Charge. Include your appointment confirmation number (format: SS-XXXXXXXX) in the dispute form. Resolution typically takes 3–5 business days. For guidance on what happens after a weather event forces a change outside your control, see What to Do When Your Installation Is Delayed by Weather.

Your cancellation confirmation email did not arrive. Check spam for noreply@brightlinesolar.com. If absent after 30 minutes, verify the cancellation status under My Project > Site Survey; if the appointment still shows as active, the cancellation did not save—repeat the steps above or call support.

articles.title: Grant Roof Access for a Scheduled Service Visit
articles.summary: Follow these steps to prepare your property and confirm roof access before a Brightline crew arrives for a maintenance or service appointment.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must have a confirmed service appointment on your Brightline Home account. You will receive a confirmation email with your appointment ID (format: SVC-XXXXXXXX) at least 48 hours before your visit. Ensure any roof-mounted obstructions such as satellite dishes or temporary equipment are removed before the crew arrives. If you live in a gated community or building with secured roof access, read Step 4 carefully.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Service in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap Upcoming Appointments and select the relevant appointment by its date or appointment ID.
  3. Tap Access & Preparation to open the roof access checklist.
  4. Toggle Roof Access Confirmed to On. If access requires a gate code, key, or building manager contact, tap Add Access Notes and enter the details. These notes are sent securely to your assigned crew lead at least 2 hours before the arrival window opens.
  5. If a dog or other animal has access to the yard or roof area, tap Pet on Property and follow the on-screen guidance to note containment arrangements.
  6. Tap Save & Confirm. You will see a green banner reading Access details saved and receive a confirmation SMS.

Troubleshooting

The Access & Preparation section is greyed out. This usually means your appointment is within 1 hour of the arrival window, at which point access notes are locked. Call Brightline Scheduling at 1-800-555-0192 to relay access information directly to dispatch.

I saved my access notes but the crew said they never received them. Notes sync to the crew app within 15 minutes of saving. If your appointment is more than 2 hours away, tap Access & Preparation again and verify the toggle is still On. If the toggle reset, this may indicate a sync error; force-close and reopen the app, then re-save. For further help, see What is a crew arrival window and how long is it?

My appointment does not appear under Upcoming Appointments. Appointments may take up to 30 minutes to appear after scheduling. If the appointment still does not show, contact support with your appointment ID.

articles.title: Request a Roof Access Waiver for a Service Appointment
articles.summary: Submit a roof access waiver when structural, legal, or safety conditions prevent Brightline crews from accessing your roof on the scheduled date, so your appointment can be reclassified or rescheduled without a cancellation fee.
articles.body:
Before you begin: A roof access waiver is only available to the primary account owner. Waivers must be submitted at least 24 hours before your appointment's arrival window opens; requests submitted later are subject to a late-cancellation fee of $75. Acceptable waiver reasons include active roof repair by a licensed contractor, a court or HOA-issued roof restriction order, or a documented structural safety concern. You will need to upload supporting documentation (PDF, JPG, or PNG, max 10 MB per file).

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Service, then Upcoming Appointments.
  2. Select the appointment for which you need the waiver and tap Manage Appointment.
  3. Tap Request Roof Access Waiver. If this option does not appear, your appointment type does not require roof access and no waiver is needed.
  4. Select the reason that best describes your situation from the dropdown: Active Third-Party Roof Work, HOA or Legal Restriction, or Structural Safety Concern.
  5. Tap Upload Documentation and attach your supporting file(s). At least one document is required for the waiver to be reviewed.
  6. In the Additional Notes field, briefly describe the situation and your earliest available date for rescheduling.
  7. Tap Submit Waiver Request. You will receive an email acknowledgment within 15 minutes. A Brightline Scheduling specialist will review your request and respond within 1 business day with a waiver decision and a rescheduled appointment offer.

Troubleshooting

I do not see the Request Roof Access Waiver option. This option only appears for appointments classified as requiring physical roof access (for example, panel cleaning, inverter swap, or post-storm inspection). If your appointment is an indoor electrical inspection, roof access is not required and no waiver is necessary.

My waiver was denied. Waivers are denied when the submitted documentation does not match the selected reason or is illegible. You will receive an email with the specific denial reason and instructions to resubmit. You have 4 hours from the denial email to resubmit before the original appointment is cancelled and the $75 fee applies.

I submitted a waiver but my appointment still shows as Confirmed. Appointment status updates after the waiver is approved, not at submission. This is expected. See Can I change my crew arrival window after scheduling? for related scheduling options while your waiver is under review.

articles.title: Prepare Your Home for Inspection Day
articles.summary: Follow these steps before your municipal inspection appointment to ensure the inspector has safe, unobstructed access and your system passes on the first visit.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Brightline will send an inspection confirmation notification in the Brightline Home app (under My Project > Permits > Upcoming Inspections) at least 48 hours before your scheduled date. Your inspection window is typically 4 hours (e.g., 8 a.m.–12 p.m.). An adult 18 or older must be present for the full window. If you need to reschedule, do so at least 24 hours in advance to avoid a $75 rescheduling fee charged to your account.

  1. Open Brightline Home, tap My Project, then tap Permits to confirm the inspection date, time window, and the name of the assigned municipal inspector.
  2. Clear a 3-foot path from your front door to your main electrical panel. Remove vehicles, storage bins, or equipment blocking the panel door or the area beneath your solar array.
  3. Locate and set aside any documentation the inspector may request: your Brightline installation completion certificate (available under My Project > Documents), the permit placard, and your interconnection approval letter.
  4. Ensure your Brightline gateway device has a solid green LED. If it shows amber or red, restart it by unplugging it for 30 seconds and reconnecting. A green light confirms the monitoring system is online, which the inspector will verify remotely.
  5. If you have a battery storage unit, leave it in Auto mode—do not manually force it to charge or discharge on inspection day, as the inspector will test automatic transfer switch behavior.
  6. On inspection day, greet the inspector at the scheduled start of your window and guide them to the electrical panel, attic access (if applicable), and roof access point.
  7. After the inspection, check My Project > Permits within 2 business days for your pass/fail result and next steps toward interconnection.

Troubleshooting

Inspector did not arrive within my window. Wait until 30 minutes past the end of your window, then call Brightline Support at 1-800-555-2477. Do not leave the property before calling; departing early is recorded as a missed inspection and may incur the $75 rescheduling fee.

Inspection failed due to a wiring discrepancy. Brightline will contact you within 1 business day to schedule a remediation visit at no charge if the issue originated from our installation. A re-inspection will then be booked automatically.

Gateway shows amber on inspection day. Follow the steps in How Do I Troubleshoot a Microinverter That Will Not Come Back Online for connectivity guidance, or call Support so a technician can push a remote reset before the inspector arrives.

For rescheduling after a weather cancellation, see How to Reschedule Your Final Inspection After a Weather Delay.

articles.title: Track and Respond to Your Inspection Day Results in Brightline Home
articles.summary: After your municipal inspection appointment, use the Brightline Home app to view the outcome, download official documents, and take the correct next action whether your system passed or requires a follow-up visit.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Your inspection must already have taken place. Results are posted to Brightline Home within 2 business days of the inspection date. You will receive a push notification and an email to your account address when the result is available. Make sure notifications are enabled under Settings > Notifications > Permit Updates in the app.

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap My Project in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap Permits, then tap Inspection History. Your most recent inspection appears at the top with a status badge: Passed (green), Failed – Brightline Action Required (amber), or Failed – Homeowner Action Required (red).
  3. Tap the inspection record to open the detail screen. You can view the inspector's notes, the permit number, and the inspection reference code (format: INS-XXXXXX).
  4. To download your official Certificate of Inspection, tap Download PDF. Store this document; your utility company will request it during interconnection review.
  5. If status is Passed: No action is needed on your part. Brightline automatically submits your interconnection package to your utility within 3 business days. You will receive a separate notification when interconnection is submitted. To learn more about what happens next, see What Is Utility Interconnection and Why Does It Take So Long.
  6. If status is Failed – Brightline Action Required: A Brightline technician will contact you within 1 business day to schedule a remediation and re-inspection visit. No fee applies. Monitor My Project > Permits for the new inspection date once booked.
  7. If status is Failed – Homeowner Action Required: The detail screen will list the specific correction needed (for example, replacing a non-code-compliant smoke detector or clearing a required clearance zone). Complete the listed items and then tap Request Re-Inspection to trigger scheduling. A $95 re-inspection coordination fee will be applied to your next billing cycle.
  8. After a successful re-inspection, repeat steps 1–5 to confirm the updated status and download the revised certificate.

Troubleshooting

Result not showing after 2 business days. First confirm the inspection took place by checking your confirmation email for the INS-XXXXXX reference code. If you have the code but see no result, tap My Project > Permits > Refresh or force-close and reopen the app. If the issue persists, contact Brightline Support with your reference code.

Download PDF button is greyed out. The certificate is generated by the municipality and may take an additional 1–2 business days beyond the result posting. If it remains unavailable after 4 business days, contact Support to request a manual document pull.

Utility rejects the package after a passed inspection. This is a separate process from the municipal inspection. See What Happens If My Utility Rejects My Interconnection Application for next steps.

articles.title: Do I need a separate permit for a ground-mount solar system?
articles.summary: Ground-mount solar installations require their own distinct permit set that differs from rooftop permits and typically involves additional review steps.
articles.question: I'm getting a ground-mount solar system instead of rooftop panels. Do I need different permits, or does Brightline handle it the same way?
articles.answer:
Ground-Mount Permits Are Different from Rooftop Permits

Yes — ground-mount systems require a separate and generally more complex permit package than rooftop installations. Because a ground-mount involves excavation, concrete footings, and a freestanding structure, most jurisdictions treat it as both an electrical permit and a structural/building permit, and some counties also require a grading or land-disturbance permit if more than 50 square feet of soil is disturbed.

What Brightline Submits on Your Behalf

Your Brightline project coordinator handles all permit applications. The standard ground-mount permit package includes:

  • Site plan showing setbacks, easements, and panel layout
  • Structural engineering stamp for the racking system (PE-stamped drawings, required in 38 of the 50 states we serve)
  • Electrical single-line diagram
  • Soil report summary if the jurisdiction requires it
  • Zoning compliance letter, where applicable

Typical Timeline

Ground-mount permit approval averages 4–8 weeks, compared to 1–3 weeks for rooftop permits. Jurisdictions with an HOA overlay or agricultural zoning can extend this to 10–12 weeks. Your Brightline Home app will show real-time permit status under My Project → Permits & Approvals.

Fees

Most permit fees are included in your Brightline installation contract. If a jurisdiction charges an additional structural review fee above $350, Brightline will notify you before submission and itemize the charge. See also: what to do when your installation is delayed by weather if permit approval pushes your install date.

articles.title: Why is my ground-mount permit taking longer than expected?
articles.summary: Several jurisdiction-specific factors can extend ground-mount permit timelines beyond the standard estimate, and this article explains the most common causes and next steps.
articles.question: Brightline told me my ground-mount permit would be approved in about six weeks, but it has been nine weeks and I still don't have a permit. What is causing the delay and what can I do?
articles.answer:
Common Reasons for Ground-Mount Permit Delays

Ground-mount permits involve more review departments than rooftop permits, which creates more opportunities for hold-ups. The most frequent causes are:

CauseTypical Added Delay
Jurisdiction requests a third-party structural peer review2–4 weeks
Zoning board or planning commission meeting cycle2–6 weeks
Missing or incorrect soil boring report1–3 weeks
HOA architectural review required1–4 weeks
Utility easement conflict flagged by county GIS1–3 weeks

How to Check Your Current Status

Open Brightline Home → My Project → Permits & Approvals. Each permit line item shows its current department, the date it was last updated, and any action items flagged with a yellow ! icon. If you see error code PMT-4402, the jurisdiction has placed the application on hold pending additional documentation — tap the error for details.

What Brightline Is Doing

Your project coordinator performs a status follow-up with the permitting office every 5 business days once a permit exceeds its estimated approval date. You will receive an in-app notification each time a follow-up is logged.

When to Contact Support

If your permit has exceeded the estimated date by more than 3 weeks and you have not received a status update in the last 7 days, contact Brightline Support via the app chat or call 1-800-555-0193. You may also want to review how to reschedule your final inspection after a weather delay if the permit delay has affected your inspection date.

articles.title: What documents are required for a ground-mount solar permit?
articles.summary: Ground-mount permits require a specific set of engineering, zoning, and site documents that differ from rooftop permit packages.
articles.question: My project is a ground-mounted solar system. What documents does Brightline need to submit for the permit, and is there anything I need to provide myself?
articles.answer:
Ground-Mount Permit Document Checklist

Ground-mount installations require a more extensive permit package than rooftop systems because they involve foundation work, setback reviews, and sometimes stormwater or grading approvals. Brightline prepares and submits the following on your behalf:

  • Structural engineering report – stamped by a licensed engineer, covering the racking foundation (helical piers, ballast, or concrete footings depending on your soil assessment)
  • Electrical single-line diagram – showing the AC/DC wiring path from array to your main panel or battery system
  • Site plan – scaled plot map indicating array location, property lines, setbacks, and overhead utility lines
  • Geotechnical or soil report – required by most jurisdictions when helical piers or concrete footings are used
  • Zoning compliance letter – confirming the array meets local height and setback rules

What You May Need to Provide

In some counties, the permit authority requires the homeowner of record to sign a notarized authorization form before Brightline can submit. Your project coordinator will send this via DocuSign if it applies to your jurisdiction. You may also need to provide a copy of your current property survey if one was not completed during your site assessment.

Typical Review Timeline

Once your complete document package is submitted, most jurisdictions return a decision within 15–35 business days. Complex parcels with HOA overlay districts or agricultural zoning can take up to 60 business days. You can track permit status in the Brightline Home app under My Project → Permits → Ground-Mount Permit.

For more on why permit timelines sometimes run long, see Why is my ground-mount permit taking longer than expected?

articles.title: Can I make changes to my ground-mount system after the permit has been submitted?
articles.summary: Design changes after permit submission often require a permit amendment, which can reset or extend your approval timeline and may involve additional fees.
articles.question: I asked to add more panels to my ground-mount array after Brightline already submitted the permit. Will that cause a problem, and how long will it delay my project?
articles.answer:
Why Changes After Submission Are Complicated

Once Brightline submits your ground-mount permit package to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), any change to the system design — panel count, inverter model, array orientation, or foundation type — typically requires a permit amendment or a full resubmission. Ground-mount systems are especially sensitive to design changes because the structural engineering report, site plan, and setback calculations are all tied to the exact array footprint and weight load.

Common Changes and Their Impact

Change TypeLikely OutcomeAdded Wait Time
Adding 1–4 panels (same footprint)Amendment required5–15 business days
Expanding array footprintNew structural stamp + resubmission15–30 business days
Swapping inverter modelElectrical diagram update, amendment5–10 business days
Changing foundation typeFull resubmission likely20–40 business days

Amendment Fees

Brightline charges a $175 permit amendment processing fee for changes requested after initial submission. Some jurisdictions also charge their own amendment filing fee, which is passed through at cost. Both charges will appear as a line item in your Brightline Home billing summary.

How to Request a Change

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to My Project → Design.
  2. Tap Request a Design Change and describe the modification.
  3. Your project coordinator will assess permit impact within 2 business days and send a written impact summary before any amendment is filed.

To understand the full permit process for ground-mount systems, see Do I need a separate permit for a ground-mount solar system?

articles.title: Paginate Through Large Result Sets in the Partner API
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for using the Partner API's cursor-based pagination to retrieve complete multi-page responses without duplicating or skipping records.
articles.body:
Prerequisites: You must have a valid OAuth2 access token with at least the read:sites scope. Pagination applies to any Partner API collection endpoint that returns a pagination object in its response envelope, including /v2/sites, /v2/reports, and /v2/alerts. Confirm your client library is up to date; see Partner API SDK Launch – Python & Node for version requirements.

  1. Make your initial request to the desired collection endpoint. Include the query parameter page_size (integer, 1–500; default 100) to control how many records are returned per page. Example: GET /v2/sites?page_size=200.
  2. Inspect the response envelope's pagination object. It contains three fields: total_records (total matching items), next_cursor (an opaque Base64 string), and has_more (boolean).
  3. If has_more is true, append the cursor query parameter to your next request using the value from next_cursor. Example: GET /v2/sites?page_size=200&cursor=eyJpZCI6MTIzfQ==.
  4. Repeat step 3, always using the next_cursor from the most recent response, until has_more returns false. Do not store or construct cursors manually; they expire after 15 minutes of inactivity.
  5. Aggregate your results across all pages in your application layer. Do not rely on record order across separate cursor sessions, as new records may be inserted between requests.

Troubleshooting

Error CURSOR_EXPIRED (HTTP 400): Your cursor was unused for more than 15 minutes or was malformed. Restart pagination from the first request with no cursor parameter.

Error INVALID_PAGE_SIZE (HTTP 422): Your page_size value is outside the 1–500 range. Adjust the parameter and retry.

Duplicate records across pages: This can occur if you reuse an old cursor after your access token was refreshed. Always pair a new token with a fresh pagination session.

Unexpectedly low total_records: Collection endpoints respect your OAuth2 scope's site permissions. If you expect more records, verify your token's granted scopes in the Developer Portal under Apps > Your App > Scopes. For report-specific pagination details, see How to Configure Report Schedules via the Partner API.

articles.title: Handle Pagination in Partner API Webhook Backfill Requests
articles.summary: How to use the Partner API's offset-based pagination on the webhook event log endpoint to backfill missed events after a delivery outage.
articles.body:
Prerequisites: Your application must have a registered webhook endpoint in the Developer Portal and an OAuth2 token with the read:events scope. This procedure covers the GET /v2/webhooks/events endpoint, which uses offset-based (not cursor-based) pagination because the event log is immutable and time-ordered. Use this workflow only to recover missed events; do not use it as a substitute for real-time delivery.

  1. Identify the time window you need to backfill. Note the UTC timestamp of the last successfully processed event stored in your system; you will use this as your starting boundary.
  2. Make an initial request to GET /v2/webhooks/events with the following query parameters: after (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of your last processed event), before (current UTC time or desired end boundary), and limit (integer, 1–200; default 50). Example: GET /v2/webhooks/events?after=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z&before=2026-03-02T00:00:00Z&limit=200.
  3. The response includes a top-level meta object with total, offset, and limit fields, plus a data array of event objects each containing an event_id, event_type, delivered_at, and payload.
  4. Process all events in the data array in ascending delivered_at order to preserve event sequence. Record the highest delivered_at value you successfully process.
  5. If offset + limit < total, increment your next request's offset parameter by the value of limit. Example: add &offset=200 to fetch the next page.
  6. Repeat steps 4–5 until offset + limit >= total. Resume normal webhook delivery once backfill is complete.

Troubleshooting

Error INVALID_TIME_RANGE (HTTP 422): The after value is later than before, or the window exceeds 30 days. Narrow your time range to 30 days or less per request and chain multiple requests for longer outages.

Error SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT (HTTP 403): Your token is missing the read:events scope. Re-authorize your application in the Developer Portal under Apps > Your App > Edit Scopes.

Missing events in backfill window: The event log retains records for 90 days. Events older than 90 days are permanently purged and cannot be recovered via this endpoint.

SDK helpers: The official SDKs include a backfill_events() convenience method that handles offset incrementing automatically. Upgrade to the latest SDK version before using it; see Partner API SDK v2 Breaking Changes – March 2026 for migration notes. For details on real-time alert event payloads, see Temperature Warning Alerts – Partner API Endpoint Launch.

articles.title: Webhook Retry Policy Updated: Longer Windows and Smarter Back-Off Starting April 1, 2026
articles.summary: Brightline is extending the maximum webhook retry window to 72 hours and switching to exponential back-off with jitter, effective April 1, 2026.
articles.abstract: Starting April 1, 2026, the Brightline Partner API will enforce a revised webhook retry policy that replaces the previous fixed 30-minute retry interval with an exponential back-off schedule and extends the total retry window from 24 hours to 72 hours, giving partner endpoints significantly more time to recover from outages before events are permanently discarded.
articles.body:
What Is Changing

The updated policy takes effect for all webhook subscriptions on April 1, 2026. Partners do not need to rotate credentials or re-register endpoints; the new schedule applies automatically.

New Retry Schedule

AttemptDelay After Previous Failure
1 (initial delivery)—
230 seconds (± 5 s jitter)
35 minutes (± 30 s jitter)
430 minutes (± 2 min jitter)
52 hours (± 5 min jitter)
68 hours (± 10 min jitter)
7 (final)24 hours (± 15 min jitter)

Failure Codes

Events that exhaust all seven attempts will be marked WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_FAILED (error code WH-4071) in the Partner Dashboard under Developer → Webhook Logs. Missed events can still be recovered using the backfill endpoint; see how to handle pagination in Partner API webhook backfill requests for details.

Action Required

  • Ensure your endpoint returns HTTP 2xx within 10 seconds; responses slower than 10 s are treated as failures.
  • Update any monitoring alerts that rely on the previous 24-hour discard window.

Questions? Contact your Partner Integration Manager or open a ticket at partners.brightlinesolar.com/support.

articles.title: New Webhook Retry Visibility Dashboard Now Live in the Partner Portal
articles.summary: Partners can now inspect per-event retry history, failure reasons, and manually trigger re-delivery directly from the Partner Portal's Webhook Logs screen.
articles.abstract: Brightline has launched a Webhook Retry Visibility Dashboard inside the Partner Portal, giving integration teams a real-time view of every delivery attempt for each outbound event, including HTTP response codes, latency, failure reason codes, and a one-click manual re-delivery option for events that have not yet been permanently discarded.
articles.body:
Available Now

The Webhook Retry Visibility Dashboard went live on March 18, 2026 and is accessible to all active Partner API accounts at Developer → Webhook Logs in the Partner Portal.

Key Features

  • Per-event attempt timeline: See each retry attempt, its timestamp, HTTP status code, and round-trip latency in milliseconds.
  • Failure reason codes: Codes such as WH-4001 (connection refused), WH-4022 (TLS handshake failure), and WH-5003 (endpoint timeout) are now surfaced inline.
  • Manual re-delivery: Any event with status PENDING_RETRY or WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_FAILED can be manually re-queued using the Resend button; re-queued events respect the current retry schedule.
  • Filterable log export: Export up to 90 days of webhook logs as CSV or JSON from the Export Logs menu.

Retention Policy

Log StatusRetention Period
Successfully delivered30 days
Failed (all retries exhausted)90 days
Manually re-delivered90 days

For accounts using the Python or Node SDKs, helper methods for programmatic log retrieval are documented in the SDK changelog; see Partner API SDK v2 breaking changes (March 2026) for version compatibility notes.

If you have questions, open a support ticket at partners.brightlinesolar.com/support and reference feature flag WHDASH-2026.

articles.title: What is an idempotency key and why do I need one in the Partner API?
articles.summary: Explains what idempotency keys are, why Brightline's Partner API requires them for certain requests, and how they protect you from duplicate operations.
articles.question: I keep seeing references to an "idempotency key" in the Partner API docs. What exactly is it, and do I really need to send one?
articles.answer:
What Is an Idempotency Key?

An idempotency key is a unique string you generate and attach to a Partner API request so that Brightline's servers can recognize a retry of the same operation and return the original result instead of executing the action a second time. If your network request times out or drops before you receive a response, you can safely resend the exact same request with the same key and know it will not be processed twice.

When Is It Required?

Idempotency keys are mandatory on all requests that create or modify state. This includes:

  • Payment and billing operations (POST /v2/payments)
  • Webhook subscription creation (POST /v2/webhooks)
  • Battery dispatch commands (POST /v2/devices/{deviceId}/dispatch)
  • Report schedule creation (POST /v2/report-schedules)

Read-only GET requests do not require an idempotency key because fetching data is already safe to repeat.

What Happens If I Omit It?

The API returns HTTP 400 with error code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISSING and the message: "A valid Idempotency-Key header is required for this request." The request is rejected and no action is taken.

Key Format Requirements

Keys must be 8–128 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, or underscores. UUIDs (v4) are the recommended format. Keys expire from Brightline's deduplication store after 72 hours.

For related guidance on scheduling report endpoints that require idempotency keys, see How to Configure Report Schedules via the Partner API.

articles.title: How do idempotency keys behave when a Partner API request fails or is retried?
articles.summary: Describes exactly how Brightline's Partner API stores, matches, and responds to retried requests that carry an idempotency key, including edge cases and error scenarios.
articles.question: I understand I need to send an idempotency key, but what actually happens on the server when I retry a request with the same key? What if my first attempt failed with an error?
articles.answer:
How the Server Processes a Keyed Request

When Brightline's API receives a request with an Idempotency-Key header, it checks its deduplication store for a record matching that key plus the authenticated OAuth2 client ID. This means keys are namespaced per client—two different partners can use the same key string without conflict.

Possible Outcomes on Retry

First-request resultRetry behavior
Success (2xx)Returns the cached response body and original HTTP status. No action repeated.
Client error (4xx)Returns the same cached error. The request is not retried on the server.
Server error (5xx) or no response recordedRequest is treated as new and executed again.

Important Edge Cases

  • Mismatched request body: If you reuse a key but change the request payload, the API returns HTTP 409 with error code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT. Always keep the body identical on retries.
  • Concurrent requests: Sending two requests with the same key simultaneously returns HTTP 409 with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT. Wait for the first to complete before retrying.
  • Expired keys: Keys older than 72 hours are purged. A request with an expired key is treated as a brand-new operation.

Recommended Retry Strategy

  1. Generate a UUID v4 key before the first attempt.
  2. Retry only on network errors or 5xx responses.
  3. Use exponential back-off: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, up to 5 attempts.

For details on how webhook deliveries interact with retry logic, see Webhook Retry Policy Update – Partner API March 2026.

articles.title: How long does an idempotency key stay valid in the Partner API?
articles.summary: Idempotency keys in the Brightline Partner API remain active for 24 hours, after which the same key can produce a new result if reused.
articles.question: I sent a request with an idempotency key and got a successful response. How long will the API continue returning that cached response if I send the same key again? And what happens after that window expires?
articles.answer:
Idempotency Key Validity Window

Every idempotency key you include in a Brightline Partner API request is stored in our deduplication cache for exactly 24 hours from the moment the request first reaches our servers. During that window, any repeat call using the identical key and endpoint will receive the original cached response—including the original HTTP status code, response body, and X-Brightline-Request-Id header—without triggering a second operation.

What Happens After 24 Hours

Once the 24-hour window closes, the key is purged from the cache. If you submit a new request using that same key after expiry, the API treats it as a brand-new request and executes the operation again. This can result in duplicate records or charges, so you should generate a fresh key for any intentional retry after the window has lapsed.

Key Format Requirements

  • Must be sent in the Idempotency-Key request header.
  • Maximum length: 128 characters.
  • Accepted format: UUID v4 (recommended) or any URL-safe alphanumeric string.
  • Keys are scoped per OAuth2 client ID—the same string used by two different clients does not conflict.

Checking Cache Status

If you need to confirm whether a key is still cached, inspect the response header X-Brightline-Idempotency-Status. A value of replayed confirms you received a cached result; original means the request was processed fresh.

For a foundational overview, see What is an idempotency key and why do I need one?

articles.title: Which Partner API endpoints require or support idempotency keys?
articles.summary: Idempotency keys are required on all state-changing Partner API endpoints and ignored on read-only GET requests.
articles.question: Do I need to include an idempotency key on every Partner API call I make, or only on certain endpoints? I want to make sure I'm sending keys where they matter and not wasting effort on requests that don't need them.
articles.answer:
Required vs. Optional vs. Unsupported

The Brightline Partner API enforces a straightforward rule: idempotency keys are required on all endpoints that create or modify data, optional-but-recommended on certain async trigger endpoints, and silently ignored on pure read operations.

MethodExample EndpointKey Required?
POST/v2/paymentsYes — 400 error if omitted
POST/v2/alerts/acknowledgeYes — 400 error if omitted
POST/v2/reports/scheduleRecommended (optional)
PATCH/v2/batteries/{id}/modeYes — 400 error if omitted
DELETE/v2/webhooks/{id}Yes — 400 error if omitted
GET/v2/production/lifetimeNot supported (ignored)

Error Code for Missing Keys

If you omit an idempotency key on a required endpoint, the API returns HTTP 400 with error code ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISSING in the response body. No operation is performed.

Conflict Errors

If you reuse a key on a different endpoint or with a different request body, you will receive HTTP 409 with error code ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT. Always pair a unique key with a unique logical operation.

Related Resources

To understand retry behavior when a request fails mid-flight, see How do idempotency keys behave when a Partner API request fails or is retried? For report scheduling specifics, see How to configure report schedules via the Partner API.

articles.title: Resolve OAuth2 Token Errors in the Partner API
articles.summary: Follow these steps to diagnose and fix the most common OAuth2 authentication errors returned by the Brightline Partner API, including expired tokens, invalid client credentials, and scope mismatches.
articles.body:
Prerequisites: You must have an active Brightline Partner account with API credentials issued from the Partner Developer Portal (portal.brightlinesolar.dev). You will need your client_id, client_secret, and the list of OAuth2 scopes your application requested at onboarding. If you are using the official SDK, ensure you are on version 2.x or later (see Partner API SDK v2 Breaking Changes – March 2026).

  1. Identify the error code. Every authentication failure returns a JSON body with an error field. Common values are OAUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED, OAUTH_INVALID_CLIENT, OAUTH_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, and OAUTH_TOKEN_REVOKED. Note the HTTP status code alongside it (typically 401 or 403).
  2. Check token expiry (OAUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED). Access tokens issued by the Brightline authorization server are valid for 3,600 seconds (1 hour). If your integration does not cache and refresh tokens proactively, request a new token using the client_credentials grant before the current token expires. The token response includes an expires_in field you should track.
  3. Verify client credentials (OAUTH_INVALID_CLIENT). Log in to the Partner Developer Portal, navigate to Settings > API Credentials, and confirm that the client_id and client_secret in your environment match exactly. Secrets are case-sensitive and must not contain leading or trailing whitespace.
  4. Confirm scopes (OAUTH_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT). The endpoint you are calling may require a scope your application was not granted. In the Portal, go to Settings > API Credentials > Manage Scopes and compare your granted scopes against the endpoint's documentation. Submit a scope expansion request from that same page; approval typically takes 1–2 business days.
  5. Handle a revoked token (OAUTH_TOKEN_REVOKED). Tokens are revoked when a partner account is suspended, a secret is rotated, or a security event is detected. Rotating your secret in the Portal automatically invalidates all existing tokens. Generate a new secret, update your environment variables, and request a fresh token.
  6. Test with a raw HTTP request. To isolate whether the error is in your SDK or your credentials, send a direct POST to https://auth.brightlinesolar.dev/oauth2/token with the Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded header and your credentials. A successful response returns 200 OK with an access_token.
  7. Retry your original request. Attach the new token in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header and confirm you receive a 200 or 202 response.

Troubleshooting

Error persists after rotating the secret: Allow up to 60 seconds for the new secret to propagate across Brightline authorization servers before retrying. Clock skew causes repeated expiry errors: The Brightline auth server rejects tokens if your server clock differs by more than 5 minutes; synchronize your system clock using NTP. Scope expansion not reflected after approval: You must request a new token after approval — existing tokens do not inherit newly granted scopes automatically. If none of these steps resolve the issue, open a support ticket from the Portal under Help > Contact Partner Support and include the X-Request-ID header value from the failed response. For guidance on idempotency when retrying failed requests, see How Do Idempotency Keys Behave When a Partner API Request Fails or Is Retried.

articles.title: Diagnose and Fix Webhook Authentication Failures in the Partner API
articles.summary: Use this procedure to identify and correct authentication failures on inbound Brightline Partner API webhooks, including invalid signature errors, mismatched secrets, and rejected endpoint responses.
articles.body:
Prerequisites: You must have at least one webhook subscription configured in the Partner Developer Portal under Webhooks > Manage Subscriptions. Your receiving endpoint must be reachable over HTTPS with a valid TLS certificate. You should have access to your server logs to inspect raw request headers. Familiarity with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification is assumed.

  1. Locate the failed delivery in the Portal. Go to Webhooks > Delivery Logs. Each delivery attempt shows the event type, HTTP status your endpoint returned, the X-Brightline-Signature-256 header value sent, and a Delivery-ID. Filter by status Failed to find recent errors.
  2. Identify the failure category. Brightline classifies webhook authentication failures into three types: SIG_MISMATCH (your endpoint rejected the signature), ENDPOINT_AUTH_REJECTED (your server returned 401 or 403), and TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED (Brightline could not establish a secure connection).
  3. Resolve SIG_MISMATCH errors. Brightline signs each webhook payload using HMAC-SHA256 with the Webhook Signing Secret shown in Webhooks > Manage Subscriptions > [Subscription Name] > Security. To verify: (a) retrieve the raw request body as bytes before any parsing, (b) compute HMAC-SHA256(signingSecret, rawBody), (c) compare the result to the value in the X-Brightline-Signature-256 header using a constant-time comparison function. A mismatch almost always means the signing secret in your code is stale — copy the current value directly from the Portal and update your environment.
  4. Resolve ENDPOINT_AUTH_REJECTED errors. If your receiving endpoint requires its own authentication (e.g., a bearer token in the request or an IP allowlist), ensure Brightline's delivery IP ranges are permitted. Current egress IP ranges are listed in the Portal under Webhooks > Delivery Settings > Egress IPs. Update your allowlist and re-enable the subscription.
  5. Resolve TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED errors. Confirm your endpoint's TLS certificate is valid, not self-signed, and covers the exact hostname registered in the Portal. Brightline requires TLS 1.2 or higher. You can test connectivity using the Send Test Event button in the Portal, which returns a detailed error message for TLS failures.
  6. Rotate the signing secret if it was exposed. In the Portal, go to Webhooks > Manage Subscriptions > [Subscription Name] > Security > Rotate Secret. During rotation, Brightline sends both the old and new signatures for a 24-hour grace period so you can deploy your update without downtime. Accept either valid signature during that window.
  7. Trigger a backfill of missed events. Once authentication is restored, you can request redelivery of failed events. See How to Handle Pagination in Partner API Webhook Backfill Requests for step-by-step instructions on retrieving missed payloads in order.

Troubleshooting

Signature still mismatches after updating the secret: Confirm you are reading the raw request body. Middleware that parses JSON before your verification handler will alter the byte sequence and invalidate the signature. Disable body pre-parsing for the webhook route. Deliveries stop after secret rotation: The 24-hour dual-signature grace period begins at the moment you click Rotate Secret; if your deployment takes longer than 24 hours, the old signature will no longer be accepted — rotate again and deploy immediately. Test events succeed but live events fail: Check that your production endpoint URL matches the registered URL exactly, including trailing slashes. Repeated failures trigger subscription suspension: Brightline suspends a subscription after 50 consecutive failed deliveries; re-enable it from the Portal after fixing the underlying issue. For details on retry timing and backoff behavior, see Webhook Retry Policy Update – Partner API March 2026. If the issue is unresolved, submit a ticket via Help > Contact Partner Support and include the Delivery-ID values from the failed attempts.

articles.title: Why did I receive a prorated charge on my invoice?
articles.summary: Prorated charges appear when your billing period starts or ends mid-month due to a plan activation, change, or cancellation.
articles.question: I just looked at my latest invoice and there's a line item called "Prorated Service Charge" that I don't recognize. Why am I being charged this, and how was the amount calculated?
articles.answer:
What Is a Prorated Charge?

A prorated charge covers a partial billing period rather than a full calendar month. Brightline Solar calculates your monthly monitoring, maintenance plan, or battery management fee on a 30-day cycle. When an event causes your billing period to begin or end on a day other than your normal billing date, we charge only for the days of service you actually received.

Common Reasons You May See a Prorated Charge

  • System activation mid-month: Your system went live on a day other than your regular billing date, so your first invoice covers only the days from activation through the end of that cycle.
  • Plan upgrade or downgrade: Switching between monitoring tiers (e.g., from Brightline Essential to Brightline Plus) triggers a prorated credit for unused days on the old plan and a prorated charge for days on the new plan.
  • Home sale or transfer: Service ending before a billing period closes results in a final prorated invoice for remaining days.

How the Amount Is Calculated

The formula is straightforward:

Prorated Amount = (Monthly Plan Rate ÷ 30) × Number of Active Days

For example, if your Brightline Plus plan is $24.99/month and you activated on the 11th of a 30-day cycle, you are billed for 20 days: ($24.99 ÷ 30) × 20 = $16.66.

Where to Find the Breakdown

Open the Brightline Home app, tap Account → Billing → Invoice History, and select the invoice in question. Each prorated line item shows the start date, end date, daily rate, and day count.

If you believe the dates shown are incorrect, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 within 30 days of the invoice date. For context on how charges are handled during a home sale, see Who is responsible for the solar system during the home sale closing period?

articles.title: How are prorated charges handled when I change my billing date?
articles.summary: Changing your monthly billing date creates a one-time short or extended billing cycle with a prorated charge or credit to bridge the gap.
articles.question: I want to move my billing date from the 15th to the 1st of each month so it lines up with my other bills. Will I get charged twice in one month, or will something else happen to my invoice?
articles.answer:
What Happens When You Change Your Billing Date

Brightline Solar allows one billing-date change every 12 months at no fee. When you submit the change, our system closes your current billing cycle early and opens a new cycle that ends on your chosen date going forward. This creates a single transition invoice that covers the days between your old cycle-end and your new cycle-start.

Two Possible Transition Scenarios

ScenarioTransition PeriodResult
Moving billing date earlier (e.g., 15th → 1st)Less than 30 daysShort-cycle prorated charge for those days
Moving billing date later (e.g., 1st → 15th)More than 30 daysExtended-cycle invoice; net amount is still prorated per day, so you pay more once but less often initially

Example: Moving from the 15th to the 1st

Suppose your plan is $29.99/month and today is June 15. Your next normal invoice would have been July 15. Instead, we close the cycle on July 1—a 16-day period: ($29.99 ÷ 30) × 16 = $15.99. From August 1 onward, you receive standard full-month invoices on the 1st.

How to Request a Billing Date Change

  1. Open Brightline Home and navigate to Account → Billing → Billing Preferences.
  2. Tap Change Billing Date and select your preferred date (available options: 1st, 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, or 25th).
  3. Review the transition invoice preview and tap Confirm.

The transition invoice is issued within 2 business days and is due 21 days after issuance. If you are enrolled in the Brightline Hardship Program and a billing-date change would create a hardship, contact support before confirming—see Hardship Program Expansion: Extended Deferral (January 2026) for deferral options. For general information on refund timing if a credit results from your transition, see Refund Processing Time Update (Payments 2025).

articles.title: What line items will I see on my invoice when a prorated charge is applied?
articles.summary: Explains every line item that appears on a Brightline invoice containing a prorated charge, including how to read the dates, daily rates, and totals.
articles.question: My invoice looks different this month and shows several unfamiliar line items. How do I read an invoice that includes a prorated charge?
articles.answer:
How Brightline breaks down a prorated invoice

When a prorated charge appears, your invoice splits the billing period into two or more partial-period segments. Each segment has its own line item so you can see exactly what you are being charged for and why.

Typical line items you will see

Line Item LabelWhat It Means
Monitoring Plan — ProratedThe daily rate for your plan multiplied by the number of days in that segment.
Daily RateYour monthly plan fee divided by the number of days in that calendar month. For example, a $24.90/month plan in a 30-day month has a daily rate of $0.83.
Segment DatesThe exact start and end dates covered by that line item, shown as MM/DD/YYYY–MM/DD/YYYY.
Previous Plan CreditA negative amount refunding unused days from a plan you downgraded or cancelled mid-cycle.
New Plan ChargeThe charge for the remaining days under your new plan or rate.

Where to find this detail in Brightline Home

  1. Open the app and tap Account → Billing → Invoice History.
