  2. Select the invoice in question.
  3. Tap View Full Breakdown to expand all line items and segment dates.

If any amount still looks incorrect after reviewing the breakdown, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 or start a chat in the app within 90 days of the invoice date to request a review.

For background on why a prorated charge was generated in the first place, see Why did I receive a prorated charge on my invoice? If you changed your billing date and want to understand how that affects proration, see How are prorated charges handled when I change my billing date?

articles.title: Can I get a refund or credit if I was billed a prorated charge by mistake?
articles.summary: Describes the conditions under which Brightline will reverse or credit an incorrect prorated charge, the dispute process, and typical resolution timeframes.
articles.question: I believe the prorated charge on my invoice is wrong. Am I eligible for a refund or a bill credit, and how do I request one?
articles.answer:
When a prorated charge can be reversed

Brightline will issue a correction if the prorated charge resulted from any of the following:

  • A plan change or billing-date update that was processed on the wrong date due to a system error.
  • A duplicate charge for the same billing segment.
  • An incorrect daily rate caused by a pricing configuration error on Brightline's side.
  • A service interruption of 48 hours or more that was not excluded from billing under your service agreement.

How to open a dispute

  1. In Brightline Home, go to Account → Billing → Invoice History and open the affected invoice.
  2. Tap Dispute This Charge and select the specific line item you believe is incorrect.
  3. Provide a brief description and, if available, attach a screenshot or note the date you made the plan change.
  4. Submit the form. You will receive a confirmation email with a case number (format: BL-INV-XXXXXXX) within 15 minutes.

What happens next

Brightline's billing team reviews disputes within 5–7 business days. If the charge is confirmed incorrect, you will receive either:

  • A bill credit applied to your next invoice (most common), or
  • A direct refund to your original payment method within 7–10 business days, if your account balance is zero.

Disputes must be submitted within 90 days of the invoice date; charges older than 90 days cannot be reviewed except in cases of documented system error.

For general refund timing details, see Refund processing time update. To understand refund eligibility rules more broadly, see Refund eligibility policy clarification.

articles.title: How do I dispute a charge on my Brightline invoice?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to submitting a formal invoice dispute through the Brightline Home app or by phone, including timelines and what to expect.
articles.question: I noticed a charge on my invoice that doesn't look right. How do I officially dispute it and what happens after I submit?
articles.answer:
How to Submit an Invoice Dispute

If a line item on your invoice looks incorrect, you can open a formal dispute within 60 days of the invoice date. Disputes submitted after this window may not be eligible for review.

Option 1: Dispute via Brightline Home App

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Billing in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select the invoice you want to dispute, then tap View Invoice Details.
  3. Tap the Dispute a Charge button (flag icon) next to the line item in question.
  4. Choose a dispute reason from the dropdown (e.g., Charge not recognized, Incorrect amount, Already paid, or Other).
  5. Add any supporting notes, then tap Submit Dispute. You will receive a confirmation email with a dispute reference number (format: DSP-XXXXXXXX).

Option 2: Call Customer Support

Call 1-800-555-0192 (Mon–Fri, 7 a.m.–7 p.m. local time) and have your account number and invoice number ready. An agent will log the dispute on your behalf.

What Happens Next?

  • Our billing team reviews disputes within 10 business days.
  • You will receive an email update at each stage: Under Review, Decision Pending, and Resolved.
  • If the dispute is upheld, a credit or refund will be applied within 5–7 business days of resolution.
  • Your account will not be sent to collections for the disputed amount while the case is open.

If your dispute involves a prorated charge you believe was calculated incorrectly, see Can I get a refund or credit for a prorated charge I was billed incorrectly?

articles.title: What happens if my invoice dispute is denied?
articles.summary: Explains why a dispute may be denied, how to appeal the decision, and alternative options like hardship assistance if you cannot pay the disputed amount.
articles.question: Brightline denied my invoice dispute. What are my options now, and can I escalate the decision?
articles.answer:
Understanding a Denied Dispute

If your dispute is denied, you will receive an email with the subject line Dispute Decision: DSP-XXXXXXXX – Not Upheld. The email includes a plain-language explanation and the specific reason code assigned by our billing team. Common denial reason codes include:

CodeMeaning
DR-01Charge validated against your signed service agreement
DR-02Dispute submitted outside the 60-day window
DR-03Duplicate dispute already resolved
DR-04Insufficient supporting documentation

How to Appeal

  1. Reply directly to the denial email within 30 days and include any additional documentation (bank statements, prior correspondence, photos of equipment readings, etc.).
  2. Request escalation to a Senior Billing Specialist. Appeals are reviewed within 15 business days.
  3. If the appeal is also denied, you may request a final review by the Brightline Billing Oversight Team by calling 1-800-555-0192 and selecting option 4.

If You Cannot Pay While Awaiting Appeal

A denied dispute does not automatically trigger a late fee while an active appeal is on file. However, if the appeal is ultimately unsuccessful, standard late fees (1.5% per month) will be applied retroactively to the original due date. If paying the charge would create financial hardship, you may qualify for a payment deferral — see Brightline Hardship Program for eligibility details. For information on how refunds are processed once a dispute is upheld, see Refund Processing Time Update.

articles.title: How long does Brightline take to resolve an invoice dispute?
articles.summary: Explains the typical timeline for invoice dispute resolution, what happens at each stage, and when to expect a final decision or credit.
articles.question: I submitted an invoice dispute — how long will it take to get a response, and what's happening behind the scenes while I wait?
articles.answer:
Dispute Resolution Timeline

Once you submit a dispute through Brightline Home → Billing → Invoice History → [Invoice] → Dispute This Charge, our billing team begins review within 2 business days. The full process has three stages:

  1. Acknowledgment (within 2 business days): You'll receive an email and an in-app notification confirming your dispute reference number (format: DSP-XXXXXXXX).
  2. Active Review (up to 10 business days): A billing specialist examines your usage data, payment history, and any supporting documents you uploaded. If additional information is needed, they'll contact you via the email on your account — responding promptly keeps the clock from pausing.
  3. Decision (by business day 12): You'll be notified of the outcome in-app and by email. If the dispute is resolved in your favor, a credit or refund is applied within 5–7 business days.

While Your Dispute Is Open

The disputed amount is placed in a temporary hold status. Autopay will not process the held amount until the dispute closes, so you won't be charged twice. However, undisputed line items on the same invoice remain due on their original due date to avoid a late fee of $4.95.

Escalating a Delayed Dispute

If you haven't received a decision by business day 13, contact us at 1-800-BRIGHTLN or chat in the app with your DSP- reference number ready. For context on refund timing after a dispute is resolved in your favor, see Refund Processing Time Update. If you're concerned a dispute may be denied, review What Happens If My Invoice Dispute Is Denied.

articles.title: What documents should I submit when disputing a Brightline invoice charge?
articles.summary: Lists the supporting documents that strengthen an invoice dispute and explains how to upload them in Brightline Home for faster resolution.
articles.question: I want to dispute a charge on my invoice, but I'm not sure what evidence or documents I need to include. What should I attach to my dispute to give it the best chance of being resolved in my favor?
articles.answer:
Why Documentation Matters

Providing clear evidence upfront allows our billing specialists to resolve disputes faster — often within 5 business days instead of the standard 12. Disputes submitted without supporting documents are still accepted but typically take longer.

Recommended Documents by Dispute Type

Dispute ReasonSuggested Documents
Charge amount doesn't match my planYour signed service agreement, original quote PDF
Payment already madeBank or credit card statement showing the debit, payment confirmation email
Prorated charge seems incorrectScreenshot of your billing date change confirmation in-app
Equipment-related billing errorPhotos of system status screen, microinverter offline alerts
Credit or refund not appliedPrior dispute resolution email, credit confirmation notice

How to Upload Documents

  1. In Brightline Home, go to Billing → Invoice History.
  2. Select the invoice and tap Dispute This Charge.
  3. On the dispute form, tap Add Supporting Files. Accepted formats: PDF, JPG, PNG (max 10 MB each, up to 5 files).
  4. Add a brief description in the Notes field explaining what each file shows.
  5. Tap Submit Dispute to finalize.

After You Submit

You'll receive a dispute reference number (DSP-XXXXXXXX) by email. If your dispute involves a prorated charge, also review Can I Get a Refund or Credit for a Prorated Charge I Was Billed Incorrectly. For refund eligibility rules that apply once a dispute is resolved, see Refund Eligibility Policy Clarification.

articles.title: Updated Failed Payment Retry Schedule Now in Effect
articles.summary: Brightline Solar has revised its automatic retry schedule for failed payments, giving customers more time to resolve issues before a late fee is applied.
articles.abstract: Effective November 1, 2025, Brightline Solar updated the automatic retry cadence for failed monthly solar payments. Customers whose payment method is declined will now receive earlier email and in-app notifications, and the system will attempt up to four retries over a 14-day window before a $15 late fee is assessed and the account is flagged for review.
articles.body:
Effective date: November 1, 2025

When a scheduled payment fails, Brightline's billing system generates error code PAY-4010 and immediately queues the account for the updated retry sequence below.

  • Day 0: Initial charge attempt fails; email and push notification sent.
  • Day 2: First automatic retry.
  • Day 5: Second automatic retry; in-app banner displayed in Brightline Home.
  • Day 9: Third automatic retry; SMS reminder sent.
  • Day 14: Fourth and final retry. If unsuccessful, a $15 late fee is added and the account enters manual review.

You can update your payment method at any time by opening Brightline Home and navigating to Account → Billing → Payment Methods → Add or Replace. Updating before the Day 14 retry will clear the pending PAY-4010 flag automatically.

Customers experiencing financial hardship may qualify for payment deferral. See Brightline Hardship Program Launch 2025 for eligibility details.

No action is required if your payment succeeds on any retry attempt; the late fee will not be applied.

articles.title: Policy Clarification: Account Suspension Steps Following Repeated Failed Payments
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is clarifying the sequence of account actions that occur when a customer account accumulates multiple consecutive failed payments.
articles.abstract: Beginning February 15, 2026, Brightline Solar formalized its escalation policy for accounts with two or more consecutive billing cycles ending in failed payments, outlining exactly when monitoring data access is restricted, when remote battery control is suspended, and what customers must do to restore full account standing.
articles.body:
Effective date: February 15, 2026

Accounts that reach the end of the 14-day retry window (PAY-4010) for a second consecutive billing cycle will enter the following escalation path:

StageTriggerAccount Impact
Stage 12nd consecutive failed cycleRead-only mode in Brightline Home; battery scheduling disabled.
Stage 230 days after Stage 1 with no paymentProduction monitoring access suspended; error ACC-5030 displayed.
Stage 360 days after Stage 1 with no paymentAccount sent to collections; reinstatement fee of $75 required.

To restore account standing at any stage, navigate in Brightline Home to Account → Billing → Resolve Balance and complete payment of all overdue amounts plus any assessed fees.

Customers who believe a suspension was applied in error should first confirm their payment history, then open a billing dispute through Account → Billing → Dispute a Charge. For full dispute guidance, see How Do I Dispute a Charge on My Brightline Invoice.

Hardship deferral requests must be submitted before Stage 2 to remain eligible.

articles.title: Check Payments Now Take Up to 14 Business Days to Post — What You Need to Know
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is extending the check payment processing window from 7 to 14 business days effective March 1, 2026, due to increased mail volume and updated banking procedures.
articles.abstract: Starting March 1, 2026, checks mailed to Brightline Solar's payment processing center will take up to 14 business days to post to your account — double the previous 7-business-day window. Customers who pay by check should mail payments at least 16 business days before their due date to avoid late fees. This change affects all residential customers on paper-check billing plans.
articles.body:
Effective March 1, 2026, Brightline Solar's payment processing center in Phoenix, AZ is updating its check handling procedures to comply with new banking partner requirements. As a result, mailed check payments will take up to 14 business days to post to your Brightline account — up from the previous 7-business-day window.

Key Dates and Guidance

  • Mail your check at least 16 business days before your due date to ensure on-time posting.
  • Checks must be made payable to Brightline Solar LLC.
  • Include your 10-digit account number (found in Brightline Home under Account > Billing > Account Details) in the memo line.
  • Send checks to: Brightline Solar Payments, PO Box 48210, Phoenix, AZ 85072.

Late Fee Policy

Days Past DueLate Fee
1–10$10.00 flat
11–30$25.00 flat
31+1.5% of balance

If your account is flagged for non-payment, please review our failed payment and account suspension policy for details on how to restore service. Customers experiencing financial hardship may also qualify for deferred payment options through the Brightline Hardship Program.

articles.title: Important: Brightline Solar Check Payment Mailing Address Changing April 15, 2026
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is consolidating its payment processing operations and updating the mailing address for check payments, effective April 15, 2026 — checks sent to the old address after that date will be returned.
articles.abstract: On April 15, 2026, Brightline Solar will migrate all check payment processing to a new centralized facility in Dallas, TX. Any check mailed to the previous Phoenix address after April 14, 2026 will be returned to the sender unprocessed, which may result in a late payment on your account. Customers who pay by check must update their records — including any bill-pay services set up through their bank — before the cutover date.
articles.body:
Brightline Solar is consolidating payment operations to improve processing speed and reliability. Beginning April 15, 2026, all check payments must be mailed to the new address below. Checks directed to the old Phoenix address after April 14 will be returned unprocessed.

Address Change Summary

Old Address (valid through April 14, 2026)New Address (required from April 15, 2026)
PayeeBrightline Solar LLCBrightline Solar LLC
PO BoxPO Box 48210PO Box 91430

Action Steps for Check-Paying Customers

  • Update your personal checkbook records immediately.
  • Log in to your bank's bill-pay portal and update the Brightline payee address before April 14.
  • Include your 10-digit Brightline account number in the check memo line to prevent processing delays.
  • Allow up to 14 business days for checks to post under our current processing window.

If a returned check causes a missed payment on your account, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0193 within 5 business days of the returned-check date to request a late-fee waiver. For details on how missed payments are handled, see our failed payment retry schedule update. Customers facing financial difficulty may also inquire about the Brightline Hardship Program for temporary relief options.

articles.title: How do I get a receipt for a payment I made to Brightline?
articles.summary: Explains how customers can view, download, and resend payment receipts from within the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: I made a payment on my Brightline account and need a receipt for my records. How do I find or download it?
articles.answer:
Where to Find Your Payment Receipts

Every payment processed on your Brightline account automatically generates a receipt, which is stored in the Brightline Home app and emailed to your account address within 15 minutes of the payment clearing.

Viewing Receipts in the App

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Billing & Payments, then tap Payment History.
  3. Locate the payment you need and tap it to open the detail view.
  4. Tap Download Receipt (PDF) to save a copy to your device, or tap Email Receipt to resend it to your address on file.

Resending a Receipt by Email

If you did not receive the original receipt email, check your spam folder first. If it is not there, use the Email Receipt option described above. The email will arrive from receipts@mail.brightlinesolar.com within 5 minutes.

Receipts for Check Payments

Mailed check payments take additional time to post. A receipt will appear in Payment History within 5–7 business days of Brightline receiving your check. See check payment processing time for details on posting timelines.

Receipt Not Appearing?

If a receipt is missing after the expected window, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 or use in-app chat. Have your payment confirmation number ready (format: PAY-XXXXXXXX).

articles.title: Why does my payment receipt show a different amount than I expected?
articles.summary: Explains common reasons a payment receipt total may differ from the expected amount, including prorated charges, partial credits, and processing fees.
articles.question: I got a receipt for my Brightline payment but the total is not what I thought I was paying. Why is the amount different, and what should I do?
articles.answer:
Common Reasons for an Unexpected Receipt Amount

Several factors can cause the amount on your receipt to differ from your expected payment. The most frequent reasons are listed below.

ReasonWhat to Look For
Prorated charge appliedLine item labeled Prorated Adjustment on your invoice
Outstanding balance rolled overLine item labeled Previous Balance
Credit or discount appliedNegative line item labeled Account Credit
Returned payment fee ($25.00)Line item labeled Returned Payment Fee

Prorated Charges

If you recently changed your billing date or your service agreement start date falls mid-cycle, a prorated amount is added or subtracted automatically. See what line items appear on my invoice when I have a prorated charge for a detailed breakdown of how these appear on your receipt.

Credits Reducing Your Total

A loyalty credit, referral reward, or hardship program adjustment may reduce your receipt total below your standard monthly amount. Credits are displayed as negative values and are applied before the payment is processed.

If You Believe the Amount Is Incorrect

If none of the above explanations account for the discrepancy, you may have grounds to dispute the charge. Review how to dispute a charge on your Brightline invoice for step-by-step instructions. Contact Brightline Support with your receipt number (format: RCP-XXXXXXXX) and a brief description of the discrepancy.

articles.title: Can I get receipts emailed automatically for every Brightline payment?
articles.summary: Explains how to enable automatic email receipts for every payment processed through Brightline Home.
articles.question: I'd like to receive an email receipt every time Brightline processes a payment on my account. Is there a setting I can turn on so receipts are sent automatically instead of me having to look them up manually?
articles.answer:
Enabling Automatic Payment Receipts

Yes — Brightline Home can send you an email receipt automatically every time a payment is successfully processed, whether it's a scheduled autopay, a one-time manual payment, or a retry after a previously failed charge.

How to turn on automatic receipts

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Billing & Payments, then tap Notification Preferences.
  3. Under the Receipt Emails section, toggle Send receipt after every successful payment to On.
  4. Confirm the email address shown is correct. To change it, tap Edit Email and save.

What the receipt includes

  • Payment confirmation number (format: BL-RCT-XXXXXXXX)
  • Payment date, amount, and method (e.g., ACH, credit card ending in ····4821)
  • Invoice number(s) the payment was applied to
  • Your account balance after the payment

Receipt delivery timing

Receipts are generated and emailed within 5 minutes of a successful payment. If a payment is settled overnight (common for ACH), the receipt arrives by 6:00 AM local time the following business day.

If you're not receiving receipts even with the toggle enabled, check your spam folder for emails from receipts@mail.brightlinesolar.com, then verify your notification settings are saved. For details on what to do if a receipt shows an unexpected amount, see Why does my payment receipt show a different amount than I expected?

articles.title: How do I download or reprint a past payment receipt in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Describes how to locate, download as a PDF, and reprint any historical payment receipt from within the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: I need a copy of a receipt for a payment I made a few months ago — my accountant needs it for tax purposes. How do I find and download an old receipt from my Brightline account?
articles.answer:
Finding and Downloading Past Receipts

Brightline Home stores receipts for every successful payment for up to 7 years, and you can download a PDF copy at any time directly from the app or web portal.

Steps to locate a past receipt

  1. Log in to Brightline Home (app or browser at home.brightlinesolar.com).
  2. Navigate to Account → Billing & Payments → Payment History.
  3. Use the date range filter to narrow results, or enter a payment confirmation number (e.g., BL-RCT-XXXXXXXX) in the search bar.
  4. Tap the payment row to open the detail view.
  5. Tap Download Receipt (PDF). The file will save to your device or open in a new browser tab.

Receipt PDF contents

FieldExample
Confirmation numberBL-RCT-00482931

If a receipt is missing

Receipts only exist for successful payments. If a payment failed or is still pending, no receipt will appear. You can also request a receipt be re-sent to your email by tapping Resend Receipt on the detail view — delivery takes up to 10 minutes.

For guidance on how to get receipts sent to you automatically going forward, see How do I get a receipt for my Brightline payment?

articles.title: Can I make a partial payment on my Brightline invoice?
articles.summary: Explains whether partial payments are accepted, how to submit one in the Brightline Home app, and what happens to the remaining balance.
articles.question: I can't pay my full invoice amount right now. Can I pay part of it, and will that stop a late fee or service interruption?
articles.answer:
Partial Payments Are Accepted

Yes, Brightline Solar does accept partial payments on outstanding invoices. You can submit any amount greater than $10.00 toward a balance due without the payment being rejected. However, a partial payment does not satisfy the invoice in full, and the remaining balance will continue to accrue a 1.5% monthly late fee (applied on the 10th calendar day after the original due date) until the balance is cleared.

How to Submit a Partial Payment in Brightline Home

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Billing in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select the invoice you want to pay, then tap Make a Payment.
  3. On the payment screen, tap Enter a custom amount and type the amount you wish to pay.
  4. Choose your payment method and tap Submit Payment.

You will receive an email and in-app receipt within 15 minutes confirming the amount applied. The invoice detail screen will update to show the new remaining balance, marked as Partially Paid.

Will a Partial Payment Prevent Account Suspension?

A partial payment reduces your balance but does not automatically pause suspension proceedings. If your account is already in a past-due state, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 or chat in-app to set up a payment arrangement. Customers facing financial hardship may also qualify for deferred billing through our assistance program.

See also: Brightline Hardship Program and Account Suspension Policy.

articles.title: How does Brightline apply a partial payment when I have multiple invoices or fees?
articles.summary: Describes the order in which Brightline applies partial payments across fees, past-due invoices, and current charges, and how to view the allocation in the app.
articles.question: I made a partial payment, but I'm not sure which invoice or fee it was applied to. How does Brightline decide where to put the money when I owe amounts on more than one invoice?
articles.answer:
Payment Application Order

When a partial payment is received, Brightline applies funds in the following fixed priority order:

  1. Outstanding late fees – any assessed 1.5% monthly late fees are cleared first.
  2. Oldest past-due invoice balance – the invoice with the earliest original due date is paid down next.
  3. Subsequent past-due invoices – additional aged balances are paid in chronological order.
  4. Current (not yet due) invoice balance – any remaining funds are applied last.

This order is automatic and cannot be manually overridden at this time. If you need a specific allocation, you must pay each invoice individually using the custom amount field on the per-invoice payment screen (Billing → [Invoice] → Make a Payment → Enter a custom amount).

Viewing Payment Allocation

To see exactly how your payment was distributed:

  • Go to Billing → Payment History.
  • Tap the payment entry to expand the Allocation Breakdown panel, which lists each invoice or fee credited and the exact dollar amount applied.

This breakdown is also included in the emailed receipt sent within 15 minutes of payment processing.

Disputing an Unexpected Allocation

If a payment was applied in a way that seems incorrect—for example, to a fee you believe was already waived—you can open a billing dispute in-app under Billing → Help → Dispute a Charge. Resolutions are typically issued within 5 business days.

See also: How to Dispute a Charge and How to Get a Payment Receipt.

articles.title: What happens if I only pay part of my Brightline invoice?
articles.summary: Explains the consequences of submitting a partial payment, including how the remaining balance is tracked and what late fees or service impacts may apply.
articles.question: I can only afford to pay part of my invoice this month. What will happen to the rest of my balance, and will I be charged any fees?
articles.answer:
What Counts as a Partial Payment

A partial payment is any amount less than the full Statement Balance shown on your current invoice. Brightline Home accepts partial payments through the app, but your account will reflect an outstanding balance equal to the unpaid portion.

How the Remaining Balance Is Handled

The unpaid amount is carried forward to your next billing cycle and appears as a Previous Balance line item on your following invoice. You will not be charged a separate balance-transfer fee for this rollover.

Late Fees and Service Impacts

If your partial payment is received by the due date, the late-payment fee of $9.95 is waived for that cycle. However, if the total outstanding balance (current charges plus carried-over balance) remains unpaid past 30 days after the original due date, the $9.95 late fee is applied automatically. Repeated partial payments over three or more consecutive cycles may trigger an account review under Brightline's collections policy.

Monitoring Your Balance in Brightline Home

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Billing in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Account Summary to see your current balance, any carried-forward amount, and the next due date.
  3. Tap Make a Payment to submit an additional payment at any time before your next statement closes.

Financial Hardship Options

If partial payments are becoming a recurring necessity, you may qualify for the Brightline Hardship Program, which offers deferred payments and reduced minimums. See Brightline Hardship Program for eligibility details.

For questions about how failed or incomplete payments are retried, see Failed Payment Retry Schedule.

articles.title: How do I make a partial payment in Brightline Home, and which charges get paid first?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to submitting a partial payment through the Brightline Home app and an explanation of the payment-application order Brightline uses when the amount paid is less than the full balance.
articles.question: I want to pay a specific dollar amount that is less than my full invoice total. How do I enter a custom payment amount in the app, and how does Brightline decide which charges to pay down first?
articles.answer:
Entering a Custom Payment Amount

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Billing in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap Make a Payment, then select your preferred payment method (bank account, debit card, or credit card).
  3. On the amount screen, tap Enter Custom Amount instead of using the pre-filled statement balance.
  4. Type your desired payment amount — the minimum accepted partial payment is $10.00.
  5. Review the summary screen and tap Confirm Payment. You will receive an email and in-app confirmation within a few minutes.

Payment-Application Order

When a partial payment is received, Brightline applies funds in the following priority order:

PriorityCharge Type
1Outstanding late fees
2Previous-cycle carried-forward balance
3Current monitoring and service plan charges
4Current energy or lease charges

This order ensures that the oldest and highest-priority obligations are cleared first, reducing the risk of additional fees accruing.

Confirming How Your Payment Was Applied

After your payment posts (typically within 1–2 business days), go to Billing > Payment History and tap the transaction to see a breakdown showing exactly how each dollar was allocated.

If you believe a partial payment was applied incorrectly, see How Do I Dispute a Charge on My Brightline Invoice. If you are facing ongoing financial difficulty, learn about deferred-payment options at Hardship Program Expansion: Extended Deferral.

articles.title: How do I view or download my loan statement in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Explains where to find, view, and download monthly loan statements inside the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: Where can I find my loan statement in the Brightline Home app, and how do I download a copy for my records?
articles.answer:
Accessing Your Loan Statement

Your monthly loan statement is available in the Brightline Home app within 24–48 hours after your statement period closes. To find it, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Financing, then tap Loan Statements.
  3. You will see a list of statements sorted by date, labeled with the statement period (e.g., May 1 – May 31, 2026).
  4. Tap any statement to open a detailed view, or tap the Download PDF button to save a copy to your device.

What Is Included in a Statement

Each loan statement contains the following information:

  • Opening balance – the amount owed at the start of the period
  • Payments received – all payments applied during the statement period, including partial payments
  • Interest accrued – interest charged under your loan agreement (typically at your fixed APR)
  • Fees assessed – any late fees (standard fee: $15.00) or returned payment fees ($25.00)
  • Closing balance – your remaining principal balance
  • Next payment due date and amount

Statement Delivery by Email

If you prefer to receive statements by email automatically each month, go to Account > Notification Preferences > Financing and enable Monthly Loan Statement Email. Statements are sent as PDF attachments to your address on file.

If you cannot access the app, see How do I log in to Brightline Home if I cannot receive SMS codes? for login help. For questions about specific charges on your statement, see How do I dispute a charge on my Brightline invoice?

articles.title: Why does my loan statement balance not match what I expected?
articles.summary: Explains common reasons a loan statement balance may differ from a customer's expectations, including interest timing, partial payments, and fees.
articles.question: My loan statement shows a balance that is higher or lower than I thought it would be. Why might that be, and what should I do?
articles.answer:
Common Reasons for an Unexpected Balance

Several factors can cause your closing balance to differ from what you anticipated. The most frequent reasons are listed below.

1. Interest Accrues Daily

Brightline Solar loans use simple daily interest. This means interest accumulates each day based on your current principal. If your payment arrived even a few days late, additional interest will have accrued before your payment was applied, leaving a slightly higher balance than expected.

2. Payment Application Order

Payments are applied in the following order: (1) outstanding fees, (2) accrued interest, (3) principal. If you carry a late fee or returned-payment fee from a prior period, your payment reduces those charges first, and less principal is paid down than you may have anticipated.

3. Partial Payments

If you made a partial payment in the previous period, the unpaid remainder rolled forward and continued to accrue interest. See How does Brightline apply partial payments to my account balance? for details on how this works.

4. Hardship Deferral Adjustments

If you enrolled in a payment deferral through the Brightline Hardship Program, deferred amounts and any associated interest adjustments will appear as separate line items on your statement. Refer to Hardship Program Expansion: Extended Deferral (January 2026) for program terms.

What to Do Next

SituationRecommended Action
Balance seems too highReview the interest accrued and fees lines; contact support at 1-800-555-0192 if a charge appears incorrect
Balance seems too lowConfirm all expected payments were processed; check Payment History in the app
Deferral not reflectedAllow up to 5 business days after deferral approval for the statement to update

If you believe there is an error, you can open a billing dispute directly in the app under Account > Financing > Loan Statements > [Statement] > Dispute a Charge.

articles.title: What information is included on my Brightline loan statement?
articles.summary: A breakdown of every section and line item you will find on your monthly Brightline Solar loan statement.
articles.question: I just received my loan statement and I'm not sure what all the different sections mean. Can you walk me through what's included?
articles.answer:
Sections of Your Brightline Loan Statement

Your monthly loan statement is generated on the first business day after your billing cycle closes and covers the prior calendar month. It is available in the Brightline Home app under Account → Financing → Loan Statements and is also emailed as a PDF to your address on file.

Statement Header

The header contains your Loan Account Number (format: BL-LN-XXXXXXXX), statement date, payment due date, and the name of the lending program (e.g., Brightline SunFlex 25-Year).

Account Summary Table

FieldDescription
Previous BalanceOutstanding principal + accrued interest at the start of the period
Payments ReceivedPayments posted during the statement period
Interest ChargedInterest accrued at your fixed APR for the period
Current BalanceTotal amount owed as of the statement date
Minimum Payment DueAmount required to avoid a late fee ($18.00 after a 10-day grace period)

Payment Activity Log

Every payment, credit, or adjustment posted during the period is listed with a date, reference number, and method (ACH, check, or card).

Interest Rate Disclosure

Your current fixed APR, the daily periodic rate, and the number of days in the billing cycle are disclosed in this section as required by federal lending regulations.

If your current balance does not look right, see Why does my loan statement balance not match what I expected? or review how to access your statement at How do I view or download my loan statement in Brightline Home?

articles.title: How do I set up automatic loan statement email delivery in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for enabling paperless statement delivery so your monthly loan statement is emailed to you automatically.
articles.question: I want to receive my loan statement by email every month instead of having to log in and find it. How do I turn that on?
articles.answer:
Enabling Paperless Loan Statement Delivery

By default, Brightline Home stores your statements in the app but does not automatically email them. You can enable automatic email delivery—sometimes called e-Statement enrollment—in a few steps.

Steps in the Brightline Home App

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Financing, then tap Statement Preferences.
  3. Under Delivery Method, switch the toggle from App Only to Email + App.
  4. Confirm or update the email address shown. You may add a second address (e.g., a co-borrower's email) by tapping + Add Recipient.
  5. Tap Save Preferences. You will receive a confirmation email within 15 minutes.

When Will the Change Take Effect?

Your preference update applies to the next statement cycle. If your current cycle closes within 48 hours of making the change, the very next statement may still be app-only; the one after that will be emailed.

Troubleshooting Delivery Issues

  • Check your spam or junk folder for messages from statements@mail.brightlinesolar.com.
  • If you are not receiving login emails either, review the steps at SMS verification code not arriving in Brightline Home as carrier filtering can sometimes affect other transactional emails too.
  • To download a past statement manually while you wait, follow the instructions in How do I view or download my loan statement in Brightline Home?

Opting Back Out

Return to Account → Financing → Statement Preferences and switch the toggle back to App Only at any time. There is no fee to change your delivery preference.

articles.body:
What Changed

articles.title: How do I change the display language in the Brightline Home app?
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions for switching the Brightline Home app interface to a different supported language.
articles.question: How do I change the language the Brightline Home app displays in? I'd like to switch from English to Spanish, but I can't find the setting.
articles.answer:
Supported Languages

Brightline Home currently supports the following display languages: English (US), Spanish (ES), French (FR), and Portuguese (BR). All app screens, alerts, billing summaries, and system status messages are fully translated in each language.

How to Change Your Language

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and sign in.
  2. Tap your profile avatar in the top-right corner of the dashboard.
  3. Select Account Settings from the dropdown menu.
  4. Tap Preferences, then tap Language & Region.
  5. Choose your preferred language from the list and tap Save.

The app will reload automatically within 2–3 seconds and display all content in the selected language. No reinstall is required.

Notes & Limitations

  • Language changes apply only to the app interface. Formal documents such as loan statements, invoices, and permit-related records are issued in English only.
  • Push notification language updates may take up to 15 minutes to take effect after saving.
  • If you do not see your preferred language in the list, it is not yet supported. You can submit a language request via Help & Support → Feature Request inside the app.

For help understanding alerts you may see in the app, see Temperature Warning Alerts Now Available in Brightline Home.

articles.title: Why did my Brightline Home app language reset to English after an update?
articles.summary: Explains why a language preference may revert to English after an app update and how to restore and lock your preferred setting.
articles.question: I had my Brightline Home app set to Spanish, but after a recent update it switched back to English on its own. Why does this keep happening and how do I stop it?
articles.answer:
Why This Happens

In rare cases, a major app version update (version increments such as 3.x → 4.x) can reset certain profile preferences, including language, to their defaults. This is a known issue tracked under internal reference BLH-PREF-412 and is most likely to occur when the update includes a full rebuild of the preferences data schema.

How to Restore Your Language Setting

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap your profile avatar in the top-right corner.
  2. Go to Account Settings → Preferences → Language & Region.
  3. Select your preferred language and tap Save.

Preventing Future Resets

To protect your preference across future updates, enable Cloud Preference Sync:

  • Navigate to Account Settings → Preferences → Sync & Backup.
  • Toggle Cloud Preference Sync to On.

With this setting enabled, your language choice is stored server-side and automatically reapplied after any app update within 60 seconds of first launch.

Still Experiencing Resets?

If the language reverts more than once after enabling Cloud Preference Sync, contact Brightline Support at 1-833-274-7652 or use Help & Support → Chat in the app. Have your account email and the app version number ready (found under Settings → About Brightline Home).

For related profile and billing preferences, see How Do I Set Up Automatic Loan Statement Email Delivery in Brightline Home.

articles.title: Which languages are supported in the Brightline Home app?
articles.summary: Lists all languages currently available in Brightline Home and explains where to find the language setting.
articles.question: What languages can I use in the Brightline Home app, and where do I go to change them?
articles.answer:
Supported Languages

Brightline Home currently supports the following languages:

  • English (US) – default
  • Spanish (Español)
  • French (Français)
  • Portuguese (Português – Brasil)
  • Vietnamese (Tiếng Việt)

Additional languages are evaluated each quarter based on customer demand. If your preferred language is not listed, you can submit a request through Help & Feedback → Feature Request inside the app.

Where to Change Your Language

To switch languages, open the app and navigate to Profile → App Preferences → Display Language. Select your preferred language from the list and tap Save. The app will reload automatically and apply the new language within a few seconds. No internet reconnection is required.

What Changes When You Switch Languages

Changing your display language affects:

  • All menus, buttons, and navigation labels

The following items are not affected by your language setting and will continue to appear in English:

  • Legal documents and terms of service
  • Invoice line-item descriptions
  • Partner API responses

For details on resetting after an unexpected language change, see Why did my Brightline Home language reset to English?

articles.title: Can I set a different language for my email notifications than the app display?
articles.summary: Explains how Brightline Home handles language settings separately for the app interface and outgoing email or SMS notifications.
articles.question: I changed my app language to Spanish, but my email notifications are still coming in English. Can I control the language for emails and texts separately from the app?
articles.answer:
App Language vs. Notification Language

Yes — Brightline Home keeps your app display language and your notification language as two independent settings. Changing one does not automatically change the other.

How to Set Your Notification Language

Follow these steps to update the language used for email and SMS notifications:

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to Profile → Notifications → Notification Preferences.
  2. Tap Notification Language at the top of the screen.
  3. Select your preferred language from the same list of six supported languages.
  4. Tap Save Changes.

Changes take effect for all notifications sent after you save. Notifications already queued (within the next 15 minutes) may still arrive in the previous language.

Which Notifications Are Affected
