If you want everything in the same language, set both Display Language and Notification Language to match. For more on temperature alert notifications specifically, see Temperature Warning Alerts Now Available in Brightline Home.

articles.title: Identify and Dismiss a False Alarm in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Learn how to recognize when an alert in the Brightline Home app is a false alarm and how to dismiss it without affecting your system's alert history.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You will need the Brightline Home app (version 4.2.0 or later) installed on your mobile device and an active internet connection. Only the account owner or an authorized household member with Alert permissions can dismiss alerts.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Alerts in the bottom navigation bar. Active alerts appear at the top under Needs Attention.
  2. Tap the alert you want to investigate. Review the alert detail screen, which shows the alert code (for example, ALT-204: Low Production Warning), the time it triggered, and the affected component.
  3. Tap Check System Status on the alert detail screen. The app polls your inverter and gateway in real time. If all readings return green within 60 seconds, the alert is likely a false alarm caused by a brief communication dropout or a transient grid fluctuation.
  4. Scroll down to the Possible Causes section. Look for entries labeled Transient — no action required. These are pre-classified false-alarm patterns based on your system's telemetry history.
  5. Tap Mark as False Alarm, then select a reason from the dropdown (options include Temporary shading, Grid momentary outage, App connectivity gap, or Other). Adding a brief note is optional but helps Brightline improve alert accuracy.
  6. Tap Confirm Dismiss. The alert moves to Alert History with a False Alarm label and is excluded from your monthly Alert Summary report.

Troubleshooting

The Mark as False Alarm button is grayed out. This occurs when an alert carries a Critical severity flag (code prefix ALT-5xx). Critical alerts cannot be self-dismissed; contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 so a technician can verify the issue before it is cleared.

The system status check times out. If the real-time poll does not complete within 90 seconds, your gateway may be offline. Check that your home Wi-Fi is active and that the Brightline gateway LED is solid blue. A flashing amber LED indicates the gateway is reconnecting; wait two minutes and retry. If the problem persists, see How to Track and Respond to Your Inspection Day Results in Brightline Home to log a follow-up service request.

You dismissed an alert by mistake. Go to Alerts > Alert History, find the entry, and tap Reopen Alert within 24 hours of dismissal to restore it to Needs Attention status.

articles.title: Configure False Alarm Suppression Rules in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Set up automatic suppression rules so Brightline Home stops generating repeated false alarms for known, recurring non-issue conditions on your system.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be the account owner with full Alert Management permissions. Suppression rules are available on Brightline Home app version 4.5.0 or later. Rules apply only to the site associated with your account; households with multiple sites must configure rules per site. Note that suppression rules cannot be applied to any alert with a Critical (ALT-5xx) or Safety (ALT-6xx) code.

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Settings (gear icon, top-right corner), then select Alerts & Notifications.
  2. Tap Suppression Rules, then tap Add New Rule.
  3. In the Alert Type field, search for or browse to the alert code you want to suppress — for example, ALT-204: Low Production Warning. Only alert codes that have been triggered at least once on your system appear in this list.
  4. Under Trigger Condition, define when the rule applies. Choose one or more conditions:
    • Time window — suppress the alert only between specified hours (for example, 07:00–09:00 to ignore early-morning shading alerts).
    • Duration threshold — suppress only if the alert clears automatically within a set number of minutes (2–30 minutes).
    • Repeat frequency — suppress if the same code fires more than a specified number of times within a rolling 7-day window.
  5. Set the Rule Expiry date. Rules must have an end date; the maximum is 180 days. You can renew a rule before it expires.
  6. Tap Save Rule. A confirmation banner appears: Suppression rule activated. Matching alerts will be logged silently under Alert History.
  7. To review suppressed alerts at any time, go to Alerts > Alert History and toggle the Show Suppressed filter to On.

Troubleshooting

The alert code I want to suppress is not listed. Suppression rules can only be created for alert codes your system has previously generated. If you are trying to prevent a future alert type, contact Brightline Support to discuss whether a system-wide sensitivity adjustment is appropriate for your installation.

Suppressed alerts are still sending push notifications. Suppression rules silence in-app alert cards but do not automatically disable push notifications configured under Settings > Notifications > Push Preferences. Disable the corresponding notification toggle there to stop push alerts for the suppressed code.

My rule expired and I need to renew it. Go to Settings > Alerts & Notifications > Suppression Rules, find the expired rule (marked with a gray Expired badge), and tap Renew to extend it by up to 180 additional days. If your system's production readings are frequently triggering low-production alerts, review Why Does My Production Estimate Differ from My Actual Output to determine whether an underlying production issue — rather than a false alarm — may be causing the alerts.

articles.title: How do I schedule a recurring production report in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to setting up automatic daily, weekly, or monthly production reports delivered by email or in-app notification through Brightline Home.
articles.question: I want to receive my production data automatically on a regular basis without logging in every time. How do I set up a recurring report schedule in the Brightline Home app?
articles.answer:
Setting Up a Recurring Report Schedule

Brightline Home lets you schedule automatic production reports so your data arrives on a cadence that works for you. Follow these steps to configure a recurring report:

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap the Reports tab in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap Schedule a Report in the upper-right corner.
  3. Under Report Type, choose one of the following: Daily Summary, Weekly Rollup, or Monthly Statement.
  4. Set your preferred Delivery Day & Time. Weekly reports default to Monday at 7:00 AM local time; monthly reports default to the 1st of the month.
  5. Under Delivery Method, select Email, In-App Notification, or Both.
  6. Optionally enable Include Weather Adjustments to add weather-corrected figures to each report (see Weather Adjustments Now Applied to Production Reports).
  7. Tap Save Schedule. You will see a confirmation banner: "Your report schedule has been saved and will begin on your next scheduled date."

Editing or Canceling a Schedule

To modify an existing schedule, go to Reports > My Schedules, tap the schedule you want to change, and select Edit or Delete Schedule. Changes take effect immediately and apply starting with the next scheduled delivery.

Limits & Notes

  • You may have up to 5 active report schedules per account.
  • Reports are generated using data finalized by 2:00 AM local time, so same-day data may be incomplete in Daily Summary reports delivered before that cutoff.
  • For lifetime production figures included in reports, see How to View Your Lifetime Production Stats in Brightline Home.

articles.title: How do I schedule automated report delivery using the Partner API?
articles.summary: Instructions for using the Partner API's report scheduling endpoints to configure recurring production report jobs, including request format, supported frequencies, and error handling.
articles.question: As a developer integrating with Brightline's Partner API, how can I programmatically schedule recurring production reports to be delivered to a webhook or pulled on a set interval?
articles.answer:
Overview

The Partner API exposes a /v2/reports/schedules resource that lets you create, update, list, and delete recurring report delivery jobs for one or more sites under your OAuth2 credentials.

Creating a Report Schedule

Send a POST request to /v2/reports/schedules with a JSON body. Required fields are shown in the table below:

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
site_idstringYesBrightline site identifier
frequencystringYesdaily, weekly, or monthly
delivery_methodstringYeswebhook or pull
webhook_urlstringIf webhookMust match a registered endpoint
include_weather_adjustedbooleanNoDefaults to false
start_dateISO 8601 dateNoDefaults to next occurrence

Response & IDs

A successful 201 Created response returns a schedule_id (e.g., rsch_8a3f2c) you should store for future updates or deletions. If the webhook_url is not yet registered, the API returns error code ERR_WEBHOOK_URL_UNREGISTERED (422).

Idempotency

Include an Idempotency-Key header on POST requests to prevent duplicate schedules if a request is retried. See What Is an Idempotency Key and Why Do I Need One? for details.

Weather-Adjusted Fields

When include_weather_adjusted is true, each delivered report includes the fields described in Weather Adjustment Fields Now Available — Partner API Reports Endpoint.

Rate Limits

You may create up to 50 active schedules per OAuth2 client. Exceeding this limit returns ERR_SCHEDULE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (429).

articles.title: Can I change or pause a scheduled report in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Explains how to edit, pause, or cancel an existing scheduled report from within the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: I set up a recurring report a few weeks ago, but I want to change the frequency or temporarily stop it from sending. Can I edit or pause my scheduled report without deleting it entirely?
articles.answer:
Managing Your Scheduled Reports

Yes — you can edit, pause, or delete any scheduled report at any time without losing your historical delivery records. Follow the steps below based on what you need to do.

How to Edit a Scheduled Report

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Reports in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select the Scheduled tab at the top of the Reports screen.
  3. Tap the report you want to change, then tap Edit Schedule.
  4. Update any combination of the following: delivery frequency (Daily, Weekly, Monthly), report type (Production, Savings, Battery, or Combined), recipient email addresses, and preferred delivery time (in your local timezone).
  5. Tap Save Changes. The updated schedule takes effect on the next scheduled run.

How to Pause a Scheduled Report

If you want to stop deliveries temporarily without deleting the schedule, toggle the Active switch to Off on the report detail screen. A paused report retains all its settings. To resume, toggle the switch back to On — delivery will resume at the next scheduled interval.

How to Delete a Scheduled Report

Tap Edit Schedule, then scroll to the bottom and tap Delete Schedule. Confirm the deletion in the dialog that appears. This action is permanent and cannot be undone, though past delivered reports remain accessible under Reports > History.

For guidance on first creating a scheduled report, see How do I schedule a recurring production report in Brightline Home?. If your reports include weather-adjusted figures, see Weather Adjustments Now Applied to Production Reports for details on what those numbers mean.

articles.title: Why did my scheduled report stop arriving or arrive late?
articles.summary: Covers the most common reasons a scheduled report is missing or delayed and how to fix each one.
articles.question: My weekly production report used to show up every Monday morning, but I haven't received it in two weeks. Sometimes it shows up a day late. What's going on and how do I fix it?
articles.answer:
Why Scheduled Reports Can Stop or Be Delayed

There are several common reasons a scheduled report may fail to arrive or arrive late. Work through the checks below to identify and resolve the issue.

1. The Report Was Accidentally Paused

Open Brightline Home > Reports > Scheduled and confirm the Active toggle is set to On for your report. A paused report will show a Paused badge in gray.

2. Email Address Changed or Recipient Inbox Is Full

If the destination address recently changed (for example, after an account email update) the scheduled report may be sending to your old address. Tap Edit Schedule on the affected report and verify all recipient addresses are correct.

3. Report Landed in Spam or Promotions

Check your spam, promotions, or junk folder for emails from reports@mail.brightlinesolar.com. Adding that address to your contacts prevents future filtering.

4. Temporary Delivery Delay

During periods of high platform load, scheduled reports may be queued and delivered up to 4 hours after their scheduled time. If your report arrived late but eventually appeared, no action is needed.

5. Data Sync Error (Error Code RPT-4402)

If your monitoring gateway lost connectivity during the reporting window, the system may skip that delivery and log error code RPT-4402. You will receive an in-app alert under Alerts > System. The next scheduled report will generate normally once connectivity is restored.

Still Not Receiving Reports?

Contact Brightline Support via Brightline Home > Help > Chat with Us and include your report name and the date of the last successful delivery. For information on lifetime stats you can review manually in the meantime, see How to View Your Lifetime Production Stats in Brightline Home. If you manage reports via the API, see How to Schedule Automated Report Delivery via the Partner API.

articles.title: Why was my installation appointment delayed due to weather?
articles.summary: Explains why Brightline Solar postpones installation appointments during unsafe weather conditions and what customers can expect next.
articles.question: I had an installation scheduled but received a notification that it was delayed because of weather. Why does Brightline cancel for weather, and how long will I have to wait?
articles.answer:
Why Weather Delays Happen

Brightline Solar crews work at height on rooftops and with high-voltage electrical components. To protect both our technicians and your property, we follow strict safety thresholds. An appointment will be automatically postponed if any of the following conditions are forecast or active within a 4-hour window around your scheduled start time:

  • Sustained winds above 25 mph or gusts above 35 mph
  • Active precipitation (rain, sleet, hail, or snow)
  • Lightning within a 10-mile radius
  • Temperatures below 20 °F or heat index above 105 °F

How You Are Notified

When a weather delay is triggered, you will receive a push notification through the Brightline Home app and an email to your account address no later than 5:00 AM local time on the day of your appointment. The notification will include a new proposed date, typically within 5–10 business days, depending on crew availability in your region.

What Happens Next

Your rescheduled date is confirmed automatically—no action is required on your part unless the new time does not work for you. To request a different date, open the app and navigate to My Projects > Appointments > Reschedule. There is no rescheduling fee for weather-related delays. For tips on getting your home ready once the new date is set, see How to Prepare Your Home for Inspection Day.

articles.title: How do I check the status of a weather-delayed appointment in Brightline Home?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to finding your rescheduled appointment date and enabling weather-delay notifications in the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: My appointment was pushed back because of weather. Where can I see my new date in the Brightline Home app, and how do I make sure I get notified if it changes again?
articles.answer:
Finding Your Updated Appointment

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap My Projects in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select the relevant project card (e.g., System Installation or Service Visit).
  3. Tap Appointments. Weather-delayed visits display a yellow Weather Hold badge alongside the new proposed date and a countdown timer.
  4. Tap the appointment row to see the full detail view, including the weather condition that triggered the delay and the crew's estimated arrival window.

Enabling Weather-Delay Alerts

To ensure you receive immediate notifications for any future changes:

  1. Go to Settings > Notifications > Scheduling Alerts.
  2. Toggle Weather Delay Updates to On.
  3. Choose your preferred channel: Push, Email, or Both.

If Your New Date Does Not Work

Tap Reschedule on the appointment detail screen to choose an available slot. Reschedules caused by weather carry no fee, and your place in the installation queue is preserved. If you need to grant a crew member access to your roof for the rescheduled visit, review How to Grant Roof Access for a Scheduled Service Visit. You can also revisit original scheduling steps at How to Reschedule or Cancel Your Site Survey.

Still Not Seeing an Updated Date?

If your appointment still shows Weather Hold with no new date after 48 hours, contact Brightline Support via the in-app chat or call 1-800-555-0174.

articles.title: How long will a weather delay postpone my installation appointment?
articles.summary: Explains typical rescheduling timeframes after a weather-related installation delay and what factors affect how soon Brightline can get back on your calendar.
articles.question: My installation was postponed because of weather. How long will I have to wait before it gets rescheduled, and what affects that timeline?
articles.answer:
Typical Rescheduling Timeframes

When Brightline Solar postpones an installation due to unsafe weather conditions—such as high winds (sustained speeds above 25 mph), active precipitation, or lightning within 10 miles of the job site—our scheduling team begins rebooking affected appointments within 1 business day of the original date. In most cases, your new appointment will fall within 5–14 calendar days of the cancelled visit, depending on crew availability and local permit validity.

Factors That Can Extend the Wait

  • Regional weather patterns: Prolonged storm systems (e.g., multi-day rain events) may push your slot further out if multiple crews are affected simultaneously.
  • Permit expiration windows: If your installation permit expires within 30 days of the delay, a Brightline permit coordinator will contact you separately to discuss extension options before rescheduling.
  • Roof-access requirements: Delays may be longer if your property requires a scheduled access window. Review how to grant roof access for a scheduled service visit to ensure your access credentials remain active.
  • Equipment staging: Pre-staged equipment at a local warehouse is held for up to 21 days before it must be reassigned to another job.

What to Expect Next

You will receive an automated push notification and email from the Brightline Home app with your new proposed appointment time. You can accept, request a different date, or view delay status details directly in the app. For step-by-step status tracking, see how to check the status of a weather-delayed appointment in Brightline Home.

articles.title: Will I be charged a fee if my appointment is cancelled due to weather?
articles.summary: Clarifies Brightline's no-fee policy for weather-initiated cancellations and explains how it differs from customer-initiated rescheduling fees.
articles.question: Brightline cancelled my installation appointment because of bad weather. Am I going to be charged a cancellation or rescheduling fee?
articles.answer:
No Fee for Weather-Initiated Cancellations

If Brightline Solar cancels or postpones your appointment due to weather conditions, you will not be charged any cancellation or rescheduling fee. Weather holds are logged in our system with reason code WX-HOLD, which automatically suppresses any fee triggers associated with that appointment slot.

How This Differs From Customer-Initiated Changes

Brightline's standard policy charges a $75 late-reschedule fee when a customer cancels or moves an appointment with fewer than 48 hours' notice. Weather cancellations initiated by Brightline are entirely separate and are never counted against your reschedule history. Your account will show the cancellation as Brightline-initiated in the Appointments section of the Brightline Home app under Menu > My Appointments > History.

What If I Want to Reschedule to a Different Date After a Weather Hold?

Once Brightline sends your proposed new appointment, you have 72 hours to accept or request an alternate date at no charge. If you request a second date change beyond that window, standard rescheduling terms apply. To understand all reschedule and cancellation options, see how to reschedule or cancel your site survey.

Preparing for Your Rescheduled Visit

Use the time before your new appointment to make sure your home is ready. See how to prepare your home for inspection day for a full checklist so nothing delays the crew once conditions clear.

articles.title: Sandbox Synthetic Dataset Refreshed with Expanded Site Profiles — May 2026
articles.summary: Brightline has updated the Partner API sandbox with a richer set of synthetic site data, including battery-equipped homes, ground-mount configurations, and multi-inverter layouts.
articles.abstract: Effective May 12, 2026, the Brightline Partner API sandbox environment received a full synthetic dataset refresh, replacing the previous 50-site fixture library with 400 pre-seeded virtual customer accounts spanning a wider range of system types, billing states, and alert histories. Partners building or testing integrations against https://sandbox-api.brightline.solar/v2/ will immediately see the expanded dataset under their existing sandbox credentials, with no credential rotation required.
articles.body:
What Changed on May 12, 2026

The refreshed sandbox dataset introduces the following new synthetic profile categories:

  • Battery-only sites (no export meter) — 60 profiles
  • Ground-mount systems with shading curves — 45 profiles
  • Multi-inverter residential arrays (2–4 inverters) — 80 profiles
  • Accounts with open invoice disputes — 30 profiles
  • Standard single-inverter rooftop sites — 185 profiles

Key Details

ItemPreviousUpdated
Total synthetic sites50400
Battery profiles includedNoYes
Data reset cadenceWeekly (Sundays 02:00 UTC)Weekly (Sundays 02:00 UTC)
Webhook delivery in sandboxSimulated onlySimulated + replayable

Sandbox webhooks can now be replayed on demand via POST /v2/sandbox/webhooks/{event_id}/replay. For guidance on scheduling automated data pulls against these profiles, see how to schedule automated report delivery via the Partner API.

No action is required for existing sandbox integrations. Partners who cached synthetic site IDs should re-query GET /v2/sandbox/sites as legacy fixture IDs were retired during the refresh.

articles.title: Sandbox Rate Limits Now Match Production Quotas Starting July 1, 2026
articles.summary: Brightline is aligning Partner API sandbox rate limits with production quotas so that integrations tested in sandbox reflect real-world throttling behavior before go-live.
articles.abstract: Beginning July 1, 2026, the Partner API sandbox environment will enforce the same per-minute and per-day request quotas as the production environment, replacing the previous unrestricted sandbox policy. This change ensures that partners discover rate-limit edge cases—and design appropriate retry logic—during development rather than after launching to production customers.
articles.body:
Effective Date: July 1, 2026

The following rate limits will apply to all sandbox credentials from July 1 onward:

Quota TypePrevious Sandbox LimitNew Sandbox Limit (matches production)
Requests per minute (per client)Unlimited120 rpm
Requests per day (per client)Unlimited50,000 req/day
Webhook delivery attempts (sandbox replay)Unlimited500 replays/day
OAuth2 token requests per hourUnlimited60 req/hour

What Partners Should Do Before July 1

  • Review integration code for loops or bulk-fetch patterns that rely on the sandbox being unrestricted.
  • Implement Retry-After header handling; the sandbox will return HTTP 429 with error code RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED identically to production.
  • Test pagination logic against large synthetic datasets — see how to paginate through large result sets in the Partner API.

Sandbox-Specific Exceptions

The sandbox will continue to accept OAuth2 token requests using the static test credential pair (sandbox_client_id / sandbox_client_secret) without requiring a registered redirect URI. All other behaviors, including error codes and response shapes, will be identical to production.

articles.title: View Your Installer Contact Information in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Find your assigned installation team's phone number, email address, and office hours directly inside the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be logged in to Brightline Home with the account used during your installation agreement. Installer contact details are populated automatically once your project is assigned an installation crew, typically within 3 business days of contract signing. If your project is still in the pre-assignment stage, the fields described below will display Pending Assignment.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap the Menu icon (☰) in the top-left corner.
  2. Select Profile from the main navigation list.
  3. Scroll down to the My Installation Team section.
  4. You will see the following details: Team Name, Primary Phone (tap to dial directly), Support Email (tap to open your default mail app), and Office Hours (displayed in your local time zone).
  5. To save the phone number to your device contacts, tap the phone number and select Add to Contacts from the prompt.
  6. If you prefer to receive an email summary of this information, tap Send to My Email at the bottom of the section. The summary arrives within 5 minutes to your account's registered email address.

Troubleshooting

The My Installation Team section is missing entirely. This can occur if your account was created through a third-party referral portal and the project link has not yet synced. Log out, wait 10 minutes, and log back in. If the section still does not appear, contact Brightline Customer Care at 1-800-555-0192.

The phone number or email shown looks incorrect. Installer assignments can change when crews are reallocated across regions. Pull down on the Profile screen to force a refresh. If the data still appears wrong after 24 hours, tap Report Incorrect Info beneath the team card and submit the short form — our scheduling team will verify and correct the record within 1 business day.

If your installation appointment has already been affected, see how to check the status of a weather-delayed appointment in Brightline Home for additional status options.

articles.title: Update Your Preferred Contact Method for Installer Communications
articles.summary: Change the phone number or email address that your Brightline installation team uses to reach you for scheduling, on-site questions, and follow-ups.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Only the primary Account Owner can update installer contact preferences. If you are an Authorized User on the account, you will see this section in read-only mode. Have your new phone number or email address ready. Changes take effect within 2 hours and will be visible to your installation crew on their scheduling dashboard by the next business day.

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap the Menu icon (☰), then select Profile.
  2. Tap Communication Preferences near the top of the Profile screen.
  3. Under the Installer Contact heading, tap Edit.
  4. To change your phone number, tap the Phone Number field, clear the existing entry, and type your new 10-digit US number. Brightline Home will send a 6-digit SMS verification code to that number; enter the code in the Verify Number field that appears and tap Confirm.
  5. To change your email address, tap the Email Address field and enter the new address. A verification link will be sent to the new address; click that link within 24 hours to confirm. Until confirmed, your original email remains active for installer communications.
  6. Select your Preferred Contact Method using the toggle: Phone, Email, or Either. Your installation crew will honor this preference for non-urgent outreach.
  7. Tap Save Changes. A green confirmation banner reading Installer contact preferences updated will appear at the top of the screen.

Troubleshooting

You did not receive the SMS verification code. Wait 2 minutes, then tap Resend Code. Codes expire after 10 minutes. If you still do not receive a code, confirm the number you entered is a US mobile number capable of receiving SMS — VoIP numbers are not supported for verification.

The Save Changes button is grayed out. This usually means a verification step is still pending. Check that both the phone and email fields show a green check mark before saving. If one field shows a yellow warning icon, tap it to see the specific error code (common codes: CONTACT-401 — duplicate number already on file; CONTACT-403 — restricted number format).

Changes are not reflected after 2 hours. Force-refresh the Profile screen by pulling down. If the old contact details persist, log out completely and log back in. Persistent issues should be reported to Brightline Customer Care.

For context on how Brightline uses your contact information during the installation process, see how to prepare your home for inspection day.

articles.title: Post-Install Walkthrough Now Bookable Directly in Brightline Home — Effective April 14, 2026
articles.summary: Brightline Solar customers can now schedule their mandatory post-installation walkthrough appointment entirely within the Brightline Home app, replacing the previous phone-based booking process.
articles.abstract: Starting April 14, 2026, all Brightline Solar residential customers whose systems have passed final inspection can book their post-install walkthrough directly through the Brightline Home app under My System > Appointments > Schedule Walkthrough. The self-service tool shows real-time availability for your assigned field technician and sends an automated confirmation with a calendar invite within five minutes of booking. Walkthroughs must be completed within 21 calendar days of your Permission to Operate (PTO) date; failure to schedule within that window will generate an in-app alert and may delay monitoring activation.
articles.body:
Effective date: April 14, 2026

The post-install walkthrough is a required step before your Brightline Home monitoring dashboard activates live production data. During the appointment, your technician will:

  • Confirm inverter communication and verify real-time production readings in the app
  • Walk you through battery charge/discharge settings (if applicable)
  • Review alert thresholds and show you how to dismiss or adjust notifications
  • Confirm billing cycle start date and answer billing questions

Scheduling Window

MilestoneDeadline
PTO issuedDay 0
Must schedule walkthroughWithin 7 days of PTO
Walkthrough must be completedWithin 21 days of PTO

To book, open Brightline Home, tap My System > Appointments > Schedule Walkthrough, and select an available two-hour window. Rescheduling is free up to 24 hours before the appointment; cancellations inside 24 hours may incur a $35 late-cancel fee. For questions about what your installer will cover during the visit, see How to view your installer contact information in Brightline Home.

articles.title: Virtual Post-Install Walkthrough Option Now Available for Eligible Customers — June 2, 2026
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is introducing an optional virtual walkthrough format for qualifying residential customers, allowing the mandatory post-install review to be completed via live video call instead of an in-person visit.
articles.abstract: Beginning June 2, 2026, eligible Brightline Solar customers can choose between an in-person or virtual post-install walkthrough when scheduling through the Brightline Home app. The virtual format uses a 45-minute live video session with a certified Brightline technician who guides customers through the same checklist as an in-person visit, including production monitoring setup, alert configuration, and battery controls. Eligibility is determined automatically based on system type, inverter model, and local jurisdiction requirements; customers who do not qualify will only see the in-person option when booking.
articles.body:
Launch date: June 2, 2026

Virtual walkthroughs are available Monday through Saturday, 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM in your local time zone, with same-week slots often available. Availability may be limited in some regions during the initial rollout.

In-Person vs. Virtual: Key Differences

FeatureIn-PersonVirtual
Duration60–90 minutes45 minutes
Physical equipment inspectionYesNo (photo upload required)
Battery hands-on demoYesApp-guided only
Late-cancel fee window24 hours12 hours
Rescheduling feeFree up to 24 hrsFree up to 12 hrs

To select your format, open Brightline Home, navigate to My System > Appointments > Schedule Walkthrough, and choose Virtual or In-Person on the appointment type screen. If you opt for virtual, you will receive a secure video link via email and push notification 30 minutes before your session. After the walkthrough, your technician will send a summary checklist to your registered email within two business days. For help updating how you receive appointment notifications, see How to update your preferred contact method for installer communications.

articles.title: New Site Ownership Transfer Endpoint Now Available in the Partner API
articles.summary: Partners can now programmatically initiate and track residential site ownership transfers directly through the Partner API, eliminating manual support tickets.
articles.abstract: As of June 10, 2026, Brightline Solar's Partner API includes a dedicated site ownership transfer workflow under the /v2/sites/{site_id}/ownership-transfer endpoint, allowing integrators to submit, monitor, and complete customer ownership changes without opening a support case. The new endpoint supports idempotent requests, real-time status webhooks, and a structured document-upload flow, making bulk portfolio transfers significantly faster for high-volume partners.
articles.body:
What Changed

Effective June 10, 2026, the Partner API exposes three new operations for site ownership transfer:

  • POST /v2/sites/{site_id}/ownership-transfer — initiates a transfer request
  • GET /v2/sites/{site_id}/ownership-transfer/{transfer_id} — polls current status
  • DELETE /v2/sites/{site_id}/ownership-transfer/{transfer_id} — cancels a pending transfer

Status Lifecycle

StatusMeaning
PENDING_DOCSAwaiting required homeowner documents
UNDER_REVIEWBrightline compliance team reviewing submission
APPROVEDTransfer complete; new owner credentials issued
REJECTEDTransfer denied; rejection_reason field populated

Key Details

  • Transfer requests must include an Idempotency-Key header. See What is an idempotency key and why do I need one? for guidance.
  • Brightline targets a 3-business-day review window for complete submissions.
  • A site.ownership_transfer.status_changed webhook event fires on every status transition.
  • A $25 processing fee per transfer is billed to the partner account monthly.

Full schema documentation is available in the Partner API reference portal under Sites > Ownership Transfer.

articles.title: Site Ownership Transfer Webhook Events and Error Code Reference Released
articles.summary: Brightline has published the complete webhook event schema and error code reference for the site ownership transfer workflow introduced in June 2026.
articles.abstract: Following the June 2026 launch of the ownership transfer endpoint, Brightline Solar is releasing supplementary documentation on July 1, 2026 that details every webhook event payload, all structured error codes, and recommended retry behavior for partners automating residential site ownership changes at scale. This reference is essential for partners building end-to-end transfer automation or integrating transfer status into customer-facing dashboards.
articles.body:
New Webhook Events

Published July 1, 2026, the following events are now emitted under the ownership_transfer event group:

  • site.ownership_transfer.created — fired immediately on successful POST
  • site.ownership_transfer.docs_received — fired when all required documents are uploaded
  • site.ownership_transfer.status_changed — fired on any status transition
  • site.ownership_transfer.completed — fired when new owner access is activated
  • site.ownership_transfer.cancelled — fired on DELETE or system cancellation

Structured Error Codes

Error CodeHTTP StatusMeaning
OT_SITE_NOT_FOUND404Site ID does not exist in your partner scope
OT_TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS409An active transfer already exists for this site
OT_INVALID_DOC_TYPE422Uploaded document format not accepted
OT_EXPIRED410Transfer request exceeded the 30-day submission window

Retry Guidance

Webhook delivery for ownership transfer events follows the standard retry policy. Review the March 2026 webhook retry policy update for backoff intervals and failure thresholds. Partners should treat OT_TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS (409) responses as non-retryable until the existing transfer resolves.

articles.title: Who can be a co-borrower on my Brightline solar loan?
articles.summary: Explains who qualifies as a co-borrower on a Brightline Solar financing agreement and what documentation they must provide.
articles.question: I want to add someone to my solar loan. Who is eligible to be a co-borrower, and what do they need to provide?
articles.answer:
Co-Borrower Eligibility

A co-borrower shares equal legal responsibility for your Brightline Solar loan. Unlike a cosigner, a co-borrower's name appears on both the financing agreement and the lien placed on your property, so eligibility requirements are strict.

Who Qualifies

  • Spouse or domestic partner — most common; must reside at or have a legal ownership interest in the installation address.
  • Co-owner of the property — any individual listed on the property deed qualifies automatically, provided they meet credit criteria.
  • Non-occupant co-owner — permitted in limited cases for properties held in joint tenancy or tenancy-in-common; subject to underwriter review.

Who Does Not Qualify

  • Relatives who have no ownership stake in the property
  • Business entities (LLCs, trusts, corporations) — these require a separate commercial financing pathway
  • Minors under 18

Required Documentation

DocumentAccepted Format
Government-issued photo IDDriver's license, passport, or state ID
Proof of property interestRecorded deed or title document
Social Security NumberProvided via secure Brightline e-consent form
Income verificationTwo most recent pay stubs or prior-year tax return

All documentation must be submitted through the Brightline Home app under Account → Financing → Manage Co-Borrower or via your assigned Brightline Financing Specialist. Processing takes 5–10 business days after a complete package is received.

For questions about how loan changes affect your statement, see What information is included on my Brightline loan statement?

articles.title: How do I add or remove a co-borrower from my Brightline solar loan?
articles.summary: Walks through the process, fees, and timelines for adding or removing a co-borrower on an active Brightline Solar financing agreement.
articles.question: My situation has changed and I need to either add or remove a co-borrower from my existing solar loan. How do I do that, and are there any fees?
articles.answer:
Making a Co-Borrower Change

Co-borrower modifications on an active Brightline Solar loan are treated as a loan assumption or restructure and require underwriting review. You cannot complete this change entirely on your own — a Brightline Financing Specialist must open a case on your behalf.

Step-by-Step: Adding a Co-Borrower

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to Account → Financing → Manage Co-Borrower → Add Co-Borrower.
  2. Enter the prospective co-borrower's name and email. They will receive a secure invitation to submit their information directly.
  3. Upload required documents (see related article below for eligibility details).
  4. A Brightline Financing Specialist will contact both parties within 3 business days to confirm next steps.
  5. Once underwriting approves, both parties sign an amended loan agreement via DocuSign. The amendment is recorded within 10–15 business days.

Step-by-Step: Removing a Co-Borrower

  1. Navigate to Account → Financing → Manage Co-Borrower → Request Removal.
  2. The remaining borrower must qualify for the full loan balance independently — a new credit check (hard pull) will be initiated.
  3. If approved, a loan modification document is issued for e-signature. The removed co-borrower receives written confirmation within 5 business days of recording.

Fees

  • Co-borrower addition: $75 loan modification fee
  • Co-borrower removal: $125 loan restructure fee
  • Fees are added to your next monthly invoice and are non-refundable once underwriting begins.

Note: Co-borrower changes do not affect your interest rate or remaining loan term unless a full refinance is requested.

To understand how a modification may appear on your next statement, visit Why does my loan statement balance not match what I expected?

articles.title: What rights and responsibilities does a co-borrower have on my Brightline solar loan?
articles.summary: Co-borrowers share equal legal and financial responsibility for the loan and have most of the same account access rights as the primary borrower.
articles.question: My spouse was added as a co-borrower on our Brightline solar loan. What can they actually do on the account, and what are they on the hook for if we can't make payments?
articles.answer:
Co-Borrower Rights

A co-borrower on a Brightline solar loan is a full legal party to the loan agreement — not just a cosigner. This means they have independent rights to:

  • Log in to Brightline Home with their own credentials and view the full loan dashboard, including statements and payment history
  • Make payments, set up AutoPay, and download receipts
  • Request a payoff letter through Account > Financing > Request Payoff Letter
  • Contact Brightline support to discuss account details without needing authorization from the primary borrower

Co-Borrower Responsibilities

Co-borrowers share joint and several liability for the entire loan balance. This means:

  • Both parties are equally responsible for on-time payments
  • A missed payment affects both borrowers' credit profiles
  • Either borrower can be pursued for the full outstanding balance if the other defaults

What a Co-Borrower Cannot Do Unilaterally

Some actions require written consent from both parties, including removing a co-borrower from the loan, modifying loan terms, or initiating a loan transfer in connection with a home sale.

Related Articles

For information on viewing your loan statement, see What information is included on my Brightline loan statement?. To understand how partial payments are applied when multiple parties pay, see How does Brightline apply partial payments to my account balance?

articles.title: What happens to my Brightline solar loan if my co-borrower and I separate or divorce?
articles.summary: Separation or divorce does not automatically change your loan agreement, and both parties remain liable until Brightline formally approves a co-borrower removal or loan refinance.
articles.question: My co-borrower and I are getting divorced. How does that affect our Brightline solar loan, and how do I get their name off the account?
articles.answer:
Your Loan Agreement Does Not Change Automatically

A divorce decree or separation agreement is a legal document between you and your co-borrower, but it is not binding on Brightline. Until the loan is formally modified, both parties remain equally liable for all payments, regardless of what your divorce settlement specifies.

Options for Resolving the Loan

  • Co-borrower removal: Either party may submit a co-borrower removal request via Brightline Home > Account > Financing > Manage Co-Borrower. The remaining borrower must qualify for the full loan amount through a new credit review. Processing takes approximately 15–20 business days. A $75 loan modification fee applies unless waived by a Brightline financing specialist.
  • Full payoff: One party may pay off the loan in full. Request a payoff letter at least 5 business days before the intended payoff date.
  • Home sale and loan transfer: If the property is being sold, the loan may be paid off from sale proceeds or, in eligible cases, transferred to a qualified buyer.

What to Expect During Review

During the co-borrower removal review period, the account remains active and payments are still due on their normal schedule. Late payments during this period will affect both parties' credit.

Get Help

Contact Brightline Financing Support at 1-800-555-0192 (Mon–Fri, 8 AM–6 PM local time) to discuss your specific situation. See also How do I add or remove a co-borrower from my Brightline solar loan? and Payoff letter request now available in Brightline Home.

articles.title: Updated Account Lockout Policy Now in Effect for Brightline Home
articles.summary: Effective March 10, 2026, Brightline Home enforces a stricter account lockout policy to better protect customer accounts from unauthorized access.
articles.abstract: As of March 10, 2026, Brightline Home has updated its account lockout rules, reducing the number of failed login attempts permitted before a lockout occurs and introducing a tiered cooldown system. All existing and new customers are subject to these changes automatically, with no action required unless an account is currently locked. Customers who are locked out can self-unlock using the in-app recovery flow or by contacting Brightline Support.
articles.body:
What Changed

Effective March 10, 2026, the following lockout thresholds apply to all Brightline Home accounts:

Failed AttemptsLockout DurationRecovery Method
3 consecutive15 minutes (automatic)Wait and retry
6 consecutive2 hours (automatic)Wait and retry or email verification
10 consecutiveIndefiniteSupport contact required

How to Recover a Locked Account

  • Open Brightline Home and tap Trouble signing in? on the login screen.
  • Select Unlock My Account and complete the email verification step.
  • For indefinite lockouts, call Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0194 (Mon–Fri, 7 AM–8 PM local time).

Partner API integrations authenticating on behalf of customers should review how to resolve OAuth2 token errors in the Partner API to handle lockout-related token rejections gracefully. No fees are associated with account recovery.

articles.title: Temporary Account Lockouts Expected During MFA Enforcement Rollout – June 2026
articles.summary: Between June 3 and June 14, 2026, some Brightline Home customers may experience temporary account lockouts as mandatory multi-factor authentication is enforced across all accounts.
articles.abstract: Brightline is rolling out mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all Brightline Home accounts in waves between June 3 and June 14, 2026. During enrollment, customers who do not complete MFA setup within the prompted window will have their accounts temporarily locked as a security precaution. Affected customers will receive an email with step-by-step unlock instructions before their wave begins.
articles.body:
Rollout Schedule

  • June 3–6, 2026: Accounts created before January 1, 2023
  • June 7–10, 2026: Accounts created January 1, 2023 – December 31, 2024
  • June 11–14, 2026: All remaining accounts

What to Expect

When your wave begins, you will see an MFA setup prompt immediately after entering your password. You have 48 hours to complete setup. If setup is not completed within that window, your account will be locked with error code AUTH_MFA_REQUIRED_7 until MFA enrollment is finished.

How to Unlock

  1. Go to brightlinehome.app/unlock or open the Brightline Home app.
  2. Enter your email address and select Set Up MFA to Unlock.
  3. Choose SMS or authenticator app as your second factor and complete verification.

Partner API integrations are not subject to MFA enforcement but should ensure OAuth2 flows remain valid. See how to resolve OAuth2 token errors in the Partner API for guidance. Contact support at 1-800-555-0194 with questions.

articles.title: Brightline Home Browser Support List Updated for 2026
articles.summary: Effective March 1, 2026, Brightline Home drops support for several legacy browsers and adds full support for the latest versions of Edge and Firefox.
articles.abstract: Starting March 1, 2026, Brightline Home will no longer support Internet Explorer 11, Chrome versions below 108, or Safari versions below 15. Users on these browsers may experience login failures, blank dashboards, or broken multi-factor authentication prompts. All customers should upgrade to a supported browser before the deadline to avoid disruption to production monitoring, billing, and battery control features.
articles.body:
What's Changing

Brightline Home is updating its supported browser matrix on March 1, 2026. The following browsers are affected:

BrowserMinimum Supported VersionStatus
Google Chrome108Supported
Mozilla Firefox110Newly fully supported
Microsoft Edge108Newly fully supported
Apple Safari15Supported
Internet Explorer 11AnyDropped February 28, 2026

Why We're Making This Change

Legacy browsers lack support for the WebAuthn and TLS 1.3 standards that power Brightline Home's secure login flow. Removing them lets us enforce stronger encryption and faster page loads for all users.

What You Should Do

  • Check your current browser version in its About menu.
  • Update to the latest stable release before March 1, 2026.
  • If you experience login errors after updating, see Account Lockout Policy Update (Login 2026) for related troubleshooting steps.

Contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 if you need assistance.

articles.title: Brightline Home Expands Mobile Browser Login Support Starting April 2026
articles.summary: Beginning April 15, 2026, Brightline Home officially supports login through Chrome for Android and Safari for iOS, with improved compatibility for in-app browsers.
articles.abstract: Brightline Home has historically recommended desktop browsers for the best login experience, but starting April 15, 2026, mobile browsers are now fully supported, including Chrome 120+ for Android and Safari 16+ for iOS. This update also improves compatibility with in-app browsers embedded in email clients, resolving a class of errors where the Brightline Home login page would freeze or fail to redirect after multi-factor authentication on mobile devices.
articles.body:
Announcement Details

Effective Date: April 15, 2026

This release resolves error code BH-LOGIN-4031 ("OAuth redirect blocked by in-app browser") that affected users who clicked login links directly from their email apps on iOS and Android.

Newly Supported Mobile Browsers

  • Chrome 120 or later on Android 10+
  • Safari 16 or later on iOS 15+
  • Samsung Internet 22 or later
  • Firefox for Android 121 or later

Known Limitations

  • Biometric login (Face ID / fingerprint) is supported only in native Safari and Chrome, not in third-party in-app browsers.
  • Battery Control scheduling requires a viewport width of at least 360px; some older budget Android devices may see a degraded layout.

What to Do If Login Still Fails

If you receive error code BH-LOGIN-4031 after April 15, open the Brightline Home link in your device's default browser rather than your email app. For MFA-related login issues, review Temporary Account Lockout & MFA Enforcement (Login 2026). Contact support at 1-800-555-0192 for further help.

articles.title: Rapid Shutdown Firmware Update Now Rolling Out to All Brightline Systems
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is deploying a mandatory rapid shutdown firmware update beginning July 14, 2026, that improves compliance with NEC 2020 Section 690.12 and introduces new alert codes in the Brightline Home app.
articles.abstract: Starting July 14, 2026, Brightline Solar will automatically push firmware version RS-4.2.1 to all eligible rapid shutdown devices, bringing systems into full alignment with NEC 2020 Section 690.12 requirements and adding clearer alert messaging inside the Brightline Home app so homeowners can immediately understand and act on any rapid shutdown event.
articles.body:
What Is Changing

Firmware version RS-4.2.1 updates the rapid shutdown transmitter logic on all Brightline-installed systems manufactured after January 2022. The update rolls out in three waves:

  • Wave 1 (July 14–21, 2026): Systems in California, Arizona, and Nevada
  • Wave 2 (July 22–29, 2026): Systems in Texas, Florida, and Georgia
  • Wave 3 (July 30–August 6, 2026): All remaining states

New Alert Codes

After the update, rapid shutdown events will surface one of the following alert codes in Brightline Home → Alerts → System Safety:

CodeMeaningRecommended Action
RSD-01Voluntary shutdown triggered via appNo action required
RSD-02Grid-loss rapid shutdownWait for grid restoration
RSD-03Communication fault between transmitter and modulesContact support

What You Need to Do

No manual steps are required. Ensure your inverter remains powered and connected to Wi-Fi during your wave window. Updates typically complete within 12 minutes between midnight and 4 a.m. local time. If you receive an unexpected RSD-03 alert after the update, review our guidance on how to identify and dismiss a false alarm in Brightline Home before calling support.

articles.title: Enhanced Rapid Shutdown Alert Notifications Coming to Brightline Home on August 18, 2026
articles.summary: On August 18, 2026, Brightline Home will introduce redesigned rapid shutdown alert notifications that include plain-language explanations, severity indicators, and one-tap access to guided resolution steps.
articles.abstract: On August 18, 2026, Brightline Solar will release version 6.5 of the Brightline Home app, which overhauls how rapid shutdown alerts are presented to homeowners — replacing terse technical codes with plain-language descriptions, color-coded severity banners, and in-app guided resolution workflows designed to help customers respond quickly and safely.
articles.body:
Why We Are Making This Change

Customer feedback collected between January and June 2026 showed that 61% of rapid shutdown alert recipients did not understand what action to take. The version 6.5 update directly addresses this by restructuring the alert experience from the ground up.

Key Improvements at a Glance

  • Plain-language titles: "Your solar array has safely shut down" instead of raw codes like RSD-02
  • Color-coded severity banners: Yellow (informational), Orange (action recommended), Red (contact support immediately)
  • Guided resolution steps: Tappable checklists inside each alert detail screen
  • Estimated restoration time: Displayed automatically for RSD-02 (grid-loss) events when utility outage data is available
  • False-alarm flag: One-tap reporting so our team can refine suppression logic

Timeline

DateMilestone
August 18, 2026App version 6.5 available in iOS and Android stores
August 25, 2026Auto-update pushed to all users on auto-update enabled devices
September 1, 2026Legacy alert format retired

To take full advantage of the false-alarm flagging feature, review how to configure false alarm suppression rules in Brightline Home before the September 1 legacy format retirement date.

articles.title: Battery Alert Thresholds Updated for More Accurate Low-Charge Warnings
articles.summary: Brightline has revised the default battery alert thresholds in Brightline Home to reduce unnecessary notifications and improve warning accuracy for low state-of-charge events.
articles.abstract: Effective July 14, 2026, Brightline Solar updated the default alert thresholds for battery state-of-charge (SOC) warnings in the Brightline Home app. The previous default low-charge alert triggered at 20% SOC, which generated frequent alerts during normal evening discharge cycles. The new default threshold is 12% SOC, with a critical alert firing at 5% SOC. Customers can still customize these values under Settings > Alerts > Battery in the app. No action is required unless you prefer to keep your old thresholds.
articles.body:
What Changed

On July 14, 2026, Brightline automatically updated default battery alert thresholds for all residential accounts with a Brightline-managed battery system. The changes apply to both push notifications and email alerts.

Alert TypeOld ThresholdNew Threshold
Low Charge Warning20% SOC12% SOC
Critical Low Charge10% SOC5% SOC
Charge Complete95% SOC98% SOC

How to Review or Restore Your Previous Settings

  • Open Brightline Home and navigate to Settings > Alerts > Battery.
  • Tap Edit Thresholds to set custom SOC values between 1% and 99%.
  • Tap Save to apply. Changes take effect within 5 minutes.

If you believe an alert fired incorrectly after this update, see our guide on how to identify and dismiss a false alarm in Brightline Home for troubleshooting steps.

Questions? Contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192.

articles.title: Improved Offline Detection Now Reduces Spurious Battery Disconnection Alerts
articles.summary: A platform update released August 5, 2026 improves how Brightline Home detects true battery offline events, cutting false disconnection alerts by an estimated 74% for customers with intermittent internet gateways.
articles.abstract: Brightline Solar has deployed an update to its alert engine that introduces a 4-minute confirmation window before a battery disconnection alert is sent. Previously, any communication gap longer than 90 seconds triggered a BATT_OFFLINE_001 alert, causing a high volume of false alarms for customers whose home network or cellular gateway experienced brief interruptions. As of August 5, 2026, the system waits 4 minutes of sustained silence before issuing the alert, and automatically clears it without a separate notification once connectivity is restored.
articles.body:
Background

Prior to this release, the Brightline monitoring platform issued a BATT_OFFLINE_001 alert after just 90 seconds of missed telemetry from a battery unit. Network micro-outages—common during router reboots or brief cellular signal drops—routinely triggered this alert even when the battery itself was fully operational.

What Is Changing

  • Effective date: August 5, 2026
  • New confirmation window: 4 minutes of sustained offline status before BATT_OFFLINE_001 is issued.
  • Auto-clear: If telemetry resumes before the alert is sent, no notification is generated and no manual dismissal is needed.
  • Persistent offline: If the battery remains offline beyond 4 minutes, the alert fires as normal and a follow-up BATT_OFFLINE_002 escalation triggers after 2 hours of continued silence.

No Action Required

This improvement is applied automatically to all accounts. You do not need to update the app or change any settings. To learn how to configure suppression rules for other alert types, visit how to configure false alarm suppression rules in Brightline Home.

Contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 with any questions.

articles.title: What happens during a Brightline site survey?
articles.summary: A site survey is a pre-installation visit where a Brightline technician evaluates your home's roof, electrical panel, and property to design your solar system.
articles.question: I have a site survey scheduled — what will the technician actually do, and how long will it take?
articles.answer:
What Is a Site Survey?

A site survey is a mandatory pre-installation assessment conducted by a certified Brightline field technician before your solar system design is finalized. It typically takes 60–90 minutes, though larger homes or complex roof layouts may require up to 2 hours.

What the Technician Will Inspect

  • Roof structure: Material type (shingle, tile, metal), pitch, condition, and available surface area for panel placement.
  • Electrical panel: Current amperage rating, available breaker slots, and compatibility with your planned system size.
  • Attic access: Rafter spacing and structural integrity for mounting hardware.
  • Shading analysis: Using a calibrated solar pathfinder tool, the technician maps obstructions such as trees or neighboring structures across all daylight hours.
  • Utility meter and interconnection point: Location and accessibility for the inverter and production meter installation.

What You Should Prepare

  1. Ensure an adult (18+) is present for the full duration of the visit.
  2. Clear a 3-foot perimeter around your main electrical panel.
  3. Provide attic access if a pull-down staircase or hatch is the only entry point.
  4. Have a recent utility bill available — the technician may ask about your average monthly usage.

After the Survey

Results are uploaded to your Brightline account within 2 business days. You will receive an in-app notification in Brightline Home under My Project > Survey Results once your customized system design is ready for review.

If the technician identifies a concern (such as a roof needing repair before installation), you will receive a separate Pre-Installation Requirements notice via email and in-app alert.

articles.title: How do I reschedule or cancel my site survey appointment?
articles.summary: You can reschedule or cancel a site survey up to 24 hours before the appointment through the Brightline Home app or by contacting your installer directly.
articles.question: Something came up and I need to change my site survey date. How do I reschedule or cancel, and are there any fees?
articles.answer:
Rescheduling Your Site Survey in Brightline Home

To reschedule, open Brightline Home and navigate to My Project > Appointments > Upcoming. Tap your site survey card and select Reschedule. You will see a live calendar showing the next available slots in your area — select a new date and time, then tap Confirm Reschedule. A confirmation email and push notification are sent immediately.

Cancellation Policy

  • More than 24 hours before the appointment: Cancellation is free. You may cancel directly in the app via My Project > Appointments > Cancel Visit.
  • Within 24 hours of the appointment: A $75 late-cancellation fee is applied to your account. This fee appears on your next invoice as a line item labeled Late Survey Cancellation Fee.
  • No-show (technician arrives, no one home): A $125 no-show fee is charged, and your project timeline may be extended by up to 10 business days depending on technician availability in your region.

Rescheduling by Phone

You may also contact your assigned installer directly. To find their contact details, go to My Project > Installer Info in Brightline Home. For guidance on locating this screen, see How to view your installer contact information in Brightline Home.

How Many Times Can I Reschedule?

Brightline allows up to 2 reschedules per site survey at no charge (subject to the 24-hour policy above). A third reschedule request requires written approval from your project coordinator and may delay your estimated installation date. If you need to reschedule due to a weather event, no cancellation fee is assessed — see Will I be charged a fee if my appointment is cancelled due to weather? for details.

articles.title: How do I prepare my home for a Brightline site survey?
articles.summary: Steps customers should take before their site survey appointment to ensure the visit goes smoothly and on schedule.
articles.question: My site survey is coming up soon. What do I need to do to get my home ready so the appointment goes smoothly?
articles.answer:
Preparing for Your Site Survey

A little preparation before your Brightline site survey helps our field technician complete the visit efficiently—usually within 60–90 minutes—and avoids the need for a follow-up trip that could delay your installation timeline.

What to Have Ready

  • Clear access to your main electrical panel. Remove any items stored in front of it. The technician needs at least 36 inches of clearance.
  • Attic or crawl space access. If your home has an attic hatch, make sure it is unobstructed. Our technician will inspect roof structure and insulation.
  • Recent utility bills. Have the last 12 months of electricity bills available, either printed or on your phone. This helps size your system accurately.
  • Roof access from outside. Unlock any side gates and ensure pets are secured so the technician can safely walk the perimeter.
  • A responsible adult on-site. Someone 18 or older must be present for the entire appointment. If your schedule changes, reschedule in advance to avoid a $75 missed-appointment fee.

Day-of Tips

  1. Confirm your appointment in the Brightline Home app under My Appointments > Upcoming at least 24 hours before.
  2. Watch for a technician arrival notification sent approximately 30 minutes before they reach your address.

For details on what the technician will actually inspect and measure during the visit, see What happens during a Brightline site survey?

articles.title: How far in advance can I schedule my Brightline site survey?
articles.summary: Explains the scheduling window for site surveys, how to book through Brightline Home, and what affects appointment availability.
articles.question: I just signed my contract. How soon can I book my site survey, and how far out can I schedule it?
articles.answer:
Site Survey Scheduling Window

Once your Brightline Solar contract is countersigned and your account is activated, you can book a site survey as early as the next business day and as far out as 90 calendar days from the contract date. Appointments are available Monday through Saturday, 8 AM – 5 PM in your local time zone.

How to Book

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap My Project in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Schedule Site Survey. If this option is grayed out, your contract countersignature is still processing—check back within one business day.
  3. Choose a date and two-hour arrival window, then confirm. You will receive an email and push notification with your confirmation number (format: SS-XXXXXXX).

Factors That Affect Availability

  • Regional demand: Slots in high-volume markets like California and Texas may fill 2–3 weeks out, especially April through August.
  • Technician coverage area: Rural addresses may have limited weekday availability; Saturday slots are often more open.
  • Weather holds: During active weather advisories, same-week slots may be automatically blocked. See Why was my installation appointment delayed due to weather? for more information.

Need to Change Your Appointment?

You can reschedule at no charge up to 48 hours before your appointment start time. For rescheduling and cancellation details, visit How do I reschedule or cancel my site survey appointment?

articles.title: What do I need to do to prepare roof access for my Brightline appointment?
articles.summary: Learn the specific steps required to ensure your technician can safely and promptly access your roof on the day of your scheduled Brightline appointment.
articles.question: My installation or service appointment is coming up and I want to make sure the technician can get onto my roof without any problems. What do I need to have ready or cleared ahead of time?
articles.answer:
Preparing Roof Access Before Your Appointment

Proper roof access preparation helps your technician start work on time and avoids same-day rescheduling fees. Please complete the following steps at least 24 hours before your scheduled appointment window.

Clear the Surrounding Area

  • Remove vehicles, trailers, or equipment parked within 10 feet of the roofline on all sides where work is planned.
  • Trim or tie back overhanging tree branches that could block ladder placement or panel positioning.
  • Ensure ground surfaces near the home are stable — soft or uneven soil must be compacted or have boards placed for ladder feet.

Gate and Yard Access

  • Unlock all gates leading to the side or rear of the property by 7:00 AM on appointment day.
  • Secure pets indoors or in a fenced area separate from the work zone.
  • If your HOA requires a visitor pass or escort, arrange this in advance and notify your Brightline coordinator by calling 1-800-BRTLINE (1-800-278-5463).

Roof Condition Notes

If you are aware of any existing roof damage, soft spots, or recent repairs, disclose these in the Brightline Home app under My Home > Property Details > Roof Notes before the visit. Undisclosed hazards may require the technician to pause work and could result in a return-trip charge.

For guidance on what else to expect on the day of your survey or installation visit, see How do I prepare my home for a Brightline site survey?

articles.title: What happens if my technician cannot access my roof on appointment day?
articles.summary: Understand the consequences, fees, and rebooking process when a Brightline technician arrives and is unable to access your roof as scheduled.
articles.question: I missed my appointment window or the technician showed up and couldn't get onto my roof. What happens next, and will I be charged anything?
articles.answer:
What Happens When Roof Access Is Blocked

If a Brightline technician arrives at your property and cannot safely or legally access the roof, the visit is logged as an Access Failure (AF) event. The technician will wait up to 20 minutes for the issue to be resolved before departing.

Fees That May Apply

ScenarioFee
First AF event on your account (lifetime)Waived
Second or subsequent AF event$95 return-trip fee
AF caused by locked gate with no contact response$95 return-trip fee
AF caused by confirmed weather or utility hazardWaived — see weather delay policy

How to Rebook

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to Schedule > My Appointments.
  2. Tap the affected appointment and select Rebook After Access Failure.
  3. Choose a new date — priority rebooking slots (within 5 business days) are offered at no extra cost for first-time AF events.

Disputing an AF Fee

If you believe a return-trip fee was applied in error — for example, because the technician arrived outside your confirmed window — you can dispute the charge directly in the app under Billing > Dispute a Charge. For tips on supporting documentation, see What documents should I submit when disputing a Brightline invoice charge? and How do I reschedule or cancel my site survey appointment?

articles.title: Can someone else provide roof access if I can't be home for my Brightline appointment?
articles.summary: A responsible adult (18+) can grant roof access on your behalf, provided you register them in the Brightline Home app before your appointment.
articles.question: I have a scheduled Brightline appointment but I won't be able to be home that day. Can I have a family member, neighbor, or property manager let the technician onto my roof instead?
articles.answer:
Yes — A Designated Contact Can Provide Roof Access

You do not need to be personally present as long as a designated on-site contact is available to grant the technician access to your roof and any electrical panels that need to be reached. This person must be at least 18 years old and physically present for the full appointment window.

How to Register a Designated Contact

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to My Appointments.
  2. Tap the relevant appointment, then select Manage Access Contact.
  3. Enter the contact's full name and a direct phone number where they can be reached on appointment day.
  4. Tap Save Contact. You will receive a confirmation notification.

Changes must be submitted at least 24 hours before the scheduled appointment start time. Same-day changes cannot be processed through the app; call Brightline Scheduling Support at 1-833-274-5566 for urgent updates.

What Your Contact Should Know

  • They should be ready 15 minutes before the appointment window opens.
  • Technicians carry Brightline-branded ID badges — your contact may ask to see one.
  • They do not need to sign any documents unless a physical permit card must be posted; the app will notify you if this applies.

If no authorized contact is present when the technician arrives, the visit will be marked as a missed access event and a rescheduling fee of $75 may apply. For more on what to have ready before the crew arrives, see What do I need to do to prepare roof access for my Brightline appointment?

articles.title: Why does Brightline need unobstructed roof access, and what counts as an obstruction?
articles.summary: Brightline technicians require a clear, safe path to every part of the roof in the work zone; common obstructions include locked gates, overhanging branches, and unsecured equipment.
articles.question: My appointment confirmation mentioned that I need to make sure the roof is "unobstructed," but I'm not sure what that means. What exactly counts as an obstruction, and why does it matter so much?
articles.answer:
Why Clear Roof Access Matters

Brightline technicians work at height with heavy panel assemblies and power tools. Any barrier that forces them to maneuver around or over unexpected objects increases the risk of injury, equipment damage, or a permit violation. If an obstruction cannot be cleared on the spot, the crew is required by Brightline's safety policy to stop work and reschedule — which can delay your system activation by 5–14 business days depending on crew availability.

Common Obstructions and How to Resolve Them

Obstruction TypeRequired Action
Locked side gate or fenceEnsure gate is unlocked or provide a key/code to your on-site contact
Overhanging tree branches within 3 ft of roof edgeTrim branches before appointment day
Satellite dishes or antennas in the work zoneContact provider to relocate, or note exception in the app
Stored items on a flat roof (furniture, planters, HVAC covers)Move items at least 5 ft from the marked work zone
Unsecured animals in the yardSecure pets indoors or in a contained area for the full appointment window

How to Check Your Work Zone

The marked work zone is shown in the Brightline Home app under My Appointments > Site Details > Roof Plan. If you believe something in your yard may be an issue but you're unsure, tap Flag a Concern on that screen to message your local crew at least 48 hours in advance.

For a full checklist of day-of preparation steps, see What happens if my technician cannot access my roof on appointment day?
